title: Genting Berhad (GENT MK) - At a crossroads
author: PhillipCapital
body:
GENT is refocusing its efforts on RWLV, following recent board changes and with much of the legal overhang now largely resolved
We cut our 2025-27E EPS estimates by 19-23% after reflecting updated GENM forecasts, lower RWLV contributions and higher interest expense
GENT trades near its all-time low valuations, at 5x EV/EBITDA and 0.4x 2025 P/BV. Maintain BUY with a lower SOP-based TP of RM3.55
Critical inflection point
We find GENT at an inflection point, where a successful turnaround of Resorts World Las Vegas (RWLV) could serve as a significant catalyst for rerating. RWLV currently accounts for 6% to group EBITDA, down from 10% in 2023. The recent board refresh and resolution of legal headwinds appear to have laid the groundwork for the next leg of growth. Management is sharpening its focus on driving profitability, with a renewed emphasis on cost discipline and targeted marketing. Although we have revised our RWLV EBITDA forecasts downwards for 2025-27E by 14-21% to US$181m/US$193m/US$210m, these still represent a meaningful improvement over the US$107m recorded in 2024.
A turnaround at RWLV could ease valuation pressure
GENT's share price has declined by 15% YTD and is now trading at 5x EV/EBITDA and 0.4x 2025E P/BV, near all-time lows (-1.8SD and -1.5SD from its 10-year mean, respectively). Nevertheless, GENT continues to generate steady annual cash flows of RM7-8bn, and a potential turnaround at RWLV could alleviate valuation pressure. GENT is trading at a 46% holding company discount, compared to an average discount of 40% over the past 5-year, further highlighting its appeal. Current valuation overlooks the upside potential from TauRx, which remains underappreciated due to its complex timeline and mixed clinical results.
Maintain BUY with a lower SOP-based TP of RM3.55
We lower our earnings for 2025-27E by 19-23%, reflecting updated GENM forecasts, lower RWLV contributions, and higher interest expense. Our 2025-26E forecasts are 14-22% below consensus due to conservative GENM estimates. Overall, we project GENT's core PATAMI growth of 21%/25%/31% for 2025-27E, albeit from a low base. We maintain our BUY rating with a lower SOP-derived TP of RM3.55 (from RM4.15). The key earnings growth driver remains its gaming and leisure operations, with potential upside from TauRx. Key risk includes include weaker-than-expected earnings contributions from its subsidiaries, lower-than-expected win rates, rising operational costs, and a decline in non-gaming revenue.
Resorts World Las Vegas (RWLV) underperformed. Recall that RWLV recorded minimal EBITDA of US$1.5m in 4Q24, with the adjusted EBITDA for the full year 2024 totaling US$107m. This represents 56% of our original forecast for the business. We believe that the investigation into violations related to illegal bookmakers' gambling at RWLV negatively impacted visitor numbers, particularly in 2H24. Recently, RWLV agreed to pay a US$10.5m fine to settle allegations of non-compliance with federal anti-money laundering laws, with the settlement terms having been reviewed and approved by the Nevada Gaming Commission. We view this settlement as somewhat positive, as we believe it will help mitigate any further negative impact on GENM's bid for a downstate casino license. As part of the remediation efforts, RWLV has undergone significant leadership changes in recent months, including the appointment of a new C-suites (Chief Executive Officer, Chief Operating Officer, and Chief Financial Officer). Furthermore, a new board of directors has been established, and the search for a new Chief Compliance Officer is currently underway.
Focus on ramping up RWLV operations. We maintain our positive outlook on RWLV's growth trajectory, despite limited direct visibility into its operations, supported by market share gain post-legal resolution, and gross gaming revenue (GGR) growth across Las Vegas Strip area (YTD: +2.8% YoY). Management remains focused on ramping up business, enhancing operational efficiencies, and executing marketing and growth strategies. However, we have revised our EBITDA margin forecasts downward, expecting rising payroll costs to pressure margins, and have adjusted our 2025-27E EBITDA forecasts lower by 14-21% to US$181m/US$193m/US$210m (from US$210m/US$230m/US$265m).
GENM likely to see continued margin pressure. Resorts World Genting (RWG) is poised to benefit from efforts aimed at boosting foreign visitations, such as increased flight frequencies, visa exemptions, and a rising influx of Chinese travellers. However, GENM's earnings will likely remain under pressure, weighed down by EBITDA margin compression, higher depreciation, and interest expenses, as well as associate losses. We believe that our earlier 11-14% cut in 2025-26E earnings forecasts, made during the 4Q24 result release, does not fully account for the extent of margin compression and prevailing headwinds. In our recent update report for GENM dated 20 Mar 2025, we further slash earnings forecasts for 2025-27E by 24-28% after pencilling in lower EBITDA margin assumptions, higher depreciation and interest costs.
GENS' Resorts World Sentosa (RWS) is expected to benefit from improved international visitors. The Singapore Tourism Board forecasts 17-18.5m international visitors in 2025 (2024: 16.5m), generating SG$29-30.5bn in tourism receipts (2024E: SG$27.5-29bn). The projected 3-12% increase is expected to be driven by major events such as Lady Gaga concerts in May25, along with new attractions like Minion Land at Universal Studios Singapore (opened in Feb25) and the Singapore Oceanarium (scheduled to open later this year), both at RWS. Despite this, we foresee a tale of two halves for RWS in 2025E, with 1H25 likely facing temporary EBITDA pressures due to elevated pre-operating costs.
Wildcard still on the table. TauRx is currently under regulatory review by the UK MHRA, which has requested further clarification. The following key milestone in Apr/May25 is expected to provide more clarity on the regulatory pathway. Based on our previous forecasts, TauRx's revenue potential could range between US$480m-US$3.6bn upon successful commercialization, which would value GENT's 20.3% equity stake in TauRx at RM1.06-RM2.64/share, assuming a 30% EBITDA margin and 10% WACC. However, the outcome is subject to uncertainties inherent in clinical trials and regulatory approvals. Nevertheless, we believe the upside potential from TauRx's successful commercialization is not fully reflected in the current GENT share price.
Recent transaction suggest TauRx could be worth US$3.9bn. In Oct24, Dundee Corporation, a publicly traded asset management company holding 3.2% stake in TauRx sold shares at US$125 per share, implying a total valuation of US$3.93bn. This figure represents a 269% upside to the RM953m carrying value of GENT's 20.3% TauRx as of Dec23.
However, we note two key caveats: 1) the transaction involves only 8,000 shares- small transaction; and a fraction of TauRx's total outstanding shares, which raises questions about its reliability as a basis for a broader valuation, and 2) Dundee Corporation views TauRx as a non-core investment and is actively seeking an exit. Given these factors, we believe the implied valuation may not accurately represent the true potential of a more significant stake, and further validation through additional transactions or market interest would be necessary.
Corporate bonds due in 2027E are likely to be refinanced. As at 4Q24, GENT's net debt stood at RM16.8bn, up from RM15.3bn, with a net gearing ratio of 0.31x. GENT faces bond maturities of RM1.9bn and US$1.5bn, respectively in 2027E, with the latter tied to RWLV. From a capital repayment perspective, repayment through internal cash flow may be challenging due to RWLV's underperformance amid ongoing headwinds. Additionally, the high-interest rate environment and widening credit spreads for underperforming assets suggest that refinancing costs will likely be significantly higher. Given the limited availability of alternative funding options, we believe that debt rollover remains the most viable approach, despite the expected increase in interest expenses. As such, we have revised our interest rate assumption to 5.4%, similar to the 2024 level (from 5% previously).
Cut 2025-27E earnings by 19-23%. We lower our 2025-27E earnings forecasts by 19-23% following revisions to our GENM forecasts, lower RWLV contributions, and higher interest expense. Post-earnings cut, we expect GENT's group revenue to grow by 3-5% YoY across 2025-27E, driven by its gaming and leisure segment. The group's EBITDA margins are expected to improve gradually, supported by a rebound in RWLV and RWS, albeit off 2024's low base. Our 2025-26E forecasts are 14-22% below consensus, mainly due to more conservative GENM estimates. Overall, we project GENT's core PATAMI growth of 21%/25%/31% for 2025-27E, albeit from a low base.
Lower dividend received from listed subsidiary. GENM has historically contributed 40% of GENT's total dividends received from its listed subsidiary (GENM/GENS/GENP), with GENT distributing 58% of these dividends to its own shareholders. However, GENM's decision to cut its 2024 final DPS to 4sen (from 9sen) and its focus on preserving capital for future investments will likely impact group-level dividend payout. We now expect total cash dividends received by GENT from listed subsidiaries to decline to RM1.2-1.3bn in 2025-27E (down 3-9% from 2024 levels).
Expecting a lower DPS. With GENT also cutting its own final DPS to 5sen (from 9sen), we adopt a more conservative stance and revise our 2025-27E DPS forecasts to 13.0/13.5/14sen (from 16sen previously), implying payout ratios of 42%/35%/27%, respectively. The lower implied payout ratios over 2025-27E reflect a more cautious capital management approach, in light of softer upstream contributions. Our forecast translates to dividend yield of 4% over the next 3-years.
Maintain BUY with a lower SOP-derived target price of RM3.55. Following the earnings cut and reflecting GENM's latest target price, our 12-month TP is lowered to RM3.55 (from RM4.15). The rest of our valuation assumptions are unchanged: 1) 7x 2025E EV/EBITDA for GENS, 2) 9x 2025E EV/EBITDA for Genting Plantation (GENP), 3) FCFF at 8.1% WACC and 0.5% terminal growth for RWLV, and associated licensing fees, 4) 4x 2025E EV/EBITDA for power, and oil & gas operations, and 5) 65% holding company discount. We believe the steep holding discount remains warranted, given the earnings contribution mismatch between RWLV and its weight in the SOP valuation. That said, our revised RWLV valuation is now more closely aligned with its $4.3bn development cost, although it still commands a premium to book value due to its cumulative losses. Our revised TP implies 5.6x 2025E EV/EBITDA, near -1SD of its 10-year historical mean.
Compelling valuation. GENT's share price has declined by 15% YTD and is now trading at 5x EV/EBITDA and 0.4x 2025E P/BV, near all-time lows (-1.8SD and -1.5SD from its 10-year mean, respectively). Furthermore, GENT is trading at a 46% holding company discount, compared to an average discount of 40% over the past 5 years, further highlighting its appeal. The current valuation does not fully reflect the upside potential from TauRx, which remains underappreciated due to its complex timeline and mixed clinical results. While there are concerns about a value trap, we believe GENT's more diversified earnings base relative to GENM makes it a more compelling pick.
Key risks to our BUY call include weaker-than-expected earnings contributions from its subsidiaries, lower-than-expected win rates, rising operational costs, and a decline in both gaming and non-gaming revenue.
Source: Phillip Capital Research - 7 Apr 2025

title: Genting Malaysia Berhad - Unfavourable Related Party Transaction
author: PublicInvest
body:
Genting Malaysia (GENM) announced the acquisition of the remaining 51% stake in New York state entity Empire Resorts (Empire) that it does not already own from Kien Huat Realty III (Kien Huat) for USD41m cash. Concurrently, GENM is also accepting a debt to be assigned by Kien Huat amounting to USD39.7m. GENM currently holds a 49% stake in Empire, which remains a loss-making unit since its initial acquisition back in 2019. After more than 5 years, the Group has failed to turnaround Empire and we view this related party transaction negatively as it is likely to drag the Group further with a higher share of losses. We cut our F25-27F earnings by 10-16% to reflect the recognition of higher losses from Empire and a weaker consumer sentiment in the US following the escalation of the trade war. As the operating environment remains uncertain in the US, we ascribe a 10% discount to our SOTP valuation. Our revise TP is RM1.66 , downgrade GENM to Trading Sell from Neutral.
Related party transaction....again. Kien Huat is the family trust of Tan Sri Lim Kok Thay, the CEO of GENM. In 2019, GENM acquired a 46% stake in Empire from Kien Huat for USD128m cash. Since 2019, GENM had invested USD724m in Empire, making several capital injections by acquiring common and preferred stocks of Empire. Essentially, we view this as financial assistance extended by GENM to ensure Empire remains operational under a competitive business environment in the US. Empire is a gaming company that owns and operates an integrated casino resort (Resorts World Catskills) located 90 miles from New York City and a shopping mall casino featuring over 1,200 video lottery terminals (Resorts World Hudson Valley) in Newburgh, New York.
Negative impact on GENM. Between FY2020 and FY2024, GENM has recognised toal associated losses of RM160-280m a year, which we attribute the bulk of this to Empire. We project that it would remain a loss-making operation of GENM due to the cannibalisation of Resorts World Catskills (RWC) following the opening of Resorts World Hudson Valley in December 2022. The distance between the two is only ~40 miles, resulting in a direct competition which affected the profitability of RWC. Coupled with a subdued consumer sentiment and rising cost of operation in the US, we slash our FY25-27F earnings forecasts by 10-16%. While GENM's share price has fallen by 22% YTD, we see little earnings catalyst at this juncture as the acquisition would aggravate its weaker-than-expected earnings recovery due to escalating costs for its overall integrated resort operations. Morever, this unfavourable related party transaction suggests that corporate governance remains a concern for this Group. As such, we downgrade GENM from Neutral to Trading Sell.
Source: PublicInvest Research - 5 May 2025

title: ‘Pricey’ Deal for Empire Resorts to Drag Genting Malaysia’s Earnings — Analysts
author: edgeinvest
body:
KUALA LUMPUR (May 5): Genting Malaysia Bhd’s (KL:GENM) deal to gain full control of loss-making Empirie Resorts Inc for US$41 million (RM177 million) is deemed “pricey” and will likely drag the group’s earnings with a higher share of losses, said analysts.
HongLeong Investment Bank (HLIB) said the price tag represents an enterprise value to earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortisation multiple of 72.7 times, compared with US-listed peers’ average of 10 times.
“Given the stark premium relative to sector benchmarks, we consider the proposed transaction to be pricey,” HLIB said in a note on Monday.
Genting Malaysia is acquiring the remaining 51% stake in Genting Empire Resorts LLC (GERL), which owns Empire Resorts, in a US$41 million deal with the Lim family’s Kien Huat Realty III Ltd. The deal also involves Kien Huat Realty assigning a US$39.7 million debt that Empire Resorts owes to Genting Malaysia.
Analysts also view the deal negatively concerning its impact on Genting Malaysia’s earnings.
Since acquiring the initial 49% stake in Empire Resorts in 2019 for US$128 million from Kien Huat Realty, Genting Malaysia has failed to turn around the unit. Assuming full control of Empire Resorts will likely drag the group further with a higher share of losses, according to PublicInvest Research.
“Between FY2020 and FY2024, Genting Malaysia has recognised total associated losses of RM160 million to RM280 million a year, which we attribute the bulk of this to Empire Resorts.
“We project that it would remain a loss-making operation of Genting Malaysia due to the cannibalisation of Resorts World Catskills following the opening of Resorts World Hudson Valley in December 2022,” the house said.
In line with this, PublicInvest cut its earnings forecast on Genting Malaysia for FY2025-27 by 10% to 16% to reflect the expected higher share of losses as well as weaker consumer sentiment in the US following the escalation of the trade war.
PublicInvest downgraded Genting Malaysia to “trading sell” and cut its target price (TP) to RM1.66 from RM2.53, saying the deal will drag the group’s weaker-than-expected earnings recovery, and corporate governance remains a concern given the “unfavourable” related party transaction.
While HLIB also expects the proposed acquisition to be profit-dilutive and place additional strain on the group’s balance sheet, the house upgraded its rating on Genting Malaysia to “hold’ but with a downgraded TP of RM1.80, from RM1.99, citing recent share price correction.
HLIB raised its earnings forecast on Genting Malaysia for FY2025 by 5% and FY2026 by 1% on annual report adjustments but noted it has not incorporated the effects of the Empire Resorts deal into its model.
At the time of writing, shares in Genting Malaysia were down five sen or 2.86% to RM1.70, valuing the group at RM10.09 billion.
Source: TheEdge - 6 May 2025

title: CreditSights Flags Genting Malaysia's Takeover of Empire Resorts as Credit Negative Amid Debt, Related-party Transaction Concerns
author: edgeinvest
body:
KUALA LUMPUR (May 7): Genting Malaysia Bhd's (KL:GENM) takeover of Genting Empire Resorts, which owns gaming properties in New York through Empire Resorts (ERI), is seen as credit negative by CreditSights. This is due to the increased debt to support ERI's weak earnings outlook and concerns over related-party transactions (RPTs).
GENM signed an agreement to acquire a 51% stake in Genting Empire Resorts from Kien Huat Realty III Ltd, owned by Genting promoters. The acquisition will increase GENM’s ownership to 100%. CreditSights is concerned about RPTs due to GENM's history with such deals, some of which were unfavorable to creditors. The deal also raises questions about its fairness.
While the acquisition strengthens GENM’s New York operations, ERI’s earnings outlook remains weak, pressured by competition and profit losses at its two New York resorts. ERI’s total debt is estimated at RM1.3 billion (US$300 million), with earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda) of US$27 million for nine-month 2024 and gross leverage of 11 times.
CreditSights said the deal will increase GENM’s debt by US$300 million and worsen its leverage metrics by 0.3 to 0.4 times. GENM’s cash will decrease by US$41 million. The acquisition, to be completed by the second quarter of 2025, will be funded by GENM’s cash and cash flow.
It expects ongoing support for ERI from GENM, as it has invested US$725 million in ERI and views it as key to its New York expansion. A default at ERI would damage Genting Bhd’s (KL:GENTING) reputation, especially as it expands in New York and Singapore, lowering the refinancing risk for ERI’s US$300 million bond due in 2026.
CreditSights said ERI’s situation is different from Genting Hong Kong (GENHK), which defaulted in 2020. GENM had exited GENHK in 2016 and did not consider it strategic. In contrast, GENM steadily increased its stake in ERI, which it sees as strategically important.
CreditSights said despite these concerns it has an "outperform" call on GENM bonds and a “market perform” call on Genting’s bonds.
It said GENM’s 2031 bonds are cheaper than similar bonds, and they are expected to rise by 10-15 basis points, supporting the "outperform" rating. It said GENM’s strong presence in Malaysia and potential growth from a New York casino could balance out its debt and governance issues.
On Genting’s 2027 bonds, it said they are fairly priced compared to peers due to its strong diversification and the expected New York casino, which also helps offset governance risks.
Source: TheEdge - 8 May 2025

title: Bursa Grills Genting Malaysia Over US$41m Empire Resorts Buyout
author: edgeinvest
body:
KUALA LUMPUR (May 8): Genting Malaysia Bhd’s (KL:GENM) proposed US$41 million (RM175.5 million) acquisition to gain full control of the loss-making Empire Resorts Inc from Genting group's founding Lim family has come under the scrutiny of Bursa Malaysia Securities Bhd.
The bourse regulator on Thursday slapped GENM with 20 questions on the deal, which would see it buy the remaining 51% stake in Genting Empire Resorts LLC (GERL) that it does not currently own from Kien Huat Realty III Ltd. GERL owns Empire Resorts, while Kien Huat Realty III is owned by the Lim family, led by Tan Sri Lim Kok Thay.
The acquisition will turn Empire Resorts, the operator of Resorts World Catskills, Resorts World Hudson Valley, and Resorts World Bet in New York, from being GENM's 49%-owned associate to a fully-owned subsidiary.
Under the deal, Kien Huat Realty III will assign a US$39.7 million debt — including accrued interest — that Empire Resorts owes, to GENM.
Among the questions posed by Bursa were those that sought to clarify the rationale for the acquisition, justifications for its purchase price, whether any valuation was done on GERL, liabilities to be assumed by GENM, financial information on GERL and Empire Resorts, and their prospects.
In response, GENM said no separate valuation was conducted on GERL, as the relevant valuation should be on Empire Resorts. The planned US$41 million acquisition also falls within the independently assessed market value range of US$36.5 million to US$46.9 million for Empire Resorts, it said.
It said the valuation was performed by independent valuer CBRE Securities LLC on April 22, 2025, based on weighted average of discounted cash flow analysis (50%), precedent transaction multiples (35%) and public market comparables (15%).
GENM assured that no additional liabilities, including contingent liabilities and guarantees, will be assumed by the company, aside from paying the purchase price upon the deal's completion.
It also stated that GERL recorded a net loss of US$54.1 million for the financial year ended Dec 31, 2024 (FY2024), down from US$65.4 million in FY2023, but slightly higher than the US$53.4 million it incurred in FY2022.
Empire Resorts, meanwhile, posted a net loss of US$53.1 million in FY2024, lower than US$57 million in FY2023, but higher than US$44.2 million in FY2022. Annual revenue grew to US$296.3 million in FY2024 from US$292.2 million in FY2023, and US$267.3 million in FY2022.
Looking ahead, GENM said Empire Resorts will concentrate on increasing gaming revenues for Resorts World Catskills by broadening its demographic reach to key upstate markets. It would also continue to streamline its operations to rationalise costs.
However, GENM cautioned that there is no guarantee Empire Resorts will be able to maintain a positive trajectory in its financial and operational performance.
“Empire [Resorts]’s performance is subject to risks inherent in the gaming industry which may include, but are not limited to regulatory policy changes, volatility of gaming revenues and additional competition. Any economic slowdown may also have an impact on the business and its cash flows,” the company said.
GENM also stated that interested directors in the deal have and will continue to abstain from all discussions and vote on the acquisition at the group’s board meetings.
GENM first acquired a 46% stake in Empire Resorts, which has been loss-making for over two decades, from Kien Huat Realty III for US$128 million in cash in 2019. GENM's investments in Empire Resorts so far totalled US$724.4 million, following several capital injections through common and preferred stocks that were widely seen as financial aid rather than investments.
A pricey, unfavourable deal
Analysts tracking GENM have expressed concerns that the deal could negatively impact the group’s earnings, as they see little chance of Empire Resorts turning a profit anytime soon.
“Between FY2020 and FY2024, Genting Malaysia recognised total associated losses of RM160 million to RM280 million a year, which we attribute the bulk of to Empire Resorts," said PublicInvest Research in its note on Monday.
“We project that it would remain a loss-making operation of Genting Malaysia due to the cannibalisation of Resorts World Catskills following the opening of Resorts World Hudson Valley in December 2022,” the research house stated.
The proposed acquisition led PublicInvest to downgrade GENM to a “trading sell” and reduce its target price (TP) to RM1.66 from RM2.53, citing concerns that the deal would hinder the group’s weaker-than-expected earnings recovery, and that corporate governance remains a worry given the “unfavourable” related-party transaction.
The acquisition price also represented an enterprise value to earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortisation multiple of 72.7 times, significantly higher than the average of 10 times for US-listed peers, Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB) flagged in another note.
“Given the stark premium relative to sector benchmarks, we consider the proposed transaction to be pricey,” HLIB said. HLIB upgraded its rating on Genting Malaysia to “hold” but with a lowered TP of RM1.80, from RM1.99, referencing the recent share price correction.
Among analysts tracked by Bloomberg , out of the 17 research firms covering GENM, six have “buy” calls, seven have “hold” recommendations, and four have “sell” ratings, with an average TP of RM2.16. CGS International gave it the highest TP at RM3.65, while Nomura has the lowest at RM1.60.
On Thursday, GENM's share price slipped one sen or 0.57% to close at RM1.73, giving the group a market capitalisation of RM9.81 billion. Year to date, the stock has dropped 23%.
Source: TheEdge - 9 May 2025

title: Genting Berhad - Disappointing Results
author: PublicInvest
body:
Genting Bhd (GENT) posted a meagre headline net profit of RM4.6m in 1QFY25 compared to RM588m in 1QFY24. The disappointing set of results was due to a sharp decline in Singapore's earnings on lower win rate and weaker business volume as well as lower contribution from Genting Malaysia (GENM). Stripping out non-operating items, core net profit of RM196m only accounted for 11% and 13% of our and consensus full-year forecasts, respectively. We believe sentiments in the leisure and entertainment industry will remain lacklustre given the uncertain global macroeconomic conditions. We cut our FY25-27F earnings forecasts by an average of 24% due to a downward revision in leisure & hospitality profit. Following our downgrade of GENM's rating on 5 May and a lower consensus valuation for Genting Singapore (GENS), we now cut our rating on GENT to Neutral with a revised TP of RM3.50 .
1QFY25 revenue fell by 12.4% YoY, as contribution from all major segments was lower, particularly Singapore (-25% YoY) and the US (-19% YoY). As the leisure & hospitality segment accounted for 82% of the group's revenue, the increase in revenue from plantation (+21% YoY) and power (+56% YoY) segments was not sufficient to mitigate the drop in revenue from its casino and integrated resorts operations.
1QFY25 core net profit was down 76% YoY, largely due to lower profit from Singapore (-40% YoY) and the US & Bahamas (-51% YoY), Both markets were affected by lower hold percentage and visitation as well as higher operating cost.
Downgrade to Neutral. As the group's hospitality businesses are generally dependent on Chinese tourist arrivals, the economic slowdown in China is expected to impact its operations, especially in Singapore. Meanwhile, the group has indicated its plan to participate in the bidding for casino license in Thailand. As the approval and construction of integrated resorts would normally take years to materialise, we do not expect this to have any immediate impact on the group's financials. As we have adjusted down our valuation for GENM following its controversial proposed acquisition of Empire Resorts and coupled with a lower consensus valuation for GENS, our SOTP-based TP for GENT is reduced to RM3.50 . In view of a possible global economic slowdown that would affect sentiments in the leisure and entertainment industry, we downgrade GENT from Outperform to Neutral .
Source: PublicInvest Research - 30 May 2025

title: Genting Malaysia Berhad - Earnings Recovery Remained Weak
author: PublicInvest
body:
Genting Malaysia (GENM) posted a net profit of RM72.6m in 1QFY25, grew by 25.7% YoY mainly due to unrealised foreign exchange translation gain of RM50.4m. After stripping out non-core items, normalised net profit came in below our and consensus full-year estimates of RM518.5m and RM636.9m respectively. Despite the weaker-than-expected performance, which we attribute to a more subdued consumer spending on leisure and entertainment activities, we retain our earnings forecasts for now given the poor earnings visibility. While we believe demand for international tourism will remain resilient, the uncertain global economic conditions could lead to higher cost of operations in the near term. We maintain our Trading Sell rating with an unchanged TP of RM1.66 .
1QFY25 revenue was down 6.1% YoY, as all business segments posted lower revenue. Malaysia suffered a 7% drop in revenue despite the Chinese New Year festival in Jan/Feb 2025, which would normally result in a seasonally stronger 1Q. Business volume in the premium players segment was weaker. The UK & Egypt and the US & Bahamas posted a 7% and 3% decline in revenue due to the strengthening of the ringgit against the GBP and USD.
1QFY25 net profit lifted by forex gain . The group posted an unrealised forex translation gain of RM50.4m from its USD-denominated borrowings, lifting 1QFY25 pretax profit by 58.7% YoY. However, this was partly offset by an increase in tax cost following the end of the tax incentives given out under the Genting Integrated Tourism Plan. Tax cost increased to RM132m from RM79.2m in 1QFY24.
Outlook . We expect visitor arrivals to continue to improve after the Malaysian government granted an extension of visa exemption for Chinese tourists until end 2026. This should augur well for Malaysia's tourism and hospitality industry. However, escalating cost of operations, has affected profitability despite the strong recovery in business volume to pre-pandemic levels. While GENM 's share price has fallen by 19% YTD, we see little earnings catalyst at this juncture as the acquisition of Empire Resorts would aggravate its weaker-than-expected earnings recovery. Moreover, the unfavourable related party transaction suggests that corporate governance remains a concern for this group.
Source: PublicInvest Research - 30 May 2025

title: Genting Malaysia - Registered a mild profit
author: HLInvest
body:
GenM registered 1QFY25 core PATMI of RM31.1m (vs -RM120.8m in 4QFY24, -84.8% YoY), which came in below our (6%) and consensus’ (6%) full year forecasts. The key negative deviation to our forecast was mainly due to higherthan-expected finance costs, share of larger losses from Empire Resorts, and elevated tax expenses. Going forward, we expect the positive outlook for tourism in Malaysia will be neutralised by continued operating challenges from the group’s UK and US business segments, as well as Empire Resorts. We lowered our FY25f-27f by -36.0%/-40.3%/-37.5%. Reiterate Hold, with a slightly higher SOP-derived TP of RM1.82, as we roll-forward our valuation base year to FY2026 from FY2025.
Missed expectations. GenM reported 1QFY25 core PATMI of RM31.1m (vs -RM120.8m in 4QFY24, -84.8% YoY), which came in below our (6%) and consensus’ (6%) full year forecasts. The key negative deviation to our forecast was mainly due to higher-than-expected finance costs, share of larger losses from Empire Resorts, and elevated tax expenses. Notably, our 1QFY25 core PATMI was arrived at after stripping off EIs amounting to RM41.5m, mainly from net forex gains.
Dividend. Nil in 1QFY25 (vs nil in 1QFY24).
QoQ. Revenue decreased 4.9% (Leisure and Hospitality businesses in Malaysia: -8.8%, UK & Egypt: -7.4%, US & Bahamas: +8.6%). The weaker group revenue was largely dragged by the leisure and hospitality businesses in Malaysia due to the Ramadan period. Despite with a weaker revenue, GenM returned to the black of RM31.1m (vs -RM120.8m), boosted by ongoing cost optimisation measures.
YoY. Revenue saw a decline of 6.1% (Leisure and Hospitality businesses in Malaysia: -7.2%, UK & Egypt: -6.6%, US & Bahamas: -3.3%). The softness in group revenue was mainly impacted by the leisure and hospitality businesses in Malaysia due to the similar reasons mentioned in QoQ paragraph. In tandem with weaker revenue, GenM’s bottom-line deteriorated at a greater pace of 84.8%, primarily due to higher finance and tax expenses.
Outlook. Despite GenM continuing to benefit from the positive outlook of tourism in Malaysia (Figure 1), we expect continued operating challenges/uncertainties from its UK and US business segments as well as Empire Resorts, which could pose downside risks to the recovery of its Malaysian operations; GenM owns and operates Malaysia's only integrated resort – Resorts World Genting (RWG).
Forecast. Given the results shortfall, we cut FY25f-27f by -36.0%/-40.3%/-37.5% to mainly reflect higher finance and tax expenses, as well as larger loss sharing from Empire Resorts.
Maintain Hold, with a slightly higher TP at RM1.82. We reiterate Hold on GenM, with a slightly higher SOP-derived TP of RM1.82 (from RM1.80 previously), as we roll-forward our valuation base year to FY2026 from FY2025.
Source: Hong Leong Investment Bank Research - 30 May 2025

title: Genting - Dragged by GenM and GenS
author: HLInvest
body:
GenT registered 1QFY25 core PATMI of RM195.8m (-16.6% QoQ, -71.4% YoY), which came in below both our (12%) and consensus’ (13%) full year forecasts. The negative deviation was mainly due to the underperformance in GenM and GenS. Hence, we cut FY25f-26f by -26.0%/-27.6% to reflect earnings revision on both of them. Besides, we introduce FY27 core PATMI of RM1,421.6m (+8.7% YoY). Going forward, GenT is expected to benefit from the stronger foreign tourist arrivals at both Singapore and Malaysia. Furthermore, GenT has the potential value-add from TauRx Pharmaceutical if HMTM receives FDA approval. Maintain BUY on GenT, with a lower SOP-derived TP of RM4.44.
Below expectations. GenT recorded 1QFY25 core PATMI of RM195.8m (-16.6% QoQ, -71.4% YoY), which came in below both our (12%) and consensus’ (13%) full year forecasts. The negative deviation from our forecast was mainly due to the underperformance at GenM (mainly higher-than-expected finance and tax expenses) and GenS (lower-than-expected EBITDA margin). Notably, our 1QFY25 core PATMI was arrived at after adding back EIs amounting to RM191.2m, mainly from the net impairment of receivables and PPE impairment losses.
Dividend. Nil in 1QFY25 (vs nil in 1QFY24).
QoQ. Revenue decreased 8.2% (Leisure and Hospitality businesses in Malaysia: -8.8%, Singapore: +2.4%, UK & Egypt: -7.4%, US & Bahamas: -4.0%; Power: -25.5%; Plantation: -32.6%). The overall revenue weakness was mainly due to lower business volume at GenM, as well as lower FFB production (arising from seasonality and unusually high rainfall in part of its estates in Malaysia) at its Plantation segment. In tandem with lower revenue, GenT’s core PATMI dropped 16.6%.
YoY. Revenue contracted 14.0% (Leisure and Hospitality businesses in Malaysia: -7.2%, Singapore: -25.3%, UK & Egypt: -6.6%, US & Bahamas: -18.7%; Power: +56.1%; Plantation: -2.8%). The overall revenue softness was mainly dragged by lower business volume at GenM (the timing of the festive season - Ramadan period), as well as GenS (lower VIP rolling win rate and temporary closure of Hard Rock hotel for renovation and rebranding works). Core PATMI deteriorated at a stronger pace of -71.4% as a result of unfavourable operating leverage in GenM and GenS.
Outlook. Going forward, GenT is expected to benefit from the stronger foreign tourist arrivals at both Singapore and Malaysia (Figure #1 & #2). The recovery in Singapore will be mainly supported by improved global flight connectivity and capacity, the launch of new attractions - such as Lady Gaga concerts, Illumination’s Minion Land, Mandai Rainforest Wild Asia, and Disney Adventure Cruise Ship - as well as the mutual 30-day visa exemption between Singapore and China. For Malaysia, it will be mainly fuelled by the ASEAN Chairmanship in 2025 and Visit Malaysia Year 2026. Besides, GenT has the potential value-add from TauRx Pharmaceutical if its drug, hydromethylthionine mesylate (HMTM) receives FDA approval.
Forecast. Cut FY25f-26f by -26.0%/-27.6% to mainly reflect earnings revision on GenM and GenS. Besides, we introduce FY27 core PATMI of RM1,421.6m (+8.7% YoY).
Maintain BUY, TP lowered to RM4.44 (from RM5.25), based on a 45% discount our SOP-derived value of RM8.08 after we impute revised valuations for GenM, GenS and GenP. We continue to like GenT for its well-established operational presence across diverse regions, mitigating regulatory and country risks.
Source: Hong Leong Investment Bank Research - 30 May 2025

title: Genting Malaysia (GENM MK) - Missed expectations
author: PhillipCapital
body:
GENM's 1Q25 core PATAMI missed expectations, but EBITDA was in line
Weaker VIP demand and continued losses from Empire Resorts hit earnings
Maintain HOLD rating and lower SOP-derived target price of RM1.80 after rolling forward our valuation horizon
1Q25 core net profit of RM54m (-76% YoY), below expectations
Stripping out unrealized forex gains and other non-core items, GENM reported a core net profit of RM54m (-76% YoY). The results missed both our and consensus estimates due to lower-than-expected gaming revenue and larger losses from the increase in its stake in Empire Resorts. Core EBITDA declined 12% YoY mainly dragged by Malaysia and US operations. This resulted in 1.9ppts contraction in EBITDA margins. PATAMI also weighed by the higher-than-expected interest expense (+26% YoY) from the refinancing in 3Q24 and a new Medium-Term Notes issued in 2Q24, and 2) effective tax (+66% YoY) after the fully utilisation of tax incentives under Genting Integrated Tourism Plan (GITP) scheme.
Hilltop traffic slows and Empire drags earnings
Visitor numbers to GenM's Hilltop property dropped 2% YoY and 7% QoQ to 5.7m, partly due to changes in festive timing. Gaming revenue also declined to RM1,852.6m, mainly due to weaker VIP demand. GenM's 2025E earnings are expected to stay well below pre-pandemic levels, impacted by continued losses from Empire Resorts. Meanwhile, the downstate NYC casino license still on track with its timetable, with the US team is in the midst of preparation for the tender submission by 27 June25. The management also guided no major capex will be incurred in the remaining of 2025.
Maintain HOLD with a lower TP of RM1.80
We cut our 2025-27E earnings by 31-50% to account for softer Malaysia and US operations. Our TP is lowered to RM1.80 (from RM1.85) after rolling forward our valuation horizon, and maintain our HOLD rating. We see potential upside if GENM secures the downstate NYC casino license, expected to be awarded by end-25. Key downside risks include lower-than-expected win rates, a hike in gaming taxes, drag from key associates, and value-destructive related-party transactions.
Source: Phillip Capital Research - 30 May 2025

title: Genting Malaysia Berhad - Challenging Outlook
author: sectoranalyst
body:
Review
Genting Malaysia’s (GENM) 1Q25 core profit of RM104.7mn came in below expectations. The variance was largely due to weaker-thanexpectation performance from Malaysia and UK operations as well as higher-than-expected tax rate.
1Q25 adjusted EBITDA expanded by 12.7% YoY to RM737.2mn despite a 6.1% drop in revenue to RM6.1bn. All gaming units reported lower revenue and EBITDA on the back of lower business volume and rise in staff cost. However, the impact was mitigated by the foreign translation gain. Excluding the gain, 1Q25 adjusted EBITDA would have declined by 12% YoY. On the tax front, the 66% jump in tax expense was due to full utilisation of tax incentive granted under the Genting Integrated Tourism Plan (GITP) in FY24.
On QoQ basis, the group managed to turn around from core losses of RM419.3mn in 4Q24. This was mainly due to foreign translation gain. Operationally, all gaming units recorded higher EBITDA due to decline in marketing costs.
Impact
We cut our FY25-26 earnings projections by 41-61% after revising our VIP volume assumptions to -8% growth (vs +5% previously) for Malaysia operations. Also, we revise our effective tax rate assumption of 24-30% (vs 15%) for FY25-26.
Conference call highlights
Resorts World Genting’s revenue slipped 7.2% YoY due to lower gross gaming revenue (GGR), which management attributed to timing of festive season and lower VIP volume. For this quarter, visitations to hilltop declined by 7% QoQ and 2% YoY to 5.7mn. Total GGR was lower by 9% QoQ and 7% YoY, where the VIP volume dropped by 19% QoQ and 18% YoY. This was partially offset by increase in non-VIP volume, up 4% QoQ and 7% YoY.
Empire Resorts (Empire) reported lower EBITDA of US$1.7mn, down from US$3mn last year. It is expected to improve in 2Q-3Q when the winter season is over. With regards to GENM’s action to acquire the remaining stake in Empire Resorts via a related party transaction (RPT), the earnings impact is expected to be muted as the group has recognised 90% of Empire’s losses given its effective holding of 90% economic interest in Empire.
Recall, GENM submitted 2 bids of up to USD1.5bn for casino resort projects in upstate New York back in 2015, but to no avail. In 2019, the company had participated in a joint acquisition exercise to privatise Empire and later subscribed for preferred stocks of Empire. Obviously, GENM has a clear determination in growing its presence in the U.S. gaming industry. As such, the acquisition of the remaining 51% stake (or 10% of the economic interest) in Empire, is just a work in progress for its U.S. expansion plan, although the market dislike the RPT, in our opinion.
With regards to the new casino licence in downstate New York, management indicated that the company is currently working on the bid and would submit before the deadline on June 27.
Valuation
Post earnings revision, we reduce GENM’s DCF valuation to RM2.24/share (from RM3.09) with unchanged CAPM of 19.3%. Maintain Buy
Source: TA Research - 30 May 2025

title: Genting Berhad - Simultaneous Setbacks
author: sectoranalyst
body:
Review
Genting Berhad’s (Genting) 1Q25 core profit of RM76.9mn came in below market expectation. The earnings miss was largely due to lowerthan-expected contribution from gaming operations in Singapore, Malaysia, UK and Las Vegas.
Genting’s 1Q25 adjusted EBITDA slumped 22.7% YoY to RM2.0bn with revenue dropping 12.4% YoY to RM6.5bn. The disappointment was driven by lacklustre performance of all gaming units, mitigated by higher contribution from the plantation and power segments.
GENS’ 1Q25 adj. EBITDA declined 36.2% YoY to S$235.8mn with revenue dropping 20.2% to S$626.2mn. The decline was due to high-base effect as 1Q24 earnings were spurred by high VIP volume, which led to margin expansion. For this quarter, the gaming revenue has normalised to S$437.5mn (-24% YoY) while the adj. EBITDA margin softened to 38.7%.
GENM’s 1Q25 adj. EBITDA expanded by 12.7% YoY to RM737.2mn despite a 6.1% drop in revenue to RM6.1bn. All gaming units reported lower revenue and EBITDA on the back of lower business volume and rise in staff cost. At the bottom-line, the decline was compounded further by a 66% jump in tax expense due to full utilisation of tax incentive granted under the Genting Integrated Tourism Plan (GITP). (see GENM report)
Resorts World Las Vegas’s (RWLV) 1QFY25 revenue declined 26.6% YoY to RM740.9mn while the adjusted EBITDA dropped 74.6% to RM47.2mn. The drop was due to lower hold percentage and lower visitation compared with the record visitation during the NFL Super Bowl event in 1Q24.
Impact
We cut GENT’s FY25-26 earnings lower by 47-68% after revising GENS and RWLV’s earnings lower, as well as incorporating GENM’s revised earnings projections.
Outlook
Pertaining to the allegation of illegal gambling, the regulator has fined RWLS $10.5mn and the case is settled. With regards to the U.S. reciprocal tariff, the group has not seen a noticeable impact on the visitation.
Valuation
Following the earnings revisions, we reduce GENT’s SOP valuation to RM3.56/share (from RM4.02) after the earnings downgrade. However, we maintain our Buy recommendation on the stock as we believe the sell down is overdone.
Source: TA Research - 30 May 2025

title: Forex Gain Lifts Genting Malaysia's 1Q Profit Despite Revenue Slip
author: edgeinvest
body:
KUALA LUMPUR (May 29): Genting Malaysia Bhd's (KL:GENM) net profit rose 25.69% year-on-year (y-o-y) in the first quarter ended March 31, 2025 on the back of foreign exchange gains and improved cost management.
The group, which fell into the red in the fourth quarter last year, saw net profit rise to RM72.58 million or 1.28 sen per share, from RM57.78 million or 1.02 sen per share a year earlier.
Quarterly revenue slipped 6.14% y-o-y to RM2.6 billion from RM2.76 billion due to weaker contributions from its leisure and hospitality segments in Malaysia and the UK, as well as currency translation effects.
No dividend was announced for the quarter.
For the quarter, Genting Malaysia’s leisure and hospitality segment accounted for RM2.54 billion or 97.76% of group revenue. Its Malaysian operations contributed RM1.62 billion, down 7% y-o-y, mainly due to the timing of festive seasons and lower premium player volumes.
Revenue from the UK and Egypt dropped 7% to RM413.4 million due to adverse forex effects. Revenue from the US and Bahamas, meanwhile, fell 3% to RM501.3 million.
The group remains cautiously optimistic on its near-term prospects as "the regional gaming market may face increasing challenges" although the hospitality sector is still positive, it said.
It aims to enhance Resorts World Genting’s appeal through new ecotourism offerings and anniversary celebrations.
A key development includes the RM177 million acquisition of a remaining 51% stake in Genting Empire Resorts LLC, positioning the group for growth in New York’s gaming market, pending regulatory approval, it said.
"The group continues to closely monitor developments related to the New York Gaming Facility Board's Request for Applications, and is preparing to participate in the process as part of its broader growth strategy," it added.
Shares of Genting Malaysia settled up two sen or 1.11% to RM1.82 on Thursday, giving it a market capitalisation of RM10.81 billion. The counter is down 19% this year.
Source: TheEdge - 30 May 2025

title: Genting's 1Q Net Profit Down Sharply Amid Lower Revenues From Casinos and Higher Taxation
author: edgeinvest
body:
KUALA LUMPUR (May 29): Genting Bhd’s (KL:GENTING) net profit shrank to only RM4.57 million for the first quarter ended March 31, 2025 (1QFY2025), from RM588.87 million a year ago.
The sharp fall in net profit was partly due to lower quarterly revenue, which fell 12.4% to RM6.51 billion from RM7.43 billion in 1QFY2024. The group’s hospitality segment generated a lower contribution of RM5.34 billion in the quarter under review compared with RM6.48 billion a year ago, according to its bourse filing.
Meanwhile, the group’s other income halved to RM257 million versus RM532 million a year ago, and losses from its share of results in joint ventures and associates also doubled to RM28 million.
Furthermore, it incurred taxation of RM348.61 million, which was roughly 9% lower compared with RM381.8 million a year ago although its pre-tax profit contracted substantially to RM626.2 million versus RM1.38 billion in 1QFY2024.
Notably, the group booked a higher impairment loss of RM72 million compared with RM6.21 million a year earlier.
Earnings per share contracted to 0.12 sen from 15.29 sen a year ago.
No dividend was declared for the quarter.
In a press statement, Genting noted that while demand for international tourism is expected to remain resilient, the recovery is likely to be uneven across regions amid ongoing global uncertainties. As a result, the regional gaming market could face mounting challenges.
The group remains cautiously optimistic about the near-term outlook for the leisure and hospitality industry and maintains a positive view on its long-term prospects.
"Amid heightened geopolitical trade tensions and macroeconomic headwinds, Genting Singapore Ltd Group continues to adopt a prudent and adaptive approach, leveraging on its strong regional presence and financial strength to navigate through a challenging global environment," said Genting.
Genting shares fell five sen to close at RM3.13 on Thursday, giving the group a market capitalisation of RM12.1 billion. The stock has fallen 32.5% over the past 12 months from RM4.64.
Source: TheEdge - 30 May 2025

title: Genting Malaysia - Bringing a Painful Chapter to a Close
author: kltrader
body:
Trim SOTP-TP to MYR2.08 but U/G to BUY
GENM will acquire the remaining 10% economic interest in loss generating Empire Resorts (Empire) (Fig. 1). Our FY25E-FY27E earnings are trimmed 2-4% on the higher economic interest. We cut our SOTP-TP to MYR2.08 from MYR2.41 as we impute higher debt and capex. We do not view this proposal positively but hope that this will be the last value destroying related party transaction (RPT). With >20% total returns to our TP, we upgrade GENM to BUY from HOLD. Key near term catalysts are: (i) resolution to the USD600m lawsuit relating to Resorts World Bimini soon; and (ii) Resorts World New York winning a full casino license by year end.
To own 100% of loss generating Empire Resorts
GENM has proposed to acquire the remaining 51% of Empire common stock from Kien Huat Realty III (KH), which is controlled by the Deputy Chairman & CEO, for USD41m (MYR177m) (Fig. 2). It is expected to be completed by end-2Q25 and does not require shareholders’ approval. Empire owns Resorts World Catskill (integrated casino resort), Resorts World Hudson Valley (video lottery terminal casino) and Resorts World Bet (mobile sports betting) which all operate in the state of New York, United States.
Trim earnings and raise net gearing estimates
Although GENM has hitherto owned 49% of Empire common stock, it has equity accounted 90% of its losses as GENM also owns Empire convertible preferred stock. Thus, accounting for the remaining 10% of Empire’s losses lowers our FY25E/FY26E/FY27E core net profit by -2%/-4%/-3% (Fig. 3). But given that Empire will be a subsidiary instead of an associate going forward, GENM will consolidate Empire’s USD300m (MYR1.3b) Senior Secured Notes and weaken its end-FY25E net gearing to 98% from 79%.
Hopefully the last value destroying RPT
With this proposal, GENM would have poured in USD765.4m (MYR3.3b) into Empire (Fig. 4). We hope this will be the last value destroying RPT by GENM. We continue to impute no value to Empire and consolidate Empire’s USD300m (MYR1.3b) Senior Secured Notes. The 10% discount to our SOTP- based valuation remains but we raise our Resorts World Genting (RWG) capex assumptions on minor housekeeping resulting in a lower SOTP-TP to MYR2.08 from MYR2.41. title: Genting Malaysia Submits Bid for New York Casino Licence
author: edgeinvest
body:
KUALA LUMPUR (June 30): Genting Malaysia Bhd (KL:GENM) announced that a formal bid has been submitted for a casino licence in New York as part of a US$5.5 billion (RM23.19 billion) resort development in Queens.
The bid was submitted on June 27 in response to the New York State Gaming Commission’s request for applications for up to three commercial casinos in downstate New York, where its Resorts World New York City (RWNYC) is located, Genting Malaysia said in an exchange filing.
“RWNYC is uniquely positioned to transform itself into a world-class integrated resort destination with a proposed multi-billion-dollar investment in conjunction with its bid,” Genting Malaysia said. “This will drive RWNYC’s next chapter of growth.”
A decision is expected by Dec 1, followed by the issuance of licences by Dec 31, 2025.
In a separate statement, RWNYC touted that its 5.6 million-square-foot project could provide tax revenue as soon as July 2026, promising to launch table game and full-casino slot machine operations within six months of receiving a gaming facility licence.
The integrated resort will feature a total of a 500,000 sq ft gaming floor with 6,000 slots and 800 table games, 2,000 hotel rooms, a 7,000-seat entertainment venue, over 30 food and beverage outlets, large-scale meeting space and other amenities, as well as more than 10 acres of greenspace.
RWNYC said its current workforce will expand from 1,000 existing employees to 5,000 permanent jobs across gaming, hospitality, food and beverage, security, maintenance, and other fields with the new development.
Genting Malaysia's wholly owned subsidiary Genting New York LLC owns and operates RWNYC, which opened 15 years ago, offering 5,500 slot machines and electronic table games, restaurants and bars, event spaces and a 400-room Hyatt hotel.
Source: TheEdge - 1 Jul 2025

title: Genting Hands Over Coal Plant in China After PPA Expiry, Pivots to Clean Energy
author: edgeinvest
body:
KUALA LUMPUR (July 1): Genting Bhd (KL:GENTING) said its 49%-owned unit has handed over a 786MW coal-fired power plant in Fujian, China, to the local government following the expiry of the 21.5-year power purchase agreement.
The unit, SDIC Genting Meizhou Wan Electric Power Company Ltd (SDICG MZW), has been operating the facility since January 2004 under a build-operate-transfer agreement.
“This handover reflects the group’s long-term commitment to developing a cleaner, more sustainable energy portfolio,” Genting said in a bourse filing on Tuesday.
Post-handover, SDICG MZW will continue to own and operate the 2,000MW ultra-supercritical Meizhou Wan power plant, commissioned in 2017 with advanced generation technology and full environmental compliance.
Genting said it does not plan to pursue new coal projects but will continue to manage its existing coal-fired assets “responsibly until the end of their operational life”, supporting a balanced transition strategy.
The group said its power division remains focused on high-potential investments in renewable and clean energy, including two projects under its joint venture with SDIC Power Holdings Co Ltd.
They are a120MWp aquaculture-complementary solar power plant in Dongwu Cha, Fujian, which commenced commercial operations on May 31, 2025, and a hydrogen-ready 1,490MW gas-fired power plant under development in Zhoushan, China, scheduled for commercial launch by mid-2026.
Genting previously disclosed in June 2024 that it will invest up to RM277 million in the Zhoushan gas plant.
Genting shares closed up three sen or 1% at RM3.08 on Tuesday, giving the group a market capitalisation of RM11.94 billion.
Source: TheEdge - 2 Jul 2025

title: US Court Dismisses Initial Suit by Genting Malaysia's Business Partner, Allows Amended Complaint
author: edgeinvest
body:
Resorts World Bimini in the Bahamas.
KUALA LUMPUR (July 7): A lawsuit filed in the US against Genting Malaysia Bhd (KL:GENM) by its business partner RAV Bahamas Ltd has been dismissed, though the court opened the door for an amended complaint.
The court agreed with Genting Malaysia’s position that the complaint in its initial form was “merely a shareholders’ dispute” in a decision on July 1, and that RAV Bahamas' current allegations are “baseless and without merit”, according to Genting Malaysia in an exchange filing on Monday.
However, the US District Court, Southern District of Florida gave RAV Bahamas one last opportunity to revise its complaint before making its final ruling to toss out the lawsuit, Genting Malaysia said.
In October 2024, Genting Malaysia’s indirect unit Genting Americas Inc, which operates Resorts World Bimini in the Bahamas, was named in a complaint by RAV Bahamas in the court.
RAV Bahamas alleged that Genting Americas has turned RW Bimini into a “financial wasteland” by dumping almost US$1 billion of debt into it, Bahamas’ news portal The Tribune reported.
RAV Bahamas is seeking damages of more than US$600 million (RM2.57 billion) from Genting Americas.
Resorts World Bimini is owned and operated by BB Entertainment Ltd, in which Genting Malaysia indirectly holds a 78% stake, while RAV Bahamas holds the remaining 22% stake. Genting Americas, which is incorporated in Delaware in the US, is an affiliate company of BB Entertainment.
Shares of Genting Malaysia were traded down one sen or 0.5% to RM2 at 2.43pm on Monday, valuing the group at RM11.88 billion.
Source: TheEdge - 8 Jul 2025

title: New York City Casinos Could Become World’s Biggest, Genting Sees Jump in Revenue
author: edgeinvest
body:
LOS ANGELES (July 8): Bidders for three New York City-area casino licences are projecting revenue that would place them among the most lucrative resorts in the world, according to an analysis of their proposals.
In Manhattan, the Freedom Plaza project is expected to generate US$2.2 billion (RM9.35 billion) in annual revenue in its first year of operation, rising to US$4.2 billion by year 10, while billionaire Steve Cohen’s project near Citi Field in Queens is forecast to produce US$3.9 billion annually by year three, according to executive summaries the bidders filed with the New York State Gaming Facility Location Board.
Those sums rival some of the world’s top casino performers. Las Vegas Sands Corp’s Marina Bay Sands Resort in Singapore generated US$4.2 billion in total revenue last year. Wynn Resorts Ltd’s two Las Vegas casinos, the Wynn and Encore, produced a combined US$2.57 billion in revenue in 2024.
The Coney, a resort proposed for Coney Island, is the only project that shared specific revenue estimates by source and year. Its backers, including real estate investor Joe Sitt, project US$669 million in table-game revenue and US$754 million in slot-machine revenue in its first year of operation. By comparison, Wynn’s two Las Vegas casinos generated US$611 million from table games and US$446 million from slots last year.
Eight bidders submitted proposals on June 27. Their bids still need approval from groups of state and local officials, and will be submitted to the state location board if they pass muster. The board plans to pick the winners by Dec 1.
The projects would bring the first full-fledged casinos to America’s most-populous city. The bidders are a mix of billionaires, property owners and established casino operators. Three of the proposals are for Manhattan, with the rest in a suburb or outer borough. Revenue estimates are just projections, and the numbers may change as the bidders update their offers later in the process.
Caesars Entertainment Inc has proposed a casino in Times Square that it said would generate US$23.3 billion in gambling revenue alone, over 10 years. A spokesperson for the project called it an opportunity to generate “historic tax revenue” for the city. “We see all of Times Square becoming the resort, with local restaurants, hotels and Broadway theaters all directly benefitting," the spokesperson said.
The Avenir, from developer Larry Silverstein, projects US$2.5 billion in gambling revenue in its first full year. “Locating a destination casino in Manhattan will generate the most revenue for the state, according to New York’s own independent study,” the Avenir executive summary said. “It is not in the economic interest of Manhattan to force its tourists to travel to other boroughs to enjoy gaming and its amenities.”
A study by consultants Spectrum Gaming Group projected nearly US$2.1 billion in gambling revenue for a hypothetical Manhattan-based casino, with ones in the outskirts generating far less.
MGM Resorts International, which operates a slot-machine-only facility in Yonkers, and Genting Group’s Resorts World, which has a similar property next to the Aqueduct racetrack in Queens, said their gambling revenue would more than double if they’re allowed to add table games like blackjack and sports betting. MGM projected casino revenue of as much as US$1.39 billion annually, while Resorts World said its casino revenue would jump to US$2.2 billion a year by 2027.
Projections from eager developers can sometimes get ahead of reality. The first four casinos to open in upstate New York fell short of initial projections, as did a temporary casino Bally’s Corp opened in Chicago in 2023, ahead of a bigger resort it’s building there.
Bally’s, which is proposing a casino at a company-owned golf course in the Bronx, is projecting US$1 billion a year in gambling revenue when it opens. It said the resort would generate US$200 million annually in gaming-related taxes.
As part of the New York bidding process, candidates will suggest their own tax rates for their casino revenue, a process designed to maximise the state’s take. That last step hasn’t happened yet.
Two of the New York bidders said they were using the minimum 10% tax rate on table games, and 25% rate on slot machines required by the state to estimate their proposed tax contributions. Others didn’t specify tax rates.

title: Genting Malaysia Berhad - Restructuring of Loss-Making Unit
author: PublicInvest
body:
Genting Malaysia (GENM) announced the restructuring of its loss-making unit, Empire Resorts Inc (Empire), which recently became a wholly-owned subsidiary following the completion of a related party transaction. Empire has proposed to sell and leaseback its non-gaming assets as well as acquire a parcel of land with the proceeds to be raised from the proposed disposal. In addition, it will redeem USD300m bond that would result in Empire becoming debt-free. While this restructuring appears to be positive as it would reduce Empire's operating costs and help address its earnings pressure, details of the various agreements (lease and management agreements of the non-gaming assets) have yet to be finalised at this juncture. However, given the recent decline in GENM's share price and the potential benefit of this proposed restructuring, we upgrade our rating to Neutral .
Details of the restructuring. Empire, a wholly-owned subsidiary of GENM, announced the proposed disposal of its non-gaming assets comprising two hotels, 18-hole golf course, entertainment centre and multiple restaurants to Sullivan County Resort Facilities Local Development Corporation (Sullivan) for a cash consideration of USD525m. Proceeds from this disposal will be used to purchase land measuring 1,554.6 acres from EPR Properties (EPR) for USD201.3m cash and to redeem USD300m of Empire's bond. Meanwhile, Empire will lease these non-gaming assets through 2066 that will be managed by Sullivan under a 20-year agreement with automatic renewal for two successive 5-year period. Note that Empire is the owner and operator of Resorts World Catskills in New York.
Preliminary benefits . The proceeds from the proposed disposal will allow Empire to fully redeem its bond, resulting in Empire being debt-free and therefore, focus on improving its operations that have been suffering from high operating costs and low business volume due to competition and muted consumer sentiment. Currently, Empire is paying lease rental to EPR but the proposed acquisition of the land would lead to the elimination of these lease payments. Empire will own the land which will be unencumbered by debt. Resorts World Catskills' gaming and non-gaming assets sit on this land (420 acres) but there is vacant land measuring 1,134.6 acres that has yet to be developed.
Our view . We note that this restructuring appears to benefit Empire as it helps to enhance its cost structure and alleviate pressure on earnings. However, details of its future lease and management agreements with Sullivan remain unavailable and will be announced in due course. For now, we maintain our FY25-27F earnings forecasts on GENM, which we had earlier cut by 10-16% to reflect higher share of losses from Empire. Given the sharp decline in its share price while this restructuring is likely to improve its cost structure in the future, we remove the 10% discount ascribed to our SOTP valuation. Our TP is revised to RM1.84 . Upgrade GENM to Neutral .
Source: PublicInvest Research - 18 Aug 2025

title: Genting Malaysia Berhad - Disposals of Non-Gaming Assets in RWC
author: sectoranalyst
body:
Announcement
Genting Malaysia (GENM) announced that it is undertaking the proposals below:
Selling its non-gaming assets comprising the 332-room Resorts World Catskills (RWC) hotel, 99-room Alder Hotel, 18-hole Monster Golf Course, 2,500-seat RWC Epicenter and multiple restaurants, to Sullivan County Resort Facilities Local Development Corporation (SCRFLDC) for a cash consideration of US$525mn;

Entering into a 20-year management agreement (with automatic renewal for 2 successive 5-year period) with SCRFLDC to manage all the non-gaming assets.
Our takes
We are positive on this US$525mn (RM2.2bn) sale and leaseback proposals. We also like the use of disposal proceeds to redeem the US$300mn notes, which are listed on the Singapore Stock Exchange, as it will provide an annual saving of US$2.3mn/year. According to announcement, the acquisition of land will allow the company to control over the land on which RWC gaming and non-gaming assets are built (420 acres), in addition to 1,134.6 acres of vacant land which have development potential.
No change to our FY25-27 earnings estimates as we believe savings from coupon payments and building depreciation cost will be offset by depreciation and finance costs related to right-of-use assets.
Valuation
We maintain GENM’s DCF valuation at RM2.24/share with unchanged CAPM of 19.3%. Maintain Buy

title: Bond Issue to Fund Purchase of Genting’s Casino in Upstate New York Delayed, Bloomberg Reports
author: edgeinvest
body:
(Aug 26): A high-yield municipal bond transaction that would fund the purchase of businesses related to a casino in upstate New York has been delayed, people familiar with the matter said.
The unrated deal, managed by KeyBanc Capital Markets, was expected to price on Aug 27, according to investor roadshow documents. The transaction has been postponed for the hiring of legal counsel to advise investors in the transaction, said the people, who were not authorised to speak publicly because the matter is private. The move is known in the market as the hiring of purchaser’s counsel.
Proceeds of the sale are expected to fund the purchase of the non-gaming businesses at Genting Group’s Resorts World Catskills in Sullivan County, New York. The bonds are issued by the Sullivan County Resort Facilities Local Development Corp, a not-for-profit organisation created under New York’s economic-development law.
The deal is now listed as day-to-day status, according to data compiled by Bloomberg . Representatives for KeyBanc and the development corporation declined to comment.
With the funds from the sale, the hospitality company plans to purchase the land the resort sits on — which it currently rents from a real estate investment trust, pay off a balloon payment on outstanding debt due in 2026, and enter into a long-term management agreement, according to a spokesperson for the resort.
A spokesperson for the company declined to comment on the delay.

title: Genting Malaysia Berhad - Higher Gaming Profit & Forex Gains
author: PublicInvest
body:
Genting Malaysia (GENM) posted a strong rebound in 2QFY25, chalking a net profit of RM416.7m compared to RM82.2m in 2QFY24. This was due to higher gaming revenue in Malaysia and the UK as well as the recognition of RM184.6m forex gains. Stripping out exceptional items, 2QFY25 core net profit was higher at RM186.5m, +128% YoY. However, cumulative 1HFY25 results still coming in below expectations, accounting for 40% of our and consensus full-year estimates. We maintain our earnings forecasts for now as the proposed disposal of Empire Resorts' non-gaming assets (expected to complete this year) should help to improve profitability due to lower interest and rental costs. We retain our Neutral call on GENM. No dividend was declared for the quarter.
2QFY25 revenue increased by 9.3% YoY, primarily due to stronger contribution from Malaysia and the UK. Revenue from Malaysia rose 10% YoY on the back of higher business volume from the gaming segment while the UK (+9% YoY) was lifted by contribution from newly acquired Stratford casino. However, the US also posted higher revenue (+9% YoY) due to consolidation of Empire Resorts.
2QFY25 net profit jumped over 400% YoY, due to higher gaming revenue as well as the recognition of RM184.6m foreign exchange translation gains on its USD denominated borrowings. However, higher profit posted by the Malaysian and the UK operations were partly offset by the consolidation of Empire Resorts and higher operating expenses in the US.
Outlook . Following the announcement of the proposed disposal of Empire Resorts' non-gaming assets, cost structure is expected to improve as Empire Resorts no longer required to make interest payments on borrowings and lease payments for the land. In addition, it would receive recurring payments for the management of the non-gaming assets and the land that it proposed to acquire. Nevertheless, it was recently reported that a municipal bond offering by the purchaser of the non-gaming assets, Sullivan County Resort Facilities Local Development Corp, has been delayed. Proceeds from the proposed bond was expected to be used to fund the acquisition of these assets. Meanwhile, in the near-term, we believe the operating environment in the US market will continue to be challenging given the weak economic outlook with the possibility of a recession that could affect consumer sentiment and spending on entertainment activities.
Source: PublicInvest Research - 29 Aug 2025

title: Genting Berhad - Weaker Contribution From The US
author: PublicInvest
body:
Genting Bhd (GENT) posted a flattish headline net profit of RM243.6m for 2QFY25. Excluding gains on forex translation from USD borrowings, asset disposal and other non-operating items, core net profit came in at only RM94m. For 1HFY25, results were below expectations, constituting 27% and 30% of our and consensus full-year estimates, respectively. We attribute the shortfall to lower-than-expected contribution from the US operations. We believe sentiments in the leisure and entertainment industry will remain lacklustre given the uncertain macroeconomic conditions in the US. We cut our FY25-27F earnings forecasts by an average of 28% due to a downward revision in leisure & hospitality profit. Our SOTP-based TP is revised to RM3.30 . We maintain Neutral on GENT as we reckon that earnings visibility remains weak at this juncture.
2QFY25 revenue fell by 1.1% YoY. Contribution from major segments were lower such as Singapore and the US & Bahamas' leisure & hospitality. Despite a strong 10% growth from Malaysia, the decline in Singapore (-2% YoY) and the US & Bahamas (-13% YoY) dragged group's revenue down by 1.1% YoY. This was due to lower forex translation, following the strengthening of the ringgit against SGD and USD, couple with lower visitation at Resorts World Las Vegas. Plantation also posted weaker revenue due to lower downstream contribution.
2QFY25 core net profit at only RM94.1m, compared to RM446m in 2QFY24. Resorts World Sentosa posted a 6% decline in adjusted EBITDA, reflecting the impact of higher costs and temporary closure of SEA Aquarium while the US & Bahamas was down 52% YoY due to higher operating and payroll related expenses.
Maintain Neutral. While GENT 's valuation looks compelling at <10x forward PER, we see potential downside risk to its earnings, as the slowdown in economic activities is likely to affect the hospitality and entertainment industry globally. Additionally, cost could continue to rise, particularly salary, administrative and tax costs. We do not expect Singapore and the US operations to deliver positive earnings growth this year given the challenging operating environment with the possibility of the US slipping into recession. However, we note that the likelihood of GENM winning a full casino license in New York could be a near-term share price catalyst for GENT .

title: Genting Berhad - Dragged by GENS and RWLV
author: sectoranalyst
body:
Review
Excluding a disposal gain of RM338mn and other exceptional items, Genting Berhad’s (Genting) 1H25 core profit of RM83.4mn came in below market expectation. The earnings miss was largely due to lower-thanexpected contribution from gaming operations in Singapore and Las Vegas, and higher-than-expected tax expense. No dividend was declared for 2Q25.
Genting’s 1H25 adjusted EBITDA slumped 14.8% YoY to RM4.1bn on the back of 7.0% YoY drop in revenue to RM13.3bn. The disappointment was driven by lacklustre performance of Genting Singapore (GENS) and Resorts World Las Vegas (RWLV), and higher payroll cost in its US and UK operations, partially mitigated by recovery in Malaysia operations.
GENS’ 1H25 adj. EBITDA declined 25.8% YoY to S$423.7mn with revenue dropping 10.8% to S$1.2bn. The decline was due to a high-base effect as 1Q24 earnings were spurred by high VIP volume and margin expansion. For 2Q25, the gaming revenue expanded by 5.3% YoY to S$401.9mn, supported by higher VIP rolling volume and win rate. However, the adj. EBITDA margin declined 6.6% to S$187.9mn due to higher operating costs and the temporary closure of S.E.A. Aquarium.
GENM’s 1H25 adjusted EBITDA expanded by 24% YoY to RM1.8bn despite a moderate 1.5% growth in revenue. This was mainly driven by the strong recovery in Malaysia operations as well as forex gain, which more than offset higher payroll cost in US and UK operations. Excluding the gain, 1H25 adjusted EBITDA would have declined by 1% YoY to RM1.5bn (see GENM report).
Resorts World Las Vegas’s (RWLV) 1HFY25 revenue and adjusted EBITDA declined by 25.6% and 69.4% YoY to RM1.5bn and RM129.2mn respectively. The dismay performance was due to lower business volume and higher payroll costs.
Impact
We cut GENT’s FY25-27 earnings projections by 35.6-65.1% after revising GENS and RWLV’s earnings lower. We also trim FY25/26/27 dividend projections to 6/10/14sen/share from 16/18/19sen/share previously.
Outlook
We look forward to major events to drive GENT’s earnings higher in 2H25. Specifically, the Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix in November and the reopening and rebranding of Singapore Oceanarium in July-25 are expected to boost RWLV and GENS’ 2H25 earnings respectively.
Valuation
Following the earnings revisions, we reduce GENT’s SOP valuation to RM3.39/share (from RM3.56). However, we maintain our Buy recommendation on the stock as we believe the sell down is overdone.
Source: TA Research - 29 Aug 2025

title: Genting Malaysia Berhad - Recovery in Sight
author: sectoranalyst
body:
Review
Excluding a forex gain of RM253.5mn, Genting Malaysia’s (GENM) 1H25 core profit of RM284.3mn accounted for 66% of our full-year forecast and 57% of consensus estimates. However, we consider this as within expectations as costs of operation are expected to rise in 2H25. No dividend was declared for 1H25.
1H25 adjusted EBITDA expanded by 24% YoY to RM1.8bn despite a moderate 1.5% growth in revenue. This was mainly driven by a strong recovery in Malaysia operations as well as forex gain, which more than offset higher payroll cost in US and UK operations. Excluding the gain, 1H25 adjusted EBITDA would have declined by 1% YoY to RM1.5bn.
On QoQ basis, the 2Q25 core profit surged more than 5-fold to RM237.4mn underpinned by a 12.5% growth in revenue. The decent performance was due to a low-base effect as 1Q25 was affected by low VIP volume and high effective tax rate.
Impact
We maintain our FY25-27 earnings projections. However, we cut FY25/26/27 dividend projections to 8/10/12sen/share from 12/14/16sen/share previously.
Conference call highlights
Resorts World Genting stage a strong recovery in 2Q25 with higher gross gaming revenue (GGR) from VIP and non-VIP, which surged 8% and 21% respectively. Coupled with higher hold percentage, the EBITDA for Malaysia operations surged 15% YoY RM606.3mn. However, management guided that FY25 EBITDA margin would likely hover at 30% versus 33% in 1H25 owing to SST impact, rise in electricity costs and higher marketing expenses in 2H25.
In view of the cost pressures in 2H25 and future capex, management exercised prudent capital management and held back the usual interim dividend for 2Q25.
With regards to the recent disposals of Resorts World Catskills’ nongaming assets, the delay in the fund-raising by the purchaser would not be a major setback and management expects to complete the disposal this year.
For the new casino licence in downstate New York, the group has submitted the bid in June and has also launched public engagement for some feedback. According to management, the response to first engagement was well-received and the second engagement will be held in Sep-25. The winners of up to 3 will be announced on Dec 1 and the award of casino licence will take place before the end of the year.

title: Genting Malaysia (GENM MK) - Earnings beat expectations
author: PhillipCapital
body:
2Q25 core net profit of RM244m was above expectations
Earnings in 2H25 are expected to moderate against 2Q25 levels

We continue like GENM as one of the main beneficiaries of Visit Malaysia 2026 and see potential upside if GENM secures the downstate NYC casino license, expected to be awarded by end25.
