title: Genting's 2Q Profit Edges Up 1.6% to RM244 Mil on Asset Disposals, Turnaround in JVs
author: edgeinvest
body:
KUALA LUMPUR (Aug 28): Genting Bhd (KL:GENTING) reported a slight 1.6% increase in its second-quarter net profit, rising to RM243.55 million from RM239.66 million a year earlier, driven by asset disposal proceeds, a turnaround at its joint ventures and associates, and lower depreciation.
These were partially offset by weaker adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation or Ebitda, and higher impairment charges, its latest quarterly results filing showed.
Quarterly revenue slipped 1.1% to RM6.784 billion from RM6.859 billion, impacted by foreign currency translation losses due to the ringgit’s appreciation on foreign operations. No dividend was declared, as the group said it plans to continue to focus on debt reduction and future growth.
Segment-wise, Resorts World Sentosa (RWS) posted lower revenue and Ebitda in ringgit terms, though local currency revenue rose 3% on stronger VIP rolling volume and increased visitation to Universal Studios Singapore following the launch of Minion Land. Ebitda declined due to higher costs and the temporary closure of S.E.A. Aquarium for upgrades.
Resorts World Las Vegas (RWLV) also saw softer revenue and Ebitda, affected by macroeconomic headwinds and lower visits. Hotel occupancy fell to 80.2% from 89.4%, while average daily rate for the rooms rose slightly to US$265 (RM1,121) from US$257 a year ago.
Elsewhere in the hospitality segment, Ebitda rose 16% in Malaysia to RM581.5 million, increased 8% in the UK and Egypt, but declined 33% in the US and Bahamas due to higher operating costs and currency effects.
Its oil palm plantation business, meanwhile, recorded higher revenue and Ebitda, supported by stronger palm kernel prices and increased production. In contrast, the downstream manufacturing segment posted losses due to weaker sales and margin compression.
The power division delivered improved revenue and Ebitda, driven by higher output from Indonesia’s Banten Plant, while the oil and gas division saw declines, reflecting lower global crude prices and US dollar weakness.
For the first half of FY2025, Genting recorded a sharp 70.1% fall in net profit to RM248.12 million from RM828.52 million, while revenue dropped 7% to RM13.292 billion from RM14.291 billion.
On outlook, Genting said its RWS 2.0 redevelopment is progressing, with phased closures and construction expected to impact operations. Upon full completion by 2030, RWS will offer expanded attractions and refreshed hospitality aimed at experience-driven travellers and families, it said.
In Las Vegas, RWLV is anticipating a post-summer recovery in visitor volume, supported by a strong events calendar. VIP play and table volumes are improving, aided by upgraded hotel and casino systems that enhance customer targeting and margin performance.
For its other business segments, outlook appears mixed.
The plantation division expects palm product prices to remain stable and production to improve in the coming months, while its property development segment is launching new projects in Johor.
The downstream manufacturing segment, however, is likely to remain under pressure given the ongoing competition from its Indonesian counterparts, overcapacity of refineries in Indonesia, and rising input costs. The power and oil and gas divisions are also making strategic moves to shift away from further investments in coal-fired projects, with a new gas processing plant.
Genting shares closed unchanged at RM2.84 on Thursday, valuing the group at RM11 billion.
Source: TheEdge - 29 Aug 2025

title: Genting Malaysia’s 2Q Profit Jumps Fivefold as Quarterly Revenue Hits Record High
author: edgeinvest
body:
KUALA LUMPUR (Aug 28): Genting Malaysia Bhd (KL:GENM) reported a surge in net profit to RM416.75 million for the second quarter ended June 30, 2025 (2QFY2025), up from RM82.24 million a year earlier.
The fivefold profit increase was mainly due to RM184.6 million in foreign exchange gains from a stronger ringgit against the US dollar, as most of Genting Malaysia’s debts are in foreign currencies. An improved performance of the Malaysian operations also helped.
Quarterly revenue rose 9.3% year-on-year to a record quarterly high of RM2.918 billion, from RM2.669 billion a year earlier, a bourse filing showed on Thursday.
Excluding forex gains, the group’s earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda) grew 13% to RM845.0 million, supported by:
A 16% increase in the Malaysian operations' Ebitda to RM581.5 million, driven by higher business volume and improved margins (34% versus 32%).
An 8% rise in the UK and Egyptian operations’ Ebitda, aided by contributions from the newly acquired Genting Casino Stratford, though partially offset by currency effects and higher operating costs.
These gains were partly offset by a 33% drop in Ebitda from the US and Bahamas, caused by higher costs at Resorts World New York City, currency effects, and losses from businesses including Genting Empire Resorts LLC in the group’s accounts.
No dividend was declared for the latest quarter.
For the first half of FY2025, net profit more than tripled to RM489.33 million, while revenue edged up 1.5% to RM5.513 billion.
Genting Malaysia, which is cautious on short-term prospects, remains optimistic about long-term growth in the leisure and hospitality sector. It said the focus for operations in Malaysia will be to increase visitors and business at Resorts World Genting through marketing and new ecotourism attractions.
For its UK operations, it is looking at growth coming from recent changes in gaming machine rules which allow for more machines in casinos. Integration of Genting Casino Stratford is also complete, with more expansion opportunities being considered, Genting Malaysia said.
For the US, its focus is on its bid to turn Resorts World New York City into a US$5.5 billion (RM23.2 billion) integrated resort and the restructuring plan for Empire Resorts.
As for its Bahamas operations, Genting Malaysia is looking to expand cruise partnerships to boost visits to Resorts World Bimini while keeping costs in check and improving efficiency.
Genting Malaysia shares were unchanged at RM1.98 at Thursday’s close, valuing the group at RM11.76 billion. Year to date, the stock has declined 12.4%.
Source: TheEdge - 29 Aug 2025

title: Genting Berhad (GENT MK) - Missing expectations
author: PhillipCapital
body:
6M25 results were below expectations
We lower 2025-27E earnings by 18-20% to factor in weaker gaming and leisure EBITDA margin
Maintain BUY with lower SOP-derived target price of RM3.80
Below expectations, dragged RWS and RWLV
6M25 recorded revenue of RM13.2bn (-7% YoY) and core profit of RM188.7m (-78.6% YoY). The results were below expectations, accounting for 26% and 19% of our and the street's full-year forecasts. The shortfall was primarily due to lower revenue contribution from RWS in the absence of 2024 visa-driven demand and lower visitation for RWLV. The EBITDA margin declined by 5.9 ppts to 27.6%, primarily due to weaker property and plantation margins. No dividend was announced in 2Q25 (2Q24: 6sen) as the company plans to reserve cash for debt settlement.
Key updates
Gaming revenue grew by 4% in 2Q25 as Resorts World Genting continued to experience strong visitation, with an increase in hotel guests from Indonesia, India, and China. 2Q25 EBITDA margin declined by 6ppts to 24.8% (1Q25: 30.6%) affected by rising cost pressure. Looking ahead, the overall gaming business is expected to continue facing margin compression, mainly due to higher operating and payroll-related expenses. In the briefing, management provided an update for the New York casino, which is currently in the process of furnishing documents requested by the regulator. As part of the requirement, Genting has recently presented a proposal to the Community Advisory Committee, and the result of the casino license is expected to be announced by Dec25. In addition, RWLV has made significant progress in its recovery since Jul25, supported by higher tourist arrivals and an expected improvement in hotel occupancy for 2H25.
Maintain BUY with a lower TP of RM3.80
We cut our 2025-27E earnings estimates by 18-20% after factoring in a weaker EBITDA margin for the gaming and leisure segment, partially offset by an improved GENM outlook. We maintain our BUY rating with a lower SOP-derived TP of RM3.80. The key earnings growth driver remains its gaming and leisure operations, with a potential catalyst from the successful commercialization and listing of TauRx. title: Sluggish Ops Weigh on Genting, Watch Out for New York Licence Bid, S&P Flags
author: edgeinvest
body:
KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 10): Genting Bhd’s (KL:GENTING) sluggish operations are narrowing its rating buffer, while its bid for New York gaming license is an event risk for the conglomerate, S&P Global Ratings flagged.
The ratio of funds from operations to debt is expected to be 22%-24% through 2026 from 23.5% in 2024, following weaker-than-expected first half dragged by its Singapore and Las Vegas operations, the ratings agency said in a report on Wednesday.
“Key to the resort and casino operator’s credit quality will be operational recovery at its Singapore and Las Vegas assets, along with the pace and level of investments,” S&P said. “We expect a gradual pickup in earnings from 2026.”
Genting’s operating profit in Singapore declined amid higher costs from ongoing brownfield construction, and the temporary closure of SEA Aquarium in May and June this year to facilitate the opening of the Singapore Oceanarium.
In Las Vegas, Genting was affected by lower visitor volume that dragged on its hotels and gaming revenue amid macroeconomic uncertainty.
Genting has submitted a formal bid for a casino licence in New York, as part of a US$5.5 billion (RM23.16 billion) resort development in Queens. A decision is expected by Dec 1, a key outcome for Genting, S&P noted.
“If awarded, the level of investment and incremental earnings from the new licence will be the main rating considerations, and we believe Genting will continue with similar financial policy settings,” the ratings agency said.
In contrast, the agency warned that a failed bid could weigh on the competitiveness of Genting’s US operations, though it would remove the overhang of the cost of investing in new business.
“Our base-case assumptions do not reflect investments or incremental earnings related to the group bidding for the New York gaming licence, as we view it as an event risk,” S&P added.
Source: TheEdge - 11 Sep 2025

title: Genting Malaysia's US Unit to Contest Amended US$600 Mil Lawsuit Filed by Business Partner
author: edgeinvest
body:
KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 17): Genting Malaysia Bhd (KL:GENM) said on Wednesday that its business partner RAV Bahamas Ltd has filed an amended complaint in a US court in Florida.
The amended complaint, lodged on July 29, names Genting Malaysia’s indirect wholly owned subsidiary Genting Americas Inc (GAI) and repeats earlier allegations without introducing new material facts.
“GAI maintains that the amended complaint is baseless and without merit and will continue to vigorously defend against these claims,” Genting Malaysia said in a filing with Bursa Malaysia.
GAI — an affiliate of BB Entertainment Ltd, the owner and operator of Resorts World Bimini in the Bahamas — was first named in a complaint by RAV in October 2024. BB Entertainment is 78%-owned indirectly by Genting Malaysia, with RAV holding the remaining 22%.
RAV alleges that GAI saddled Resorts World Bimini with nearly US$1 billion in debt, turning it into a “financial wasteland”, according to Bahamian news portal The Tribune . It is seeking more than US$600 million (RM2.57 billion) in damages.
The US District Court, Southern District of Florida, had previously dismissed RAV’s initial lawsuit in July but allowed it to be refiled. At the time, the court agreed with Genting’s position that the original claim was “merely a shareholders’ dispute”.
Shares of Genting Malaysia ended three sen or 1.4% higher at RM2.17 on Wednesday, valuing the group at RM12.9 billion.
Source: TheEdge - 18 Sep 2025

title: GAMING - Proposed Privatisation of GENM
author: PublicInvest
body:
Proposed Privatisation of GENM Genting Bhd ( GENT ) has announced a RM6.74bn proposed privatisation of Genting Malaysia ( GENM ). The conditional voluntary takeover offer will extend to all the remaining 2,870m ordinary shares in GENM not already owned by GENT , representing 50.64% equity interest at a cash offer of RM2.35 per GENM share. The offer implies a FY25F PBR of 1.12x and a PER of 25.5x. If the deal is fully funded with debt, GENT 's net gearing is projected to increase from 0.43x to 0.50x. Despite posting a strong topline growth, GENM 's profitability has not recovered back to the pre-pandemic levels due to a combination of factors - rising operating cost, forex losses, corporate governance issue etc. At a 9.8% premium to the last closing price, we believe the offer is likely to become unconditional as GENT is already holding 49.4% of GENM . However, a successful privatisation remains a key hurdle. The rationale stated by GENT is to gain statutory control of GENM and to enable the group to execute the potential downstate New York integrated resort project that requires a substantial investment of USD5.5bn. We maintain Neutral on GENT but upgrade GENM to Trading Buy given the upside to the privatisation offer and the possibility of it winning the downstate New York casino license.
The offer . Currently, GENT holds 49.36% of GENM and we believe the offer is likely to become unconditional with GENT securing >50% of total issued GENM shares (excluding treasury shares). The proposed privatisation would cost RM6.74bn with GENT plans to utilise external debt financing of RM6.3bn and the remainder via internally generated funds. The offer price translates to an implied EV/EBITDA of 9.1x. Based on our FY25F forecast, the offer is valued at 1.12x PBR and 25.5x PER. It is not subject to the approval of GENT 's shareholders but requires the clearance from the Securities Commission within 4 days from the date of the notice. Given a fragmented shareholding structure of GENM , a successful privatisation (i.e gaining >90% acceptance) remains a hurdle.
Rationale . GENT intended to gain statutory control of GENM . On 30 June 2025, GENM announced that its wholly-owned subsidiary, Genting New York LLC , the owner and operator of Resorts World New York City ( RWNYC ), has submitted a bid to the New York State Gaming Commission for a commercial casino license. The bid involves a proposed development of an integrated resort in Queens with an estimated project cost of USD5.5bn. There were eight contenders at the start of the bidding process but only four survived the first round of elimination to compete for up to three casino licenses in downstate New York. Last month, RWNYC and MGM 's Empire City Casino managed to secure approval from the Community Advisory Committee. These two proposals will now progress to the New York Gaming Facility Location Board for approval. A final decision is expected to be released by 1 December 2025. Two other contenders are still awaiting review by local advisory committees namely Bally's Corp in the Bronx and Steve Cohen's City Field in Queens.
Source: PublicInvest Research - 14 Oct 2025

title: Gaming Sector - Unattractive VGO to Privatise Genting Malaysia
author: sectoranalyst
body:
Announcements
Yesterday, Genting launched a conditional voluntary take-over offer (VGO) to acquire all the remaining 2.87bn shares in Genting Malaysia (GENM), representing 50.64% equity interest in GENM for a cash offer price of RM2.35/share.
Other salient terms and conditions include:-
The offer is conditional upon Genting having received more than 50% of the total GENM’s share, excluding treasury shares;
Genting does not intend to maintain the listing status of GENM if the valid acceptance received by Genting results in GENM not meeting the public shareholding spread of 25%; and
The offer price will be adjusted for any dividend declared and distributed by GENM on or after the date of this notice but prior to the closing date.
Our Views
We view this acquisition merely a move for Genting to tighten grip on GENM and to become a statutory controlling shareholder of GENM. This will allow Genting to continue consolidating GENM’s earnings not only from Resorts World Genting Highlands, but also from Genting New York LLC (GENNY), the owner and operator of Resorts World New York City (RWNYC). Note that GENNY has submitted a bid for a commercial casino licence to elevate RWNYC into a world-class integrated resort destination with an estimated cost of USD5.5bn. The winners of casino licences are expected to be announced in Dec-25.
From GENM’s standpoint, the offer price of RM2.35, which works out to an implied acquisition EV/EBITDA of 6.4x FY26 earnings, is unattractive when benchmarked against regional peers’ average of 8.4x (Figure 2). Meanwhile, the chance of Genting revising the offer price higher is slim as there is no incentive for GENM’s board of director to seek any competing offer. As such, the current offer may not garner the necessary shareholder acceptance required to successfully privatise and delist GENM. From a strategic perspective, it is not in the best interest for Genting group, in our opinion, to delist GENM as the access to equity market is crucial for future fund-raising activities. This is particularly relevant to GENM’s plan to spend USD5.5bn to elevate RWNYC, if it wins the casino licence.
In the event of a successful takeover of 100% stake in GENM, the acquisition will cost a total RM6.7bn. Assuming the acquisition is funded via 100% debt, Genting’s net gearing will rise to 0.46x from estimated 0.34x for FY26. Its FY26 net profit will increase by 75.8% to RM981.3mn (from est. RM558.3mn).
Recommendation
All in all, we believe Genting would be able to up its stake to 50% by acquiring additional 0.64% GENM shares in the open market or receiving valid acceptance of approximately 36.3mn GENM shares, which we think is relatively easy. In fact, Genting had started acquiring 1.9mn GENM shares in the open market recently. However, we think it is challenging for Genting to obtain 25.6% stake or 1.5bn GENM shares, thus breaching the public shareholding spread requirement, in view of the unattractive offer price.
We upgrade GENM’s target price to RM2.35 (from RM2.24 previously) to be on par with the takeover offer price and reiterate our Buy recommendation on the stock. Meanwhile, we also raise Genting’s SOP valuation higher to RM3.44 (from RM3.39 previously) after factoring in the increased target price for GENM and maintain its Buy recommendation. We advise GENM’s shareholders to Reject the Offer made by Genting.
Source: TA Research - 14 Oct 2025

title: Genting Malaysia (GENM MK) - Conditional voluntary take-over offer at RM2.35
author: PhillipCapital
body:
Tan Sri Lim Kok Thay and his PAC extend a conditional voluntary takeover offer to acquire all GENM's remaining shares at a cash offer of RM2.35
We advise investors to accept the takeover offer, which provides an opportunity to exit the stock given GENM's continued earnings headwinds and challenging operating environment
Maintain HOLD rating with higher TP of RM2.35
The share transactions and the conditional voluntary take-over offer
On 10 Oct 25, Tan Sri Lim Kok Thay (Deputy Chairman and Executive Director), through GENT acquired an additional 185,500 units at RM2.14 per share (total RM396.5k). This acquisition raised the collective shareholding of Tan Sri Lim and his persons acting in concert (PAC) to 49.4%, thereby triggering the obligation for Tan Sri Lim and GENT to extend a conditional voluntary takeover offer for all remaining GENM shares at a cash offer price of RM2.35.
Offer acceptance
The offer price of RM2.35 represents a premium of 11.5% to GENM's 5-day volume weighted average price (VWAP), but implies a 17% discount to its 5-year historical average EV/EBITDA multiple of 9x. While the offer price appears less compelling from a valuation standpoint, we view it as an opportunity for investors to exit the stock, given GENM's subdued earnings outlook amid persistent cost pressures. Escalating operating and labour costs across all key markets are expected to weigh on earnings, with earnings likely to moderate in 2H25. Meanwhile, the planned US$5.5bn New York Downstate casino expansion will require significant capex funding, that could require additional borrowings. With GENM's gearing level at 0.7x, further debt may heighten interest expenses, further limiting balance sheet flexibility, and potentially constrain dividend payouts. Our back-of-the-envelope estimates suggest that securing the New York Downstate casino licence could lift GENM's 2026E EBITDA by RM240-310m, adding roughly RM0.20-0.25/share to valuation. We believe the RM2.35 offer price has partially priced in the potential upside from the proposed New York project.
Maintain HOLD with a higher target price at the RM2.35
We maintain a HOLD rating and increase our TP to RM2.35 (from RM2.10) to match the offer price. While the offer provides an exit opportunity, we believe some investors may choose not to accept it, given their higher entry cost. The offer is voluntary upon Tan Sri Lim being the offeror receiving acceptances that would result in the offeror and PACs holding in aggregate >50% share in GENM.
Key downside risks include lower traffic footfall to RWG, potential gaming tax hikes, and drag from key associates' contributions.
Source: Phillip Capital Research - 14 Oct 2025

title: Genting to Privatise Genting Malaysia in RM2.35-per-share Buyout
author: edgeinvest
body:
KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 13): Genting Bhd (KL:GENTING) plans to buy out and delist its unit Genting Malaysia Bhd (KL:GENM) in a deal worth RM6.7 billion.
The offer to minority shareholders is equivalent to RM2.35 per share, according to the takeover notice posted to Bursa Malaysia on Monday. The price tag is a premium of nearly 10% to Genting Malaysia's last price of RM2.14 last Friday before trading of the stock was suspended for the announcement.
There is no share-swap offer for the privatisation deal.
The offer is conditional upon Genting receiving enough acceptance to raise its shareholding above 50% of the voting shares in Genting Malaysia.
Currently, Genting holds a 49.36% stake in Genting Malaysia.
The privatisation, if successful, would mark the exit of a company listed on the Malaysian stock exchange nearly four decades ago.
The acquisition would be the largest since the takeover of Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd worth over RM12 billion and completed earlier this year, according to data from Dealogic.
The buyout comes at a time when Genting Malaysia is bidding for a casino licence in New York as part of a US$5.5 billion (RM23.19 billion) resort development in Queens. A decision is expected by Dec 1, followed by the issuance of licences by Dec 31.
Shares of Genting Malaysia, meanwhile, have largely remained below pre-Covid levels partly dragged by related-party transaction concerns after the company took over the loss-making Empire Resorts owned by the founding family of the Genting group.
Both Genting and Genting Malaysia have also been kicked out of the FBM KLCI, the country’s benchmark equity index.
The takeover could face resistance and hold-out from shareholders, UOB Kay Hian analyst Jack Goh told The Edge . The offer price of RM2.35 per share is “unattractive”, coming in below average valuations and about 20% below the stock’s peak last year, he flagged.
Goh also noted that the offer price also does not take into account the potential earnings upside from the downstate New York casino licence and the large free float of Genting Malaysia shares that makes the stock highly liquid.
While off lows, Genting Malaysia is still down over 5% year to date while a large majority of research houses have been cautious of the stock’s outlook.
There are now 11 ‘hold’, four ‘sell’, and only three ‘buy’ calls on the stock. The average target price is RM2.06, according to Bloomberg , which implies a potential decline of about 4% in the next 12 months from the current share price.
Both Genting and Genting Malaysia will resume trading on Tuesday morning.
Genting Malaysia, listed on Bursa since 1989, holds the group’s flagship Resort World Genting that draws tens of millions of visitors to the hilltop facilities annually.
The company also operates the group’s major US and UK operations and a small casino in Egypt.
Source: TheEdge - 14 Oct 2025

title: Genting Malaysia Takeover Splits Analysts Amid Valuation Debate, New York Casino Bid
author: edgeinvest
body:
KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 14): Genting Bhd’s (KL:GENTING) conditional voluntary takeover offer (VTO) bid to acquire the remaining 2.87 billion shares or 50.64% stake in Genting Malaysia Bhd (KL:GENM) drew mixed reactions as analysts’ views split between valuation concerns and strategic upside.
Maybank Investment Bank Bhd (Maybank IB) in a note on Tuesday (Oct 14) argued that the RM2.35 offer price undervalues GENM, failing to reflect several key catalysts that could materially lift its fair value (FV).
“First is the revaluation of its Miami land, acquired in 2011 [at a cost] of US$442 million ... GENM had attempted to sell it at a market value of US$1.2 billion in 2023. If the land is revalued, it will add 55 sen to our fair value,” said Maybank IB in the note.
The second catalyst is the potential sale of Empire Resorts’ non-gaming assets to the Sullivan County Resort Facilities Local Development Corporation, which could add 30 sen to its fair value.
The third is the potential award of a downstate commercial casino licence in New York, which could boost value by 48 sen per share after a 10% discount, with results expected by Dec 1, 2025.
TA Securities shared the negative stance, advising shareholders to reject the offer, noting that it is "not in the best interest of the Genting group” to delist GENM given its future fundraising needs.
“This is particularly relevant to GENM's plan to spend US$5.5 billion to elevate RWNYC if it wins the New York casino licence,” said TA Securities in its separate note.
While Genting could easily raise its stake to 50% through open-market purchases, TA Securities noted that achieving the 75% threshold required for privatisation could prove difficult, given the unattractive offer price.
The research house estimated the offer price implies an undemanding EV/EBITDA multiple of 6.4 times FY2026 earnings, compared to regional peers’ average of 8.4 times.
“The chance of Genting revising the offer price higher is slim, as there is no incentive for GENM's board of directors to seek any competing offer,” the firm added.
Shares of GENM surged over 10% to RM2.36 in early trading on Tuesday, before easing to end the day at RM2.32, still up 8.4%. This values the company at RM13.15 billion.
Meanwhile, Genting rose nearly 6% to RM3.06 at the opening, before closing 5.24% up at RM3.01, giving the company a market capitalisation of RM11.59 billion.
Earlier this year, both stocks were excluded from the FBM KLCI benchmark index and have struggled to regain pre-pandemic valuations, partly due to investor concerns over related-party transactions, including GENM's acquisition of the loss-making Empire Resorts from Genting’s founding family.
CGS International and HLIB favour acceptance
Conversely, CGS International and Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB) advised shareholders to accept the offer, citing the premium to target prices (TPs) and a timely exit opportunity.
CGS International said the offer provides “a good opportunity to exit” as it is above its target price of RM1.88 and the group could face higher operating and capital costs at RWNYC if it secures the New York licence.
“We think Genting’s management believes Genting Malaysia’s [value] is higher than what the market is willing to ascribe ... and would rather privatise it now. We reckon there is also a possibility that Genting could relist GENM in the future after possibly restructuring it and when there is more positivity towards its earnings outlook,” CGS said in its notes.
However, it also cautioned that the privatisation may fail, as many shareholders are sitting on paper losses, with the offer price below its RM2.50–RM3.00 trading range between 2022 and 2024 and offering less than a 10% premium to the recent market price.
HLIB, in its brief note, also advised acceptance, saying: “We advise existing shareholders to accept the offer is higher than our previous SOP-derived TP of RM2.06 — representing a 14.1% premium.”
The offer — launched on Tuesday — values GENM at approximately RM13.6 billion and would enable Genting to fully consolidate earnings from its flagship Resorts World Genting Highlands and the Resorts World New York City (RWNYC) operations owned by Genting New York LLC (GENNY).
Genting said it does not intend to maintain GENM's listing status should the acceptance level cause the group to fall below the 25% public shareholding spread.
Source: TheEdge - 15 Oct 2025

title: MGM's Withdrawal From NY Casino Project leaves Genting, Two Other bidders in the Race
author: edgeinvest
body:
MGM Resorts International said in a statement on Tuesday the newly defined competitive landscape — with four proposals clustered in a small geographic area — challenges the returns we initially anticipated from this project.
(Oct 15): MGM Resorts International pulled out of the competition to operate a casino in the New York area, leaving just three bids, including one from billionaire hedge fund manager Steve Cohen, vying for three possible licences to build gambling complexes serving the largest US city.
The Las Vegas-based resort and gambling company blamed shifting economic and competitive conditions, including a shorter-than-expected duration for its licence. “The newly defined competitive landscape — with four proposals clustered in a small geographic area — challenges the returns we initially anticipated from this project,” MGM said in a statement on Tuesday.
The number of companies in the running to operate casinos in New York has been winnowed from eight in the past few months with elected officials rejecting all Manhattan-based proposals. The remaining contenders were required to submit final bids on Tuesday indicating what they’re willing to pay in licence fees and taxes as the state nears an awarding of the licences.
MGM said its bid was based on a 30-year licence, but newly issued guidance from the state suggested only a 15-year permit would be granted. The company had proposed a US$2.3 billion (RM9.72 billion) investment at its existing facility at Yonkers Raceway. It will continue to operate a slot machine parlour there.
New York officials have proposed tying the duration of a licence to the amount of investment, with bigger outlays obtaining a permit that lasts longer. The licences will allow for table games like blackjack and roulette, as well as sports betting.
Mets owner Cohen is partnered with Hard Rock International for an US$8.1 billion entertainment complex next to Citi Field in Queens. Their proposal lists a licence fee of US$500 million and tax rates of 25% for slot machines and 10% for table games, which were the minimums required by the state.
Genting Group’s Resorts World has a US$5.5 billion resort planned next to the Aqueduct race track in Queens. The company already offers slot machines at that site, and proposed paying US$600 million for its new licence, along with tax levies of 56% on slots and 30% on table games.
Bally’s Corp has proposed a US$4 billion resort at a golf course it owns in the Bronx. Its potential tax rates were redacted from the document posted online by the state. President Donald Trump’s company, the former owner of the golf course, is to receive a US$115 million payment if Bally’s wins the licence, according to testimony made public in a civil trial involving the president.
“Bally’s is ready and willing to bet on the Bronx,” the company said in a statement.
Yonkers Mayor Mike Spano called for a probe into why MGM dropped its bid.
“This decision by MGM defies all logic and it’s nothing short of a betrayal to the people of Yonkers and Westchester County. I am calling on governor Hochul to launch an independent investigation into this process, because the reasons MGM gives for its 180-degree reversal just don’t add up.”
The bidding is the outgrowth of a 2013 voter referendum that permitted up to seven non-tribal casinos in New York. Four upstate casinos opened years ago. Three remaining licences were held for the New York City area.
Eight groups submitted proposals in June, and four were eliminated through a process that gave local and state officials a chance to vet them based on feedback from the neighbouring communities. None of the Manhattan casino proposals won approval in that stage, an outcome that some see as a disappointment.
“The largest potential revenue would have been to come from a Manhattan casino,” said Bennett Liebman, a former member of the state’s racing and wagering board. “Now you have three casinos in the outer boroughs about 10 miles apart. The chance that they attract tourists, foreign visitors, to go out the Bronx seems somewhat unlikely.”
Two other major casino operators, Las Vegas Sands Corp and Wynn Resorts Ltd, dropped out of the bidding earlier this year.
The process is now in the hands of five-member Gaming Facility Location Board, which is expected to make a final decision by Dec 1. The proposals are to be evaluated based on four criteria, with economic and business development accounting for the largest share at 70%.
New York already has among the highest gambling industry tax rates in the US, tying New Hampshire and Rhode Island with a 51% levy on online sports wagering, according to the Tax Foundation. The state generated nearly US$2.3 billion in casino tax revenue last year, second only to Pennsylvania, according to the American Gaming Association.
Uploaded by Felyx Teoh
Source: TheEdge - 16 Oct 2025

title: Moody's Places Genting on Downgrade Watch Over Debt-funded Acquisition of Genting Malaysia
author: edgeinvest
body:
KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 16): Moody’s Ratings has placed Genting Bhd’s (KL:GENTING) Baa2 issuer rating on review for downgrade, following its planned RM6.3 billion debt-funded acquisition of the remaining 50.6% stake it doesn't own in Genting Malaysia Bhd (KL:GENM).
The trigger was Genting's conditional voluntary offer to buy the remaining Genting Malaysia shares for RM2.35 apiece, in cash. If fully accepted, the deal would cost Genting RM6.3 billion, and be primarily funded by new borrowings.
"The review for downgrade reflects our expectation that GENB's credit quality will weaken materially, depending on the level of acceptance of its proposed takeover offer for GENM, which will be largely debt-funded," said Moody's Ratings analyst Anthony Prayugo.
Moody's already considers Genting’s credit metrics "stretched", with its adjusted debt-to-Ebitda ratio having exceeded the 4.0 times downgrade threshold for several years.
With the acquisition, this leverage ratio is projected to climb to around 5.1 times in 2025, which would delay any meaningful debt reduction.
The rating agency's projections exclude a potential US$5.5 billion (RM23.2 billion) investment related to Genting’s uncertain bid for a New York casino licence, which, if successful, could further strain the company's balance sheet.
Review details and potential for multi-notch downgrade
The review, expected to conclude within 60 to 90 days, will focus on assessing the deal's final funding structure, Genting’s deleveraging plans and its post-transaction financial policy.
Moody’s issued a clear warning: Genting’s rating could face a multi-notch downgrade if its leverage increases without a credible debt-reduction strategy.
Specifically, a trigger for further negative action would be a sustained adjusted debt/Ebitda above 4.0 times or an adjusted retained cash flow/net debt below 20%–25%.
Implications on Genting Overseas Holdings and Genting Singapore
The ratings review extends beyond the parent company, Genting, to its key subsidiaries, Genting Overseas Holdings Ltd (GOHL), which carries a Baa2 rating, and Genting Singapore Ltd (SGX:G13), which has an A3 issuer rating. All ratings were previously given a stable outlook.
GOHL : The review on GOHL mirrors that of its parent's, given their close financial and operational ties. The Baa2-backed senior unsecured rating on notes issued by GOHL Capital Ltd (a wholly-owned GOHL subsidiary) is also under review.
GOHL, which owns 53% of Genting Singapore, relies on Genting Singapore's dividend income to service interest payments and redeem its US$1.5 billion notes due in 2027. “GOHL’s credit quality is capped by Genting, which can extract cash from GOHL and redeploy it within the group,” Moody's said.
Genting Singapore : Its stronger A3 issuer rating has been placed on review due to contagion risk from its parent. But it has strong standalone metrics, including S$3.3 billion in cash and minimal debt as of June 2025. But Moody’s warned that the rating gap could narrow if Genting Singapore's independence weakens, or if cash outflows to the parent increase.
Genting Singapore is currently undertaking a major expansion of Resorts World Sentosa in Singapore at a total cost of S$6.8 billion, with annual capital spending expected to peak at about S$1 billion in 2027–2028.
Meanwhile, Genting shares closed seven sen or 2.1% higher at RM3.47 on Thursday, valuing the group at RM13.45 billion, on improved prospects over a New York gaming licence being bid by Genting Malaysia. Genting has climbed over 20% since the acquisition was announced.
In a note earlier in the day, CIMB Securities said the downstate New York casino licence is "nearly in the bag" after MGM Empire City — one of the three contenders — withdrew its application. Among 15 analysts covering Genting, nine have "buy" calls and six have "hold" calls on the stock, with an average target price of RM3.48.
Source: TheEdge - 17 Oct 2025

The privatisation, if successful, would mark the exit of a company listed on the Malaysian stock exchange nearly four decades ago.
Genting Malaysia, listed on Bursa since 1989, holds the group’s flagship Resort World Genting that draws tens of millions of visitors to the hilltop facilities annually.

title: Is Genting Malaysia’s Privatization Offer a Fair Deal? Here’s What Expects Say
author: StockTipRatings
body:
On 13 October 2025, Bursa Malaysia witnessed a major corporate announcement when Genting Berhad unveiled a proposal to acquire the remaining 2.87 billion shares (representing a 50.6% stake) in Genting Malaysia that it does not already own, at a cash offer price of RM2.35 per share. The deal is valued at approximately RM6.7 billion in total cash consideration.
Currently, Genting Berhad holds a 49.4% stake in Genting Malaysia and stated that it does not intend to maintain the latter’s listing status if the public shareholding spread falls below the required 25% threshold.
Both companies have seen their share prices decline sharply since 2017. Genting Berhad ’s share price once peaked at RM10.00 in May 2017 before sliding to RM2.76 in September 2025, while Genting Malaysia ’s share price fell from RM2.94 to RM1.46 during the same period. The prolonged downtrend has been attributed to weak earnings, continued losses from U.S. operations, lower dividends, and Genting Malaysia ’s removal from key indices, including the FBM KLCI (December 2024) and the MSCI Malaysia Index (February 2025).
The RM2.35 offer price represents a 9.8% premium to Genting Malaysia ’s last closing price of RM2.14 on 12 October, and a 22.9% premium over its 12-month volume weighted average price (VWAP).
Analysts Divided on Genting Berhad’s Bold Takeover
According to StockTipRatings.com, market professionals are divided on the fairness of Genting Berhad ’s offer. Genting Malaysia is currently covered by 9 analysts — 3 Buy, 3 Hold, 2 Sell, and 1 Non-Rated — with a consensus target price of RM2.17, about 8.3% below the offer price.
Among them, 4 analysts have publicly shared their views on the proposal. Interestingly, we are noted that 2 top-ranked analysts — Yin Shao Yang from Maybank Investment Bank and Tan Kam Meng from TA Securities share the similar stance on Genting Berhad ’s takeover offer.
Here’s Where Higher-Ranked Analysts Stand on the Offer
Note: The following content is exclusive to STR Elite Subscribers
Maybank Investment Bank analyst Yin Shao Yang upgraded Genting Malaysia to Buy from Hold and raised his target price from RM1.95 to RM2.97 , implying a 27.5% upside from its 17 October closing price of RM2.33. Yin advised shareholders to reject the offer , arguing that the RM2.35 offer price undervalues Genting Malaysia ’s latest catalysts, which could unlock substantial long-term value.
These include a potential revaluation of its Miami land (which could add RM0.55 to fair value), the sale of non-gaming assets under Empire Resorts (adding another RM0.30), and the possible award of a New York downstate casino licence (lifting value by at least RM0.48 per share). Taking these catalysts into account, Yin estimated its “blue-sky” fair value at RM3.28 — significantly above the offer price.
According to StockTipRatings.com data, Yin is ranked No.1 among 9 analysts covering Genting Malaysia , holding a 71% expert rating, with an average return of 17% and a 69% success rate across the stocks he covered over a 1-year period following his calls . His strong track record is supported by his top call on Gamuda , which delivered a 100% average return across all Buy calls since November 2023.
Meanwhile, TA Securities analyst Tan Kam Meng maintained a Buy call and raised his target price to RM2.35 from RM2.24. Tan likewise advised shareholders to reject the offer , describing it as unattractive given the EV/EBITDA multiple of only 6.4x FY26 earnings, versus regional peers’ average of 8.4x. He added that Genting Berhad has little incentive to raise the offer, while delisting Genting Malaysia would limit access to equity markets needed to fund the group’s USD5.5 billion New York casino expansion.
Tan is ranked No.4 among 9 analysts covering Genting Malaysia , holding a 50% expert rating. His best-performing stock over the past year was Westports Holdings , which gained 22% before he downgraded it in July 2025.
The Other Two Analysts Say “Accept” — Offer Seen as Attractive
In contrast, Hong Leong Investment Bank’s Chee Kok Siang (39% expert rating) and CGS International’s Lew Cheng Wei (37% expert rating) took a more favourable view of Genting Berhad ’s offer. Both analysts recommended shareholders accept the offer , seeing it as an opportunity to realise value amid limited near-term catalysts for Genting Malaysia .
Chee, who revised his target price to RM2.35 , viewed the offer as attractive, representing a 14.1% premium over his previous target price of RM2.06. Similarly, Lew noted that the offer represents a 25% premium over his target price of RM1.88 , while maintaining a Reduce call.

title: Genting Resorts World Catskills Hotel’s US$561 Mil municipal Bond Sale Delayed Over Merger
author: edgeinvest
body:
Resorts World Catskills casino in 2018. (Photo by Victor J Blue/Bloomberg)
(Oct 23): Genting Group’s plan to sell the hotel at its Resorts World Catskills casino to a government development corporation in New York’s Sullivan County has been put on hold until early January, again delaying a US$561 million (RM2.37 billion) municipal bond sale.
The transaction is being postponed because Genting Bhd (KL:GENTING) has proposed buying out investors in its Genting Malaysia Bhd (KL:GENM) subsidiary and can’t enter into other material transactions in the meantime, Walter Bogumil, chief financial officer of Resorts World US, said in a letter that was read at a meeting of the Sullivan County Resorts Facilities Local Development Corp on Monday (Oct 20).
The corporation had planned to issue municipal bonds to acquire the hotel. The bond sale had already been delayed twice to answer investor questions.

title: Genting’s Takeover Offer for GENM Turns Unconditional After Crossing 50% Threshold
author: edgeinvest
body:
KUALA LUMPUR (Nov 3): Genting Bhd (KL:GENTING) said its takeover offer for Genting Malaysia Bhd (KL:GENM) has become unconditional after the group surpassed the 50% ownership threshold on Monday (Nov 3).
According to a statement issued by Genting's principal adviser AmInvestment Bank, the group now owns 2.84 billion GENM shares — representing 50.105% of GENM’s total issued shares (excluding treasury shares) — following open market acquisitions.
Genting, which held 49.999% of GENM shares prior to the posting of the offer document, acquired an additional six million shares to cross the threshold.
The offer, announced on Oct 13, is priced at RM2.35 per share — a nearly 10% premium to GENM’s last traded price of RM2.14 on Oct 10 before the stock was suspended for the announcement.
Genting has stated that it does not intend to maintain GENM’s listing status. If successful, the privatisation would mark the exit of a company that has been listed on Bursa Malaysia for nearly four decades.
With the acceptance condition now met, the offer will remain open until Nov 24, unless extended or revised, said AmInvestment Bank.
It added that the independent advice circular is expected to be released by Nov 13.
Settlement for valid acceptances will be made within 10 days of receipt, either via direct bank transfer or by cheque, depending on the shareholder’s registration status with Bursa Depository, the principal adviser said.
Shares in Genting rose two sen or 0.6% to close at RM3.40 on Monday, valuing the group at RM13.18 billion. Genting Malaysia edged up one sen or 0.4% to RM2.34, bringing its market capitalisation to RM13.9 billion.
Source: TheEdge - 4 Nov 2025

title: Bakri MP Flags Potentially Suspicious Genting Malaysia Stock Movements; Govt Says Trading Appears Legit
author: edgeinvest
body:
KUALA LUMPUR (Nov 5): A lawmaker has raised concerns over the volatility of Genting Malaysia Bhd’s (KL:GENM) stock price this year ahead of the privatisation announcement.
Bakri Member of Parliament Tan Hong Pin noted that the stock hit a one-year high of RM2.48 on Feb 18 before a 42% drop to RM1.46 on April 9. Genting Malaysia gradually recovered to RM2.14 on Oct 10. Three days later, trading in the shares was suspended to facilitate the announcement.
“This pattern raises questions about whether there were any suspicious trading activities or use of insider information that should be investigated by the SC (Securities Commission Malaysia),” Tan said.
He said many retail investors had bought shares above RM3, with some holding them since earlier periods when the stock traded above RM6 at its historical peak, urging the Finance Ministry and SC to fairly and transparently assess the actual impact of the privatisation on public investors.
In response, Deputy Finance Minister Lim Hui Ying said the sharp movements in Genting Malaysia’s stock during the period were due to material developments within the company, as well as external factors affecting market sentiment and performance.
“For instance, between late February and early April 2025, Genting Malaysia’s share price declined significantly following the release of its fourth-quarter financial results, its weakest performance in four years,” she said.
The stock’s movements during the period were also affected by global market turmoil over a series of US trade policy flip-flops.
Lim said that the price movements indicated that investors and shareholders had sufficient information to make informed investment decisions.
“However, if any trading misconduct, including insider trading, is detected and proven, appropriate action will be taken,” she stressed.
Source: TheEdge - 6 Nov 2025

title: Genting Taps Bond Market for RM900m to Finance Genting Malaysia Acquisition
author: edgeinvest
body:
KUALA LUMPUR (Nov 10): Genting Bhd (KL:GENTING) said it has issued bonds for a nominal value of RM900 million on Monday to part-finance the acquisition of Genting Malaysia Bhd (KL:GENM) shares under the takeover offer announced last month.
The medium-term notes have a one-year tenure and carry an interest rate of one-month KLIBOR plus 1.80% per annum, said Genting in a bourse filing. The one-month KLIBOR rate stands at 3%, implying an effective annual interest rate of 4.8%.
In a separate announcement, Genting said it now holds 52.63% of Genting Malaysia shares following further open-market purchases and additional acceptances under its takeover offer.
The takeover bid became unconditional on Nov 3 after Genting crossed the 50% ownership threshold. The offer, announced on Oct 13, was priced at RM2.35 per share — representing nearly a 10% premium to Genting Malaysia’s last traded price of RM2.14 on Oct 10, before the stock was suspended for the announcement.
Analysts have raised concerns that Genting’s debt-funded acquisition could further strain its already heavy debt burden and materially weaken its credit quality. Moody’s Ratings previously noted that if the offer is fully accepted, the deal would cost Genting RM6.3 billion, financed primarily through new borrowings.
Moody’s already regards Genting’s credit metrics as “stretched”, with its adjusted debt-to-Ebitda ratio having exceeded the 4.0 times downgrade threshold for several years. Additional debt from the acquisition is projected to push this ratio to about 5.1 times in 2025, heightening leverage pressures and delaying any meaningful debt reduction.
Genting has indicated that it does not intend to maintain Genting Malaysia’s listing status. If successful, the privatisation would mark the exit of a company that has been listed on Bursa Malaysia for nearly four decades.
With the acceptance condition now met, the offer will remain open until Nov 24, unless extended or revised.
Genting shares rose six sen or 1.8% to RM3.46 on Monday, giving the group a market capitalisation of RM13.41 billion. Shares in Genting Malaysia, meanwhile, edged up one sen or 0.4% to RM2.35.
Source: TheEdge - 11 Nov 2025

title: Independent Adviser Tells Genting Malaysia Shareholders to Reject Genting’s RM2.35 a Share Offer
author: edgeinvest
body:
KUALA LUMPUR (Nov 13): The independent adviser for Genting Malaysia Bhd (KL:GENM) has recommended shareholders reject Genting Bhd’s (KL:GENTING) RM2.35 a share offer to privatise the company.
The recommendation is based on Kenanga Investment Bank Bhd’s (Kenanga IB) view that the RM2.35 per share voluntary takeover offer is “not fair”, as it is below Genting Malaysia’s sum-of-parts derived valuation, and “not reasonable”, as investors may have the opportunity to realise their investment via the open market, according to a circular filed with Bursa Malaysia on Thursday.
The RM2.35 apiece offer represents a discount of between 32.47% and 37.67% to Genting Malaysia shares' estimated value of RM3.48 and RM3.77, and a 3.69% and 19.52% discount to the shares’ one-year and two-year high market prices, Kenanga IB noted.
Meanwhile, the independent adviser said Genting Malaysia shares are relatively liquid, with a two-year average monthly trading volume of 219.21 million shares (representing 8.08% of free-float).
At 8.08% of free-float, Genting Malaysia’s two-year average monthly trading liquidity is above the FBM KLCI’s average of 7.1%.
Kenanga IB said the offer isn’t reasonable since investors could sell shares on the open market if Genting can’t acquire 90% to delist GENM, and due to Genting’s US prospects with a New York license bid submitted and Empire Resorts restructuring.
As of Nov 6, the offerors owned 52.13% of Genting Malaysia and needed another 22.87% to breach the public spread requirement and 37.87% to delist the company.
The offer’s first closing date falls on Nov 24 but can still be extended. The offer notice was issued on Oct 13, when Genting held a 49.36% stake in Genting Malaysia.
Genting Malaysia’s non-interested directors, save for non-executive chairman Tan Sri Mohd Zahidi Zainuddin, who is also an indirect major shareholder of Kenanga IB, concurred with Kenanga IB’s opinion that the offer is “not fair” and “not reasonable”.
At noon break, shares in Genting were one sen or 0.28% lower at RM3.51, valuing the group at RM13.61 billion.
Genting Malaysia’s shares were one sen or 0.43% higher at RM2.36, giving the group a market capitalisation of RM14.01 billion.
Source: TheEdge - 14 Nov 2025

title: Genting Extends Takeover Offer for Genting Malaysia to Dec 1
author: edgeinvest
body:
KUALA LUMPUR (Nov 13): The closing date for the voluntary takeover offer by Genting Bhd (KL:GENTING) for Genting Malaysia (KL:GENM) has been extended to 5pm, Dec 1, from Nov 24.
The offer turned unconditional on Nov 3 after the cumulative stake held by Genting and parties acting in concert with the company crossed the 50% mark.
According to a statement issued by Genting's principal adviser AmInvestment Bank, the group now owns 3.23 billion GENM shares — representing 57.008% of GENM’s total issued shares (excluding treasury shares) — following share purchases on the open market.
Following the additional 34.93 million GENM shares acquired on the open market on Thursday, Genting has collectively acquired a total of 114.47 million GENM shares or a 2.02% stake, excluding treasury shares and shares received through valid acceptances.
The group bought an additional 34.93 million GENM shares on the open market on Thursday (Nov 13), according to the statement.
The offer price of RM2.35 per share represents a nearly 10% premium to GENM’s last traded price of RM2.14 on Oct 10 before the stock was suspended for the announcement.
“In view of the above, the present unconditional voluntary takeover offer has become an unconditional mandatory takeover offer on Nov 13,” AmInvestment Bank added.
The offer notice was issued on Oct 13, when Genting held a 49.36% stake in GENM.
Independent adviser Kenanga Investment Bank has recommended that shareholders reject Genting’s takeover offer that paves the way to take GENM private. It said the offer is “not fair”, saying that the RM2.35 per share voluntary takeover offer is below GENM’s sum-of-parts derived valuation.
The RM2.35 apiece offer represents a discount of between 32.47% and 37.67% to GENM shares' estimated value of RM3.48 and RM3.77, and a 3.69% and 19.52% discount to the shares’ one-year and two-year high market prices, Kenanga IB noted.
Kenanga IB also said the deal is “not reasonable”, noting that investors may have the opportunity to realise their investment via the open market if Genting doesn’t manage to acquire the required 90% stake to delist GENM, and due to Genting’s US prospects with a New York licence bid submitted and the restructuring of Empire Resorts.
Genting’s share price dropped two sen to close at RM3.50 on Thursday, valuing the group at RM13.57 billion. GENM’s share price was unchanged at RM2.36, giving the group a market capitalisation of RM13.95 billion.
Source: TheEdge - 14 Nov 2025

title: GenM: The ‘Offer’ gets a bit Complicated!
author: BLee
body:
GenM: The ‘Offer’ gets a bit Complicated!
From ‘Conditional Voluntary Take-Over Offer’ to ‘UnConditional Voluntary Take-Over Offer’ to as at 13 Nov.2025, ‘Mandatory Take-Over Offer’; is there any other ‘evolution’ forthcoming? Most likely, there will be 2 more at 75% and 90/95%!
The ‘Mandatory Take-Over Offer’ triggers when “the Offeror and the PACs have collectively acquired a total of 114,469,300 GENM Shares during the Period (as defined below), representing 2.02% of the total issued GENM Shares (excluding treasury shares), at prices not exceeding the Offer Price of RM2.35 per Offer Share…. As the Offeror and the PACs have acquired (other than through Valid Acceptances received) more than 2% of GENM Shares during the Period, GENT is required under paragraph 4.01(b) of the Rules to extend a mandatory take-over offer (“MO”) to acquire all the remaining GENM Shares (excluding treasury shares) not already held by GENT.”
What has changed and what remains?
The Offer date extended to 1st Dec., 2025 due to the count date of this MO..all other conditions remain.
Why is the MO in this case triggered by the Offeror and the PACs and who are they?
Offeror - Genting Berhad
PACs - Persons deemed to be acting in concert with the Offeror in relation to the Offer pursuant to subsections 216(2) and/or 216(3) of the CMSA.
An AI search on the following Q;
Q: mandatory takeover offer in malaysia public listed company
“AI Overview
A mandatory takeover offer (MTO) in Malaysia is triggered when a party and its concert parties acquire control of over 33% of a public listed company's voting shares, or when they hold between 33% and 50% and acquire an additional 2% within a six-month period. An MTO can also be triggered if the Securities Commission Malaysia (SC) determines that a party has control, even if their shareholding is below 33%. The MTO is a formal offer to buy the remaining shares and must be made to all shareholders, with the offer price determined by the MTO Rules, and it is subject to certain conditions, such as accepting enough shares to gain over 50% ownership…
Key characteristics of a mandatory takeover offer
‘- Offer to all shareholders: The offer must be made to all shareholders of the target company, not just a select few.
‘- Conditional acceptance: The offer is subject to the condition that it receives enough acceptances to result in the offeror and its PACs holding more than 50% of the target's voting shares.
‘- Securities Commission's role: The SC oversees the process and can grant exemptions in certain circumstances.
‘- Price determination: The offer price is governed by the MTO Rules, and the offeror must ensure it has sufficient funds to satisfy the offer.
Important considerations:
‘- Disclosure obligations: Stake-building strategies must consider relevant disclosure obligations.
‘- Control during the process: An offeror cannot appoint directors to the target board or exercise their voting rights until the offer document is dispatched and SC consent is obtained.
Exemptions: It is possible to seek an exemption from the MTO requirements from the SC, depending on the specific circumstances.”
Note: Accuracy of AI search is for reading pleasure only, Not verify..
Will discuss further if ‘75% and 90/95%’ stage triggered..

Detail 2: The Trading on 14 Nov., 2025 which “the Offeror and the PACs” have very limited opportunity to Acquire at the Offer price of RM2.35! My comment at i3 to one Forumer:
“Sell to which parties? GenT and PACs can't buy at 2.36 and above unless they trigger Mandatory buy at a higher price! As seen at trading volume yesterday, 14 Nov., 2025, only 2.502m done at 2.35. Over 52.8m GenM Shares which GenT and PACs cannot be bought. If this trend continues, it will be out of GenT and PACs control; most likely a price war will be erupted if the target of 75% is to be achieved.. let the market dictates when to sell or buy, let's not be emotional (no person in particular as we can write freely anonymously), Happy Trading and TradeAtYourOwnRisk”

title: GenM: The True or False?
author: BLee
body:
GenM: The True or False?
A few Questions linger in our mind; What happens when the Offer to Unconditional/Conditional Voluntary/Mandatory Offer reaches their Goals? This is not the first time my investment was taken private, the previous AP Land, UDA, Brem, etc taken private can't be bothered as too busy at work, now at semi-retirement, have the time and resources to read and write…
It is quite difficult to understand some of the jargon written in the Offer Doc, some more makes it more complicated with new development which is not covered in the Offer Doc. Different readers posted their opinions in the i3 forum, could wrongly interpret what has been written, me included… The True or False.
Q1. Can the Offeror buy small quantities above RM2.35, the Offer price will not change? True or False?
A1. Item 6 in the Offer Doc. “PURCHASES IN THE OPEN MARKET: If the Offeror or any of the PACs purchase or agree to purchase any Offer Shares during the Offer Period at a consideration that is higher than the Offer Price, the Offeror will increase the Offer Price to at least the highest price (excluding stamp duty and commission) paid or agreed to be paid by the Offeror or any of the PACs for the Offer Shares during the Offer Period.
If the Offeror increases the Offer Price, Holders who have accepted the Offer prior to the revision of the Offer Price will be entitled to receive the revised Offer Price in cash.” clearly stated the True or False..
Q2. Can PACs offer or buy the shares in open market, then act as ‘Acceptance Offer’ and who are PACs?
A2. As in A1, the ‘Offeror or any of the PACs’ is acting as one entity, any person stated in the PACs shall be binded by the TnC in the Offer Doc.
Detai 1: List of PACs that are binded by the TnC in the Offer Doc.
Q3. What are the condition of 75% and 90/95% of Acceptance Offer when met?
A3. As spelt out in the “Definition; Offer Shares: All the remaining GENM Shares (excluding treasury shares) which are not already held by the Offeror. As at the LPD, the Offer Shares comprise 2,833,939,874 GENM Shares, which represents 50.001% of the total GENM Shares in issue (excluding treasury shares).” As stated total GENM Shares in issue (excluding treasury shares); 25% equal 1,416,969,937, 75% equal 4,250,909,811, 90% equal 5,101,091,774 and 95% equal 5,384,485,761.
Also, the “Definition; Public Spread Requirement: The requirement under subparagraph 8.02(1) of the Listing Requirements, whereby a listed issuer must ensure that at least 25% of its total listed shares (excluding treasury shares) are in the hands of public shareholders to ensure its continued listing on the Main Market of Bursa Securities.”, the 25%, 75%, 90% and 95% must be met…
There are others conditions must be met such as “Pursuant to subparagraph 8.02(1) of the Listing Requirements, a listed issuer must ensure that the Public Spread Requirements are met. Bursa Securities may accept a percentage lower than 25% of the total number of listed shares (excluding treasury shares) if it is satisfied that such lower percentage is sufficient for a liquid market of such shares… However, the non-compliance of the Public Spread Requirement will not automatically result in the delisting of GENM from the Official List… upon 90% or more of the listed shares (excluding treasury shares)... where the offeror has announced that it does not intend to maintain the listing status, Bursa Securities shall suspend the trading of the listed issuer’s securities immediately upon the expiry of 5 market days from the Closing Date, in accordance with subparagraph 16.02(3) of the Listing Requirements”
On the “Revision of the Offer: … the revised Offer will remain open for acceptances for a period of at least 14 days from the date of posting… Where any of the terms of the Offer are revised, the revised terms of the Offer will be made available to the Holders who have previously accepted the Offer prior to such revision.”
On the “Closing of the Offer: Where the Offer has become or is declared unconditional as to acceptances on a day falling on or before Friday, 19 December 2025, being the 46th day from the Posting Date, the Offer will remain open for acceptances for at least 14 days from the date on which the Offer becomes and is declared unconditional which, in any event, shall not be later than Friday, 2 January 2026, being the 60th day from the Posting Date.”

title: Genting Malaysia Berhad - Dragged By Higher Costs & Lower Forex Gains
author: PublicInvest
body:
Genting Malaysia (GENM) posted a 79% YoY decline in 3QFY25 net profit to RM119.7m, mainly due to lower unrealised foreign exchange translation gains on its USD borrowing, higher finance and tax costs. For 9MFY25, core profit of RM332.6m came in below our and market expectations at 64% and 59% of full-year estimates respectively. The shortfall was mainly due to higher-than-expected depreciation, interest and tax costs. We cut our FY25-27F earnings by 2-7% to account for higher costs. While share price is already trading at the voluntary general offer price, we maintain our Trading Buy call in view of the potential near-term catalyst of it securing a casino license in the downstate New York. Announcement is expected to be made on 1 December 2025.
3QFY25 revenue increased by 22.1% YoY, primarily due to stronger contribution from Malaysia and the US operations. Revenue from Malaysia rose 19% YoY on the back of higher business volume from the gaming segment while the US & Bahamas posted a 64% jump due to the consolidation of Genting Empire Resorts following the acquisition of the remaining 51% membership interest.
3QFY25 core net profit fell 34.7% YoY, due to higher operating costs in the UK and higher interest cost after refinancing. Tax cost has also increased to RM159.2m from an income of RM12.5m in 3QFY24. Meanwhile, headline net profit dropped by 79% YoY mainly due to lower foreign exchange translation gains on its USD denominated borrowings of only RM2.8m versus RM601.8m in 3QFY24.
Outlook . Following the announcement of the proposed privatisation, Genting Bhd (GENT) has extended the closing date for its voluntary takeover to 1 December from 24 November. This date also coincides with the release of the final decision of GENM's bid for a commercial casino license in New York by the New York State Gaming Commission. GENT currently holds 57% of GENM. Meanwhile, the independent adviser has recommended that GENM shareholders reject the offer at RM2.35 a share, indicating that the bid is "not fair" and "not reasonable". If GENT is unable to secure sufficient acceptance rate, it could possibly revise up the offer price. More so if GENM manages to secure the downstate New York casino license.
Source: PublicInvest Research - 28 Nov 2025

title: Genting Berhad - Results Below Our Expectations
author: PublicInvest
body:
Genting Bhd (GENT) posted an 86.5% YoY decline in headline net profit to RM30.3m in 3QFY25 due to the recognition of lower unrealised foreign exchange translation gains from its USD denominated borrowings. For 9MFY25, core profit of RM551m came in below our estimates at ~50% of full-year estimates due to higher-than-expected financing cost and effective tax rate. We slash our FY25-27F earnings forecasts by an average of 36% after raising our interest and tax cost assumptions. We maintain our Neutral rating on GENT with an unchanged SOTP-based TP of RM3.30 , pending further announcement of its proposed voluntary takeover of Genting Malaysia as well as the results of the award of casino license for the downstate region in New York.
3QFY25 revenue rose 14.3% YoY . Resorts World Sentosa (RWS) delivered a robust result (+13% YoY) on the back of improved VIP rolling volume and higher win rate while non-gaming revenue has also increased. Resorts World Genting (RWG) posted a 19% jump in revenue due to higher business volume from the gaming segment. Revenue in the US & Bahamas rose 20% YoY after the consolidation of Genting Empire Resorts ' contribution. The UK & Egypt only delivered a 2% growth due to the strengthening of the ringgit against GBP. The leisure & hospitality segment accounted for 83% of group's revenue.
3QFY25 core net profit was down 62% YoY, largely due to higher financing cost and effective tax rate at 47%. The increase in tax cost was due to higher Malaysian income tax charge and deferred tax charge, as losses of certain subsidiaries have not been allowed for tax deduction.
Maintain Neutral. While GENT 's valuation looks compelling at 13x FY26F EPS, we see potential downside risk to FY26F earnings, as the slowdown in economic activities is likely to affect its hospitality and entertainment industry globally. Additionally, cost could continue to rise, particularly salary, administrative and tax costs. Apart from the impact of a stronger ringgit against the USD and GBP, a declining job market and consumer confidence in the US and UK may lead to lower gaming revenue going forward. However, we note that the likelihood of GENM winning a full casino license in New York could be a near-term share price catalyst for GENT .
Source: PublicInvest Research - 28 Nov 2025

title: Genting Berhad - Recovery in Progress
author: sectoranalyst
body:
Review
Genting’s 9M25 core profit of RM83.4mn accounted for 53.5% of our fullyear forecast and 10.7% of consensus estimates. We consider this as above expectation as 4Q earnings tends to be strong due to seasonal factors. Note that Genting Singapore (GENS) has recovered strongly from 2Q25 slump in terms of VIP volume while Resorts World Genting 3Q25 earnings remained robust. We expect the trend to persist into 4Q25.
Genting’s 9M25 adjusted EBITDA slumped 12.2% YoY to RM6.2bn while revenue was largely flat at RM20.8bn. The disappointment was driven by lacklustre performance of all casino units in Singapore, UK, US, partially mitigated by increased contribution from Resorts World Genting.
GENS’ 9M25 adj. EBITDA declined 12% YoY to S$646.4mn with a slight 3.1% drop in revenue to 1.9bn. The decline can be attributed to weaker 1H25 performance as 1Q24 earnings were spurred by high VIP volume and margin expansion. For 3Q25, the gaming revenue expanded by 21.9% YoY to S$402.3mn, supported by recovery in VIP rolling volume and win rate. 3Q25 adj. EBITDA grew 36% YoY to S$222.7mn.
GENM’s 9M25 adjusted EBITDA contracted by 5% YoY to RM2.6bn despite a moderate 8.5% growth in revenue. This was mainly due to weaker performance from its UK and US operations, partially offset by higher contribution from Resorts World Genting (see GENM report).
Resorts World Las Vegas’s (RWLV) 9MFY25 revenue and adjusted EBITDA declined by 20.1% and 64.1% YoY to RM2.3bn and RM179.8mn respectively. The dismay performance was due to lower visitation amid macroeconomic uncertainty. In addition, the margin was weakened by weaker hold percentage in 1Q25 and higher payroll costs.
Impact
We raise GENT’s FY25-27 earnings projections by 38.9/8.2/-9.0% after factoring in revised GENM’s earnings projections.
Outlook
With regards to privatisation of GENM, GENT has accumulated 63.4% stake in GENM on Nov 26 and the offer will expire on Dec 1. We still think the chance of getting more than 75% is slim as GENM’s current price has gone up to the offer price of RM2.35/share.
We expect the Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix in November to spur RWLV’s 4Q25 performance. Management is optimistic on 2026 performance as Las Vegas will host a variety of exciting events, including conventions and concerts.
Valuation
Following the change in our target price for GENM to RM3.06, along with the increase of stake in GENM to 63.4%, we raise GENT’s SOP valuation to RM4.20/share (from RM3.44). Maintain Buy
Source: TA Research - 28 Nov 2025

title: Genting Malaysia Berhad - No Signs of VIP Volume Slowing Down
author: sectoranalyst
body:
Review
Genting Malaysia’s (GENM) 9M25 core profit of RM446.1mn beat our expectation but was in line with consensus forecast. The variance was largely due to higher-than-expected hold percentage for casino operations in Malaysia. No dividend was declared for 9M25.
GENMN’s 9M25 adjusted EBITDA contracted by 5% YoY to RM2.6bn despite a moderate 8.5% growth in revenue. This was mainly due to weaker performance from its UK and US operations, partially offset by higher contribution from Resorts World Genting. The core profit slipped 15.9% YoY due to high effective tax rate.
On quarterly basis, the 3Q25 adjusted PBT surged 62.9% YoY to RM299.0mn, driven by higher hold percentage for its casino operations in Malaysia. However, the core profit contracted by 25.4% to RM161.8mn due to the high effective tax rate.
Impact
We raise our FY25-26 earnings projections by 6.6-48.9% after factoring in higher win rates on VIP and non-VIP volumes for Malaysia casino segment. However, we cut FY27 earnings projections lower by 18.8% after revising our ringgit assumptions to 4.10/US and 5.20/GBP.
Conference call highlights
Resorts World Genting chalked up another decent performance for 3Q25. VIP and non-VIP volume surged 25% and 17% YoY respectively with a mix of 57%:43% for the quarter. YTD VIP volume soared 5% while the non-VIP volume increased 15% YoY. Foreign visitation was strong led by visitors from Singapore (+7%), China (+17%) and India (+8%) in 3Q25.
For those new casino licences in downstate New York, the winners are expected to be announced on Dec 1. The chance of GENM securing the licence is high after MGM Resorts withdrew its bid. GENM has pledge a US$7.5bn investment, comprising a community fund of US$2bn, existing premises worth US$1.1bn and expansion capex of US$4.4bn.
Upon receiving the licence in end-Dec, GENM will rejuvenate this brownfield development and is expected to start offering table games on July 1. It will have the first mover advantage as the other two bidders are embarking on new resort projects.
However, we are not overly excited before we can get hold of the information regarding the casino tax and licence validity period. Note that one of bidders withdrew its bid after knowing that it was a 15-year licence instead of a 30-year licence, along with a minimum tax of about USD400mn.
Valuation
Given the change in earnings, we raise GENM’s DCF valuation to RM3.06/share (from RM2.35) with a revised CAPM of 14.0%. Maintain Buy
Source: TA Research - 28 Nov 2025

title: Genting Malaysia (GENM MK) - Above expectations
author: PhillipCapital
body:
9M25 core net profit of RM453m was above expectations
We raise our EPS forecasts by 10-17% to account for better-than-expected leisure and hospitality businesses
Maintain HOLD rating with an unchanged TP of RM2.35
Result above expectations
GENM reported 9M25 revenue of RM8.9bn (+8% YoY) and core net profit at RM453m (-19% YoY). The results were above our and consensus expectations on the back of stronger-than-expected leisure and hospitality businesses. EBITDA margin eased by 0.7ppts to 26.6% reflecting higher operating costs, marketing and payroll expenses across segments. Management anticipates better 4Q25 performances supported by 50% anniversary promotional pricing in conjunction with GENM's 60th anniversary and contribution from newly acquired Stratford casino.
3Q25 earnings dragged by higher operating costs
Sequentially, 3Q25 revenue rose 15% mainly driven by leisure and hospitality business in Malaysia (+12%), UK (+7%) and US (+34%). Despite the stronger topline, EBITDA margin slipped 4ppts at 24.8% as operating costs rose across key geographical markets. Core net profit was lower at RM154m weighed down by softer margin as well as higher finance and tax expenses. In the analyst briefing, management highlighted encouraging progress on its New York casino expansion plan, noting strong support from the local community advisory committee- an important milestone towards securing a full casino license. Management reiterated that GENM would be able to roll out table games within 6 months upon securing the licence, which it aims by end-Dec25.
Maintain HOLD with unchanged TP of RM2.35
We raise our 2025E-27E earnings forecasts by 10-17% to reflect the stronger-than-expected leisure and hospitality businesses. We maintain our HOLD rating with unchanged 12-month TP of RM2.35. While the offer price provides an exit opportunity, we believe some investors may choose not to accept it, given their higher entry cost. We continue to see GENM as one of the main beneficiaries of Visit Malaysia 2026 and see long term potential if GENM secures the downstate NYC casino license, expected to be awarded by end25. Key risks include higher/lower-than-expected win rates, a hike/reduction in gaming taxes, lift/drag from key associates, and value-destructive related-party transactions.
