title: Genting Berhad (GENT MK) - Above expectation
author: PhillipCapital
body:
9M25 core earnings of RM497m, above our expectations
Sequentially, 3Q25 earnings were dragged by contraction in EBITDA margin amid rising cost pressure as well as higher interest and tax expenses
Maintain BUY with a higher SOP-derived target price of RM4.00
Above our expectations, driven by the RWG and palm oil segments
9M25 revenue was broadly flat at RM20.8bn (-0.3% YoY). Lower revenue contribution from RWS and RWLV was due to the absence of 2024 visa-driven demand and weaker visitation amid macroeconomic uncertainty. Nonetheless, this was offset by higher sales volume in the plantation and property segments. EBITDA margin declined by 4.1 ppts to 30%, primarily due to weaker margins in leisure & hospitality (-4.9 ppts YoY), property (-1.5 ppts YoY), and plantation (-9.7 ppts YoY) segments. Overall, weaker margins combined with higher tax rate of 47.3% (+18ppts YoY) and lower interest income, led to YoY decline in net core profit to RM497.3m. Results came in at 83% of our and 64% of consensus full-year estimates. The earnings beat our estimates due to higher-than-expected effective tax and margin from RWG and palm oil businesses.
3Q25 earnings dragged by higher expenses
GENT's 3Q25 revenue rose 10.2% QoQ to RM7.5bn, mainly driven by stronger visitation at RWG, supported by higher guests' arrival from Singapore, China, and India, as well as higher palm products price and sales volume. Despite the stronger topline, core net profit declined by 77.3% QoQ to RM77.8m mainly dragged by 1ppts contraction in EBITDA margin amid rising cost pressure as well as higher interest and tax expenses. In the briefing, management highlighted that the company plans to reserve cash for upcoming debt maturities and capital commitments for the New York casino license, with dividend payments to be considered thereafter to ensure a balance between shareholder returns and financial obligations.
Maintain BUY with a higher TP of RM4.00
We lift our 2025-27E earnings estimates by 7-14% after incorporating in higher revenue and EBITDA margin from gaming and leisure and plantation segments We maintain our BUY rating with a higher SOP-derived TP of RM4.00 (from RM3.80) to factor in higher earnings assumption and TP revision of GENM from RM2.10 to RM2.35. Key risks to our BUY call include lower-than-expected win rates, rising operational costs, and a decline in both gaming and non-gaming revenue.
Source: Phillip Capital Research - 28 Nov 2025

title: Genting Malaysia’s 3Q Net Profit Slumps 79% on Lower Forex Gains
author: edgeinvest
body:
KUALA LUMPUR (Nov 27): Genting Malaysia Bhd’s (KL:GENM) third-quarter net profit fell 79% from a year earlier as the group recorded sharply lower unrealised foreign exchange gains.
Net profit for the three months ended Sept 30, 2025 (3QFY2025) declined to RM119.69 million from RM569.16 million, as forex-related income dropped to RM2.8 million from RM601.8 million, according to the group's exchange filing on Thursday.
Earnings per share stood at 2.11 sen, down from 10.04 sen in 3QFY2024.
Revenue for the quarter increased 22.1% year-on-year to RM3.36 billion from RM2.75 billion, driven by higher business volume at Resorts World Genting in Malaysia and contributions from newly consolidated assets of Empire Resorts Inc in the US.
No dividend was declared for the quarter.
In terms of segmental performance, the Malaysian leisure and hospitality segment posted a 19% year-on-year increase in revenue to RM1.99 billion and a 27% increase in adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda) to RM627.4 million.
In the US and the Bahamas, revenue surged 64% to RM774.3 million, while adjusted Ebitda rose 22% to RM151.2 million, supported by the consolidation of Empire Resorts.
In the UK and Egypt, revenue grew 2% to RM546.6 million but adjusted Editda declined 17% to RM86.3 million due to higher operating costs.
For the nine-month period, Genting Malaysia's net profit fell 14.1% year-on-year to RM609.02 million, while revenue rose 8.4% to RM8.87 billion.
The group said it remains cautious on near-term prospects due to geopolitical tensions and macroeconomic uncertainties but maintains a positive outlook over the longer term, anchored by recovery in international tourism and strategic growth initiatives.
In Malaysia, the group aims to capitalise on the Visit Malaysia Year 2026 campaign to boost visitor arrivals to Resorts World Genting. The upcoming launch of its ecotourism attraction, Eufloria, and the near-completion of the revamped 18-hole golf course at Resorts World Awana are expected to strengthen the group’s leisure offerings.
In the US, Genting Malaysia said it has submitted supplementary materials to the New York Gaming Facility Location Board as part of its bid for a full commercial casino licence for Resorts World New York City. The decision is expected by Dec 1, with licences slated for issuance by year end, potentially transforming Resorts World New York City into a full-fledged integrated resort.
In the UK, the group is rolling out additional gaming machines across its casinos following legislative changes. Emphasis remains on disciplined cost management and operational efficiency, alongside continued investment in new products to enhance customer experience and attract a broader audience.
Shares of Genting Malaysia slipped one sen or 0.42% to RM2.35 on Thursday, giving the group a market capitalisation of RM13.95 billion. The stock has gained over 4% year to date.
Source: TheEdge - 28 Nov 2025

title: Genting Posts Steep Drop in 3Q Net Profit, Hit by Forex and Interest-income Headwinds
author: edgeinvest
body:
Genting Bhd posted an 86.5% drop in net profit of RM30.3 million for the third quarter Sept 30, 2025 from RM223.8 million a year earlier on weaker unrealised forex gains, lower interest income and higher depreciation.
KUALA LUMPUR, (Nov 27): Genting Bhd (KL:GENTING) has posted a sharp 86.5% decline in its net profit for the third quarter, largely driven by weaker unrealised foreign-exchange gains, lower interest income and higher depreciation.
Net profit for the three months ended Sept 30, 2025 (3QFY2025) came in at RM30.3 million, compared to RM223.8 million a year earlier, the group's bourse filing on Thursday showed. Earnings per share dropped to 0.79 sen from 5.81 sen.
Revenue, however, increased 14.25% to RM7.48 billion from RM6.54 billion.
No dividend was declared for the quarter.
The group's Malaysia leisure and hospitality segment reported a 19% year-on-year increase in revenue to RM1.99 billion, supported by higher gaming volumes at Resorts World Genting.
Singapore’s Resorts World Sentosa posted a revenue growth of 13% to RM2.14 billion, with profit before taxation (PAT) climbing 35% to RM759.4 million due to improved VIP rolling volumes and non-gaming business.
The UK and Egypt operations delivered RM546.6 million in revenue, a modest 2% increase, aided by the newly acquired Stratford casino, though PAT declined due to rising payroll and operating expenses.
Revenue from the US and the Bahamas rose 20% to RM1.51 billion, underpinned by the consolidation of Genting Empire Resorts LLC, but Resorts World Las Vegas experienced lower earnings due to weaker visitation.
Genting's plantation operations saw a 3% rise in revenue to RM882 million, with stronger palm product prices, while the power division posted a 5% gain in revenue to RM305.9 million, benefitting from improved generation at the Banten plant in Indonesia.
Conversely, the oil and gas division was impacted by weaker global crude prices and a stronger ringgit, with revenue down 21% to RM89.6 million.
The group’s property segment more than doubled its revenue to RM106.5 million, driven by recent project launches.
For the cumulative nine months ended Sept 30, 2025, Genting's net profit declined 73.5% to RM278.42 million, compared with RM1.05 billion in the previous corresponding period, while revenue was marginally lower at RM20.77 billion from RM20.84 billion.
Looking ahead, Genting faces a mixed outlook. While recovery in tourism and leisure demand may lift its hospitality and resort segments, ongoing currency volatility, interest-rate and cost pressures pose clear headwinds.
In Malaysia, the Visit Malaysia Year 2026 campaign and the upcoming launch of ecotourism attraction Eufloria and the revamped golf course at Resorts World Awana are expected to support growth at Resorts World Genting.
In Singapore, Resorts World Sentosa aims to sustain momentum with the opening of The Laurus luxury hotel and upcoming large-scale activations, while progressing on its RWS 2.0 development including Super Nintendo World and a new waterfront precinct.
In the US, the group awaits the outcome of its bid to transform Resorts World New York City into a full-fledged casino resort, while in Las Vegas, it is positioning to benefit from expected record convention attendance in 2026 and ongoing recovery in high-end casino play.
In the Bahamas, marketing efforts and cruise partnerships are expected to support visitor growth at Resorts World Bimini.
Genting's plantation segment anticipates firmer palm product prices in the near term, although full-year fresh fruit bunches production may be marginally lower.
In property, ongoing launches in Genting Indahpura and Genting Pura Kencana are expected to drive revenue, supported by positive reception of recent developments.
The power division anticipates stable performance, barring plant outages, while development of the Kasuri gas block and related infrastructure in Indonesia is progressing, with financing arrangements targeted for early 2026.
Genting shares slipped two sen or 0.6% to close at RM3.32 on Thursday, for a market capitalisation of RM12.87 billion. Year to date, the counter has fallen more than 13%.
Source: TheEdge - 28 Nov 2025

title: Genting Malaysia to Remain Listed After Genting Falls Short of 75% Ownership Threshold
author: edgeinvest
body:
KUALA LUMPUR (Dec 1): Genting Malaysia Bhd (KL:GENM) will remain listed, after Genting Bhd (KL:GENTING) secured less than a 75% stake in the company following its privatisation bid.
In a filing with the bourse, Genting said that as at 5pm on Dec 1, it had only managed to secure a 73.133% interest in the GENM at the close of its offer. Another 0.202% in acceptances were yet to be vetted.
Genting had said it would not maintain GENM's listing status should the acceptance level for its RM2.35-a-share offer cause the company to fall below the 25% public shareholding spread.
The deal’s independent adviser recommended that shareholders reject Genting’s privatisation offer, citing a steep discount and the stock’s easy tradability.
The RM2.35 per share offer was a nearly 10% premium to GENM’s last traded price of RM2.14 on Oct 10, before the stock was suspended for the offer announcement.
Genting extended its voluntary takeover offer for Genting Malaysia to Dec 1 from Nov 24, after it only managed to up its stake to 57.008% by Nov 13.
It started with 49.999% when the offer was announced on Oct 13, and acquired another six million shares to surpass the 50% ownership threshold, turning it unconditional on Nov 3.
Genting's offer for GENM closes as GENM's ambitious casino bid in New York is due to be announced on Dec 1 in the US. The New York Gaming Facility Location Board is expected to announce its selections for one of three coveted downstate commercial casino licences, ending a multi-year contest that originally drew eight contenders.
GENM closed unchanged at RM2.35 on Monday, valuing the company at RM13.3 billion. The stock is up 3.98% this year.
Genting’s share price closed 2.75% higher at RM3.36, valuing the company at RM12.9 billion. It is down 12.95% this year.
Source: TheEdge - 2 Dec 2025

title: Genting Malaysia (GENM MK) - Shortlisted for downstate casino license
author: PhillipCapital
body:
GENM has been shortlisted by NYGFB to proceed to the licensing stage under NYSGC
The group is now undergoing mandatory security, fitness, and background checks, with the license expected to be issued by 31 Dec 25 and Phase 1 of gaming facilities slated for opening by Mar26
Maintain HOLD rating and 12-month TP of RM2.35
Selected for the downstate New York license
GENM's wholly-owned subsidiary, Resorts World New York City (RWNYC), has been shortlisted as 1 of the 3 New York casino licenses by the New York Gaming Facilities Location Board (NYGFB), alongside Bally's Bronx and Hard Rock Metropolitan Park. The results did not come as a surprise following MGM's withdrawal in Oct25, which left 3 contenders in the running. By remaining the only casino in the downstate market until new licensees begin operations (likely 2030), this gives GENM an exclusive exposure to the region in the near term. The casino involves US$500m in license fees over a 30-year term with an estimated capex of US$3.3bn.
License target to be issued by 31 Dec 25
GENM is currently undergoing the mandatory security, fitness, and background checks required for its New York casino license. The due diligence covers integrity and background reviews of key owners, management personnel, and affiliated group entities, as well as a detailed review of legal compliance. The license is expected to be issued by 31 Dec 25, subject to the successful completion of these checks. Operationally, RWNYC has begun closing certain casino areas in 3Q25 to allow for the expansion of gaming facilities. The upgraded facilities are now expected to reopen by Mar26, ahead of the previously guided Jun26 timeline, providing potential earnings upside.
Maintain HOLD and TP of RM2.35
We maintain HOLD rating and TP of RM2.35. We have not factored in any potential contributions from new downstate license as we expect the positive earnings would be offset by set-up costs and finance cost for new downstate development in the first few years of operation. We continue to see GENM as one of the main beneficiaries of Visit Malaysia 2026 and see long-term potential from the new downstate NYC casino license. Key risks include higher/lower-than-expected win rates, a hike/reduction in gaming taxes, lift/drag from key associates, and value/destructive related-party transactions.
GENM maintains listing status. As of closing date of take-over offer on 1 Dec 25, Tan Sri Lim Kok Thay (Deputy Chairman and Executive Director) and his persons acting in concert (PAC) increased their shareholding on GENM by 23.1% to 73.1% but failed to privatise due to public holdings spread staying above the mandated 25% threshold. With the intention of privatising GENM, we expect Tan Sri Lim and his PAC will continue increasing their holdings to above 75% to achieve the required threshold via open market.
Source: Phillip Capital Research - 3 Dec 2025

title: Genting Malaysia Berhad - Winning of Casino License in Downstate New York
author: sectoranalyst
body:
Announcement
Yesterday, Genting Malaysia (GENM) announced that its wholly owned subsidiary, Genting New York LLC, has been selected by the New York Gaming Facility Location Board to proceed to licensure consideration by the New York State Gaming Commission (NYSGC). The NYSGC is expected to announce the issuance of licenses by 31 Dec 2025.
Previously, the company announced that it has pledged US$5.5bn investments to convert the existing Aqueduct Racetrack to a full-fledge resort casino. An estimated 5,000 union construction jobs would be created to realise an integrated resort with a total of a 500k sf gaming floor with 6,000 slots and 800 table games; 2,000 hotel rooms; a 7,000-seat entertainment venue; more than 7,000 car spaces, over 30 food and beverage outlets, large-scale meeting space; other resort amenities and more than 10 acres of community greenspace.
Our takes
Judging from the huge catchment market with an estimated population of 2.3mn in Queens and 8.3mn population in New York City (NYC). We are positive on GENM’s win of a casino licence in downstate New York. Besides, NYC is also one of the most visited destinations in the U.S., comprising approximately 51.6mn local visitors and 12.9mn international tourists. Importantly, we believe GENM will have a first mover advantage over its competitors in offering table games.
From the risk perspective, the concentration risk, where 61% of 9M25 revenue and 67% of 9M25 EBITDA came from Malaysia operations, can be further diversified via additional contribution from Resorts World New York City (RWNYC).
Forecast
We raise our FY26-27 earnings by 10.7-15.6% after factoring in higher revenue growth of 20-25% (vs. 5% previously) from RWNYC, capex of RM1.0bn in 2026 and RM2.0bn in 2027, and debt-equity financing ratio of 80:20.
Valuation
We maintain GENM’s DCF valuation at RM3.06/share with a revised CAPM of 15%. The new casino licence win comes as no surprise, and we consider it to be fully embedded in the current valuation. Maintain Buy
Source: TA Research - 3 Dec 2025

title: Genting Malaysia Wins New York Casino Licence; Shares Slip
author: edgeinvest
body:
KUALA LUMPUR (Dec 2): Genting Malaysia Bhd (KL:GENM), now over 73% controlled by Genting Bhd (KL:GENTING), has been selected for one of the three prized casino licences in New York.
According to a Bursa Malaysia filing, its subsidiary, Genting New York LLC, has been chosen by the New York Gaming Facility Location Board (GFLB) to advance to the final licensing review stage with the New York State Gaming Commission (GC).
The board is anticipated to finalise and announce the issuance of licences by Dec 31, 2025.
Genting Malaysia’s shares fell after the news, ending the day 10 sen or 4.26% lower at RM2.25 for a market capitalisation of RM13.36 billion. Genting also slipped, finishing seven sen or 2.08% lower at RM3.29, valuing it at RM12.75 billion. The stock is down 14.77% this year.
The win comes on the heels of an unsuccessful RM2.35-per-share privatisation exercise of Genting Malaysia by Genting, as the latter did not meet the 75% shareholding threshold required to delist the target company from Bursa Malaysia.
Genting Malaysia’s proposal outlined a US$5.5 billion (RM23.19 billion) plan to convert Resort World New York City (RWNYC) from a racino, that combines horse racing track and slot machines, into an integrated resort with expanded gaming floors and extensive non-gaming facilities.
“Applicants made ambitious commitments to workforce diversity, community investment and local, unionised hiring,” Genting Malaysia’s board said in a statement, stressing the need for the bidders to fully deliver on their commitments.
Nonetheless, Maybank Investment Bank in a separate note said Genting Malaysia has struck “gold” with the licence, estimating that net profit generated from the expanded RWNYC could reach a whopping RM1.93 billion in 2030.
Meanwhile, CIMB Securities highlighted that key commercial terms — including licence duration, gaming tax rates, and the final number of allowed table games and slot machines — remain unclear, as it reiterated a “hold” call on the stock at RM2.55.
Genting Malaysia’s proposal includes a 500,000 square-feet gaming floor, 6,000 slot machines, 800 table games, 2,000 hotel rooms, a 7,000-seat entertainment venue, more than 30 food and beverage outlets, large meeting spaces and over 10 acres of greenspace.
However, CIMB noted that the GFLB is particularly concerned that RWNYC is seeking to lower its proposed tax rates (slots: 56%, tables: 30%) to levels similar to those offered by other bidders — Metropolitan Park (slots: 25%, tables: 10%) and Bally’s Bronx (slots: 30%, tables: 10%). The board has urged the GC “to resist any back-tracking” on RWNYC’s initial commitments.
The GFLB also recommended that RWNYC be licensed for 4,635 slots and 534 tables, versus Genting Malaysia’s application for 6,000 slots and 800 tables, to preserve the quality of the visitor experience.
Resorts World likely only full-service casino in coming years
In the near term, Genting Malaysia’s Resort World will be the only full-service casino operational in New York City, as the other winners’ greenfield projects will only open their doors to gamblers around 2030.
RWNYC now offers mostly slot machines and electronic table games, with the licence allowing it to expand and deploy live table games as soon as June 2026.
The exclusive casino position in New York City until 2030 will provide stronger earnings and cash flows, significantly easing funding gap for the expansion and concerns over dilution from cash call, Kenanga Investment Bank said in a note.
The Malaysian casino operator has told US regulators that it can begin table-game and full-casino slot machine operations within six months of receiving the licence, and projected that the new casino could deliver tax revenue for the state as early as July 2026.
Apart from Genting Malaysia’s RWNYC, two other proposals were also picked for licences: Bally Corporation and Queens Future LLC, a joint venture between Steve Cohen, the owner of major baseball team New York Mets, and Hard Rock International.
According to Bloomberg , Genting Malaysia currently has six "buy" calls, eight "hold" calls and no "sell" call, with a consensus 12-month target price of RM2.59.
Source: TheEdge - 3 Dec 2025

A: AI Overview
To launch a second offer after a failed privatization in Malaysia, the offeror is generally required to observe a 12-month waiting period before making another attempt. This restriction, imposed by the Malaysian Code on Take-Overs and Mergers (the "Code"), can only be bypassed with the express consent of the Securities Commission (SC).
Key Regulations and Steps
‘1. 12-Month Restriction: The primary rule is that if an offer fails (meaning it does not become unconditional in all respects and is withdrawn or lapses), the offeror and parties acting in concert (PACs) cannot, for 12 months from the date of failure, do either of the following:
‘- Announce a new takeover offer or possible takeover offer for the same target company.
‘- Acquire any voting shares that would oblige them to make a mandatory general offer (MGO).
‘2. Seeking SC Consent: The only way around the 12-month cooling-off period is to apply for and obtain the SC's consent. The SC has the authority to issue rulings and exemptions based on the specific circumstances of the case.
‘- The offeror must present compelling reasons or a materially different proposal to convince the SC to waive the restriction.
‘- In the past, the SC has shown willingness to consider specific situations, as seen in cases where offerors have made subsequent offers (e.g., the FGV Holdings Bhd privatisation attempt).
‘3. Offer Price: If a second offer is eventually launched, especially if it is a mandatory offer, the offer price must adhere to the Code's guidelines. This generally means the price should not be less than the highest price paid by the offeror or their PACs during the offer period and the six months prior to the offer period.
‘4. Meeting the Thresholds: A key reason for a failed privatization is not reaching the required shareholding threshold (typically 90% of the total shares for compulsory acquisition and delisting). A second offer will need to aim for these thresholds to successfully take the company private.
‘5. Shareholder Circulars: Any new offer would require the preparation and dispatch of new offer documents and an independent adviser's circular to shareholders, which must be cleared by the SC, ensuring all shareholders are treated equally and provided with sufficient information to make an informed decision.

title: Genting Malaysia’s Shares Continue to Fall as Ratings Worries Overshadow New York Casino Progress Optimism
author: edgeinvest
body:
KUALA LUMPUR (Dec 3): Genting Malaysia Bhd’s (KL:GENM) share price extended its decline on Wednesday, as market optimism over its potential first-mover advantage in securing a downstate New York casino licence was offset by renewed concerns about a possible ratings downgrade at the group level.
CreditSights, a Fitch Solutions unit, said parent Genting Bhd (KL:GENTING) and Genting Malaysia face heightened risks of rating downgrades due to Genting’s high leverage and weak cash flow.
Based on Genting’s pro-forma results for the first nine months of 2025 (9M2025), the group breached downgrade trigger thresholds for cash flow, leverage, and earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortisation (Ebitda) at both Moody’s and Fitch, it said. Genting’s takeover bid for Genting Malaysia has raised its holdings in the company to 73.133%.
The stock slipped as much as 3.1% to RM2.18 shortly after the opening bell, before paring losses to settle at RM2.19 at the closing bell — making it among the top 20 losers by value on the local bourse.
At RM2.19, the gaming group had a market capitalisation of RM13 billion.
TA Research and Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB) Research raised their earnings forecasts for Genting Malaysia on expectations of stronger contributions from Resorts World New York City (RWNYC).
HLIB forecast core earnings of RM620.3 million for the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026 (FY2026), up 21.3% from FY2025, and projected FY2027 core earnings of RM735.2 million (+23.7%). The research house maintained its 'hold' rating with an unchanged target price (TP) of RM2.35.
TA Research expects Genting Malaysia’s net profit to rise 10.7% to RM986.2 million in FY2026, and a further 15.6% to RM1.08 billion in FY2027. It kept its 'buy' call with a TP of RM3.06.
The firm said RWNYC’s location — supported by a large Queens population and strong tourist traffic — provides Genting Malaysia early table-game advantages, while helping diversify earnings away from Malaysia, which still accounts for the bulk of revenue and Ebitda.
CIMB Securities, however, flagged that the New York Gaming Facility Location Board has yet to finalise critical licensing terms, including the licence duration, approved gaming capacity and tax rates. Regulators have also recommended reducing Genting’s proposed 6,000 slot machines and 800 table games to 4,635 slots and 534 tables. CIMB maintained its 'hold' call with a TP of RM2.55.
Still, RWNYC could begin offering live table games as early as mid-2026, potentially capturing the entire table-games gross gaming revenue pool from 2026 to 2030, CIMB said. Table rollout is expected to start with 250 tables in 2026, before expanding to 800 by 2029.
Genting New York LLC has proposed a US$5.5 billion (RM23.2 billion) upgrade of RWNYC, featuring a 500,000 sq ft gaming floor, 6,000 slots, 800 tables, 2,000 hotel rooms, a 7,000-seat arena, and more than 7,000 parking bays.
The New York gaming board has chosen the company to advance to the final licensing review stage with the New York State Gaming Commission. Licences are to be issued by Dec 31, 2025.
Source: TheEdge - 4 Dec 2025

title: CreditSights: High Debt, Weak Cash Flow Put Genting, Genting Malaysia at Downgrade Risk
author: edgeinvest
body:
KUALA LUMPUR (Dec 3): Genting Bhd (KL:GENTING) and Genting Malaysia Bhd (KL:GENM) are facing increased risks of rating downgrades with parent Genting’s high debt and weak cash flow situation, according to CreditSights.
In a report on Wednesday, the Fitch Solutions company said Genting breached Moody’s and Fitch downgrade triggers for cash flow, leverage, and earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda) based on the first nine months of 2025 (9M2025) pro-forma numbers.
“A rating downgrade of Genting by Moody’s and Fitch will bring it to Baa3/BBB-, with Genting Malaysia ratings tied to Genting,” said CreditSights. At present, both Moody’s and Fitch have placed Genting at Baa2/BBB ratings, while Fitch has a BBB rating on Genting Malaysia.
The research firm projected Genting’s retained cash flow-to-net debt could fall to 17%, below Moody’s trigger of 20% to 25%.
Genting’s gross leverage is at 5.9 times, above Moody’s four times trigger, and its Ebitda net leverage is over five times, above Fitch’s 3.5 times threshold.
“The situation is less clear at S&P (BBB-),” it added.
CreditSights said the credit ratings downgrade risk also affects Genting Malaysia because its ratings are tied to Genting’s and warned that its leverage could worsen from the front-loaded US$5.5 billion (RM22.71 billion) New York expansion costs that are largely debt-funded.
The research firm said Genting may narrowly avoid breaching Moody’s and Fitch triggers in FY2026 if the planned unused Miami land sale for US$1 billion goes through, but this is seen as unlikely.
“...we think the sale may be a long shot that both rating agencies may not be willing to factor in,” it said in its note.
CreditSights expects Genting Malaysia’s net leverage could worsen to highs of 6.0 times to 6.2 times by end-FY2026 (9M2025: 4.7 times) in the absence of the Miami asset sale.
Genting has secured 73.133% of Genting Malaysia shares at the close of its RM2.35-per-share offer on Dec 1 — below the 75% threshold required to delist the company.
CreditSights was surprised by strong shareholder support for Genting’s takeover bid given the unattractive offer price but sees Genting Malaysia’s privatisation as unlikely, saying the goal is to strengthen control, not delist. Genting was expected to increase its stake to 60%-65%.
The research firm kept its "market perform" recommendation on Genting and an "outperform" call on Genting Malaysia.
CreditSights said Genting has good geographical and business diversification outside of gaming and expects the company's earnings to pick up at the Singapore, UK, and Las Vegas units. The research firm also highlighted Genting's access to its cash-rich Genting Singapore subsidiary.
At the closing bell on Wednesday, Genting’s share price pared some of its losses to settle at RM3.27, down two sen or 0.61%. Earlier, the stock fell as much as 2.12% or seven sen to RM3.22. At RM3.27, Genting is valued at RM12.68 billion. The stock is down 15% this year.
Meanwhile, Genting Malaysia’s share price fell six sen or 2.67% to RM2.19, giving the company a market capitalisation of RM13 billion. Year to date, the stock is down by 3.1%.
Source: TheEdge - 4 Dec 2025

“Yes, very ‘Complex’ if GenT keeps buying from the open market. The question is can the buying burst through 75% without triggering any written regulations? The scenario could be different with and without the Offer Doc..? Again, good source is from AI, therefore Q&A as below:
Q: Upon failure of mandatory general offer, how can an offeror buy from open market bursa to reach 75% ownership?
A: “AI Overview
If a Mandatory General Offer (MGO) fails to reach the 50% threshold (or higher, if conditions set by Securities Commission Malaysia (SC) allowed), the offeror can't simply keep buying to 75% in the market without consequences; they'd need to re-evaluate, potentially seek an exemption, consider private arrangements, or potentially allow the MGO to lapse, then try a Voluntary Offer (VO) with SC approval to adjust conditions or address spread issues, all while adhering strictly to Bursa Malaysia rules on shareholding limits and disclosures.
Here's a breakdown of strategies and considerations:
‘1. Understanding the Failure:
‘- An MGO must reach 50% plus one share (or a higher condition approved by SC) to become unconditional. Failure means the offer conditions weren't met.
‘2. Post-Failure Actions (Options):
‘- Seek Extension & Re-evaluation: The offeror can request an extension from Bursa/SC to assess market conditions and decide on next steps, potentially with the target company's board.
‘- Voluntary Offer (VO) Approach: The offeror might withdraw the failed MGO and launch a new VO, asking the SC for permission to set different (e.g., higher) acceptance conditions or specific conditions to reach 75%.
‘- Private Placements/Direct Deals: With SC approval and specific conditions (often to address shareholding spread), an offeror might negotiate with large shareholders or place shares privately to cross thresholds, but this is complex.
‘- Seek Exemption: Apply to the Securities Commission Malaysia (SC) for an exemption from MGO rules if circumstances warrant, though this is difficult.
‘- Let it Lapse: The offeror can simply let the MGO lapse if they cannot achieve their goals, meaning they don't own over 50% and must wait for future opportunities.
‘3. Why Direct Market Buying to 75% is Tricky Post-MGO Failure:
‘- Mandatory Trigger: Once an MGO triggers, the offeror is generally bound to proceed. Failing it means a reset.
‘- Shareholding Limits: Buying significant amounts (like from 50% to 75%) in the open market without a valid offer can also trigger new mandatory offer obligations or raise regulatory red flags (e.g., market manipulation, disclosure issues).
‘- Public Spread: If the failed MGO results in a low public float (shareholding spread), the company (and offeror) must rectify it, often requiring further public offerings or buy-backs, which can be challenging.
In essence, after an MGO fails, it's a regulatory reset. The offeror must formally address the failure with Bursa and the SC, often leading to a new, carefully planned Voluntary Offer or other authorized methods, rather than just freely buying up to 75% in the market.”

title: Moody’s Downgrades Genting, Genting Singapore and Genting Overseas on Increased Debt, Slower Earnings Recovery
author: edgeinvest
body:
Moody’s Ratings on Monday lowered the ratings of Genting and Genting Overseas Holdings Ltd to Baa3 from Baa2 while Genting Singapore Ltd was downgraded to Baa1 from A3 with stable outlook on increased debt, slower earnings recovery.
KUALA Lumpur (Dec 8): Moody’s Ratings has downgraded the issuer ratings of Genting Bhd (KL:GENTING) and two of its subsidiaries — Genting Overseas Holdings Ltd (GOHL) and Genting Singapore Ltd (GENS) — following the group’s planned RM6.3 billion debt-funded acquisition of the remaining 50.6% stake it does not own in Genting Malaysia Bhd (KL:GENM).
In a statement on Monday, Moody’s lowered the ratings of Genting and GOHL to Baa3 from Baa2, while GENS was downgraded to Baa1 from A3, with all three entities carrying a stable outlook. The downgrade comes after Moody’s placed the group on review in October pending the outcome of the GENM acquisition.
Last week, Fitch Solutions’ unit CreditSights also flagged Genting and GenM as facing downgrade risk, citing Genting’s elevated debt levels and strained cash flow position.
"The ratings downgrade reflects Genting’s already weak position due to prolonged deleveraging amid slower than expected earnings recovery, further strained by increased debt to fund its takeover offer for GENM and expected spending following the potential award of a downstate New York City (NYC) commercial casino licence," said Moody’s.
“The stable outlook reflects our expectation that earnings will continue to improve at Genting’s operations in Singapore and Las Vegas, that execution risk for its downstate NYC project remains minimal such that the project will be earnings accretive by the second half of 2026, supporting a recovery in credit metrics, and that the group will not undertake any additional debt-funded expansion projects,” it added.
Moody’s also downgraded the backed senior unsecured rating of notes issued by GOHL Capital Ltd — a wholly owned unit of GOHL — to Baa3 from Baa2. The notes are guaranteed by GOHL, with both GOHL and GOHL Capital supported by a Keepwell Deed involving Genting, GOHL, GOHL Capital and the trustee of the guaranteed notes.
Earlier this month, Genting secured 73.133% stake in GENM at the close of its privatisation offer, with GENM remaining listing following the takeover bid.
GENM has also been selected for a commercial casino licence in New York, with its subsidiary Genting New York LLC being chosen by the New York Gaming Facility Location Board to advance to the final licensing review stage with the New York State Gaming Commission, which is expected to issue licences by Dec 31, 2025.
Beyond capital spending at Genting New York LLC, Moody’s expects Genting to incur annual capital expenditures of RM8 billion in 2026 and 2027, up from the expected RM6 billion in 2025, driven by expansion works at GENS and investments in a new floating liquefied natural gas project in the Kasuri block in Indonesia.
“We expect Genting’s adjusted debt/Ebitda to rise to 4.9 times in 2025 and 4.8 times in 2026 before declining to around 4.3 times in 2027. Deleveraging will be supported by earnings contribution from its downstate New York City casino, continued growth at existing gaming operations in Singapore, Malaysia, and Las Vegas, and LNG production starting in the second half of 2027,” it added.
Genting’s standalone liquidity is excellent, supported by fees and dividend income from its operating subsidiaries, said Moody’s.
“However, Genting’s debt maturity wall will build in 2027 when the US$1.5 billion [RM6.16 billion] notes under GOHL Capital Ltd are due for repayment in January 2027. This will be followed by RM1.9 billion of borrowings under Genting RMTN Bhd (RM400 million) and Genting Capital Bhd (RM1.5 billion) — both wholly owned subsidiaries of Genting — that will be due in March 2027 and June 2027 respectively,” it said.
“We expect Genting will need to refinance at least a portion of those debt maturity over the next six to 12 months,” it added.
Genting's share price slipped 15 sen or 4.62% to close at RM3.10 on Monday, giving it a market capitalisation of RM12.02 billion. GENM closed five sen or 2.27% lower at RM2.15, valuing it at RM12.77 billion.

CreditSights: High debt, weak cash flow put Genting, Genting Malaysia at downgrade risk
Source: TheEdge - 9 Dec 2025

title: One of Malaysia Top Analyst Successfully Predicted GENTING Failed to Privatize GENM — Now He Predicts 3 Stocks Could Jump Over 100%

On 1 December 2025, Genting Berhad ’s mandatory general offer (MGO) for Genting Malaysia expired, with the privatisation attempt ultimately failing. The company also did not seek an extension to the MGO deadline, confirming that Genting Malaysia will remain listed. The next day, the stock fell 4.3% to RM2.25, while Genting Berhad slipped 2.1% to RM3.29.
Interestingly, this outcome had been anticipated much earlier by CGS International analyst Chong Tjen-San . On October 13, when Genting Berhad first launched its voluntary takeover offer on Genting Malaysia at RM2.35 per share, Chong argued that Genting Berhad was likely to raise its stake beyond 49.4% of Genting Malaysia ; however, privatisation was unlikely. Many shareholders were still sitting on paper losses, and the offer price remained below the RM2.50–3.00 range seen between 2022 and 2024. He maintained an Add rating on Genting Berhad , with a target price of RM3.57 on the same day.
In his subsequent report dated November 28, Chong reiterated that privatisation remained unlikely even after Genting Berhad lifted its stake to 62.7% of Genting Malaysia . However, following a weaker-than-expected 3Q25 result, he downgraded Genting Berhad to Hold from Buy and trimmed his target price to RM3.34 from RM3.57.
Notably, Chong Tjen-San , currently ranked No.4 among 203 analysts in Malaysia on StockTipRatings.com (based on data since 2023), holds a 95% expert rating, supported by 30% average returns and a 67% success rate across stocks he covered over a 1-year period. title: New York Votes to Formally Approve Casino Licences for Genting, Two Other Winners
author: edgeinvest
body:
In the near term, Genting Malaysia’s Resort World will be the only full-service casino operational in New York City, as the other winners’ greenfield projects will only open their doors to gamblers around 2030.
KUALA LUMPUR (Dec 16): The New York State Gaming Commission has voted to award casino licences for Genting Malaysia Bhd (KL:GENM) and two other winners, ending a decade-long process to set up gambling house in the city.
The decision was unanimous, according to the commission's meeting minutes. "Each of the projects made significant commitments to their communities and to the New York state, and the gaming commission was clear that they will hold these projects accountable and make sure they keep their promises,” governor Kathy Hochul said in a statement.
The vote on Monday follows the Gaming Facility Location Board’s recommendations on Dec 1 to the commission. Apart from Genting Malaysia’s Resort World New York, Bally’s Bronx and Hard Rock Metropolitan Park also won the bids.
In addition to the US$1.5 billion (RM6.1 billion) in one-time licensing fees, the state is expected to rake in billions of dollars in tax revenue as the winners promised an economic boom for the five boroughs.
Hochul said the approved casinos will generate funding for the Metropolitan Transportation Authority and education as well as create “tens of thousands of jobs and deliver real benefits to their surrounding communities”.
In the near term, Genting Malaysia’s Resort World will be the only full-service casino operational in New York City, as the other winners’ greenfield projects will only open their doors to gamblers around 2030.
Resort World New York City is now offering mostly slot machines and electronic table games, and the licence will allow Resort World New York City to expand and deploy live table games as soon as June 2026.
Genting Malaysia submitted its proposal on June 27, outlining a US$5.5 billion (RM23.2 billion) plan to convert Resort World New York City from a racino that combines horse racing track and slot machines into an integrated resort with expanded gaming floors and extensive non-gaming facilities.
The proposal includes a 500,000 sq ft gaming floor, 6,000 slot machines, 800 table games, 2,000 hotel rooms, a 7,000-seat entertainment venue, more than 30 food and beverage outlets, large meeting spaces, and over 10 acres of greenspace.
The Malaysian casino operator has told US regulators that it can begin table-game and full-casino slot machine operations within six months of receiving the licence, and projected that the new casino could deliver tax revenue for the state as early as July 2026.
Analysts warned that Genting Malaysia and its parent Genting Bhd (KL:GENTING) may face higher debt ahead of their New York casino project. Genting Malaysia’s net debt of RM9.72 billion is set to increase as it borrows US$5.5 billion to fund the casino construction. The total New York investment is US$7.5 billion, including US$2 billion for community programmes.
Genting Malaysia’s share price was up two sen to RM2.06 a share, valuing the company at RM12.23 billion on news of the win, while Genting’s share price was up three sen to RM3.05 a share, valuing it at RM11.82 billion.
Source: TheEdge - 17 Dec 2025

title: Genting Issues RM3 Bil Notes Under New RM5 Bil Debt Programme
author: edgeinvest
body:
KUALA LUMPUR (Dec 30): Genting Bhd (KL:GENTING) has issued its maiden series of medium-term notes under its new RM5 billion unrated MTN programme, lodged with the regulator earlier this month.
The Series 1 issuance by wholly owned unit Genting Vista Bhd comprised RM3 billion in nominal value, with a one-to-five-year tenure, and carries an annual interest rate of three-month Klibor plus 1.8%, according to the group’s bourse filing on Tuesday.
Proceeds will be used to redeem the debt notes previously issued by its unit, Genting RMTN Bhd, to part-finance the takeover offer for Genting Malaysia Bhd (KL:GENM).
“... Genting RMTN has today fully redeemed the aggregate RM3 billion nominal value of MTN issued on Nov 10, 20, 27 and Dec 5, 2025 under the MTN programme,” it noted.
The now-redeemed RM3 billion notes under Genting RMTN's MTN programme of up to RM10 billion were issued at par with a one-year tenure and carry an interest rate of one-month Klibor + 1.8%.
Genting’s RM2.35 per share privatisation offer for Genting Malaysia closed on Dec 1 with the group securing 73.133% of Genting Malaysia shares, coupled with another 0.202% of acceptances pending validation at that time.
The closing figure was short of the 75% requisite threshold to withdraw the company’s listing status. Thus, Genting Malaysia remains listed on Bursa Malaysia.
Affin Hwang Investment Bank Bhd and AmInvestment Bank Bhd are the lead managers for Genting Vista’s Series 1 MTN issuance.
Shares in Genting ended two sen or 0.67% lower at RM2.98, valuing the group at RM11.55 billion.
Genting Malaysia shares closed one sen or 0.49% lower at RM2.05, valuing the company at RM12.17 billion.
Source: TheEdge - 31 Dec 2025

title: Genting Berhad - Lower Contribution From Malaysia & Singapore
author: PublicInvest
body:
Genting Bhd (GENT) posted a net loss of RM290m in 4QFY25, compared to a net loss of RM169.4m a year ago. This was mainly due to lower earnings contribution from its two key markets, namely Malaysia and Singapore . Stripping out non-operating items, cumulative FY25 results came in below expectations due to lower-than-expected profit contribution from Malaysia and Singapore . We slash our FY26-27F earnings forecasts by an average of 24% to factor in lower business volume in both Resorts World Genting and Resorts World Sentosa . While the Visit Malaysia Year 2026 should benefit the tourism industry, we expect a slowdown for the casino operations given a challenging macroeconomic environment. Following the cut in our GENM's TP and a lower consensus valuation for Genting Singapore (GENS), our TP for GENT is revised to RM2.90 . Maintain Neutral .
4QFY25 revenue was flattish, as the lower revenue contribution from Malaysia and Singapore was offset by higher revenue from the US and the UK. Malaysia posted a 3% decline in revenue due to weaker business volume while Singapore was down 7% due to lower gaming revenue.
Posted headline net loss of RM290m in 4QFY25. After adjusting for non-operating items such as impairments, gains on disposal and foreign exchange impact, GENT 's core net profit stood at RM15.1m compared to RM263.8m in 4QFY24. The weaker earnings was largely due to lower contribution from Malaysia and Singapore .
Maintain Neutral. Earnings visibility remains weak, as the slowdown in economic activities is likely to affect the hospitality and entertainment industry globally. Additionally, we expect cost to escalate towards 2H26, particularly salary and administrative cost. We do not expect the US operations to deliver stronger earnings growth this year given the challenging operating environment, in view of a weakening US job market and consumer confidence. Meanwhile, we are concerned of GENT 's gearing level considering the heavy capital commitment of its subsidiaries, Genting Malaysia and Genting Singapore , for their development projects in New York and Resorts World Sentosa .

title: Genting Malaysia Berhad - Lifted By Forex Gains
author: PublicInvest
body:
Genting Malaysia (GENM) posted a headline net profit of RM145.9m in 4QFY25, compared to a loss of RM458m a year ago. This was mainly due to higher contribution from the UK operations and the impact of a favourable foreign exchange movement on USD borrowings. Stripping out non-operating items, core net profit stood at RM39.1m in 4QFY25 versus a loss of RM91.6m in 4QFY24 due to better profit from the UK and US. The full-year results came in below our and consensus expectations, mainly due to lower-than-expected profit from Resorts World Genting. Although the Visit Malaysia Year 2026 should help to boost tourist arrivals, we do not expect this to translate to higher gaming revenue. As such, we cut of FY26-27F earnings forecasts by 7-13%. Following the unsuccessful takeover bid, we revise our TP from RM2.35 (voluntary offer price) to our SOTP-based valuation of RM2.14 . While market remains optimistic of its foray into a full-scale casino operation in New York, we are concerned of potential start-up costs of converting the existing facility into an integrated resort. Given a limited upside to our revised TP , we downgrade GENM from Trading Buy to Neutral .
4QFY25 lifted by foreign exchange translation gains. Revenue rose 10.4% YoY primarily due to stronger contribution from the UK & Egypt and the US & Bahamas. The newly acquired Stratford casino and higher business volume has helped to lift revenue in the UK by 17% YoY while the US posted a 55% jump due to consolidation of Genting Empire. However, this was partly offset by lower revenue from its Malaysian operations due to lower business volume. A headline net profit of RM145.9m was reported mainly due to the impact of a favourable foreign exchange movement on its USD borrowings. Stripping out forex gains and other non-operating items, GENM delivered a core net profit of RM39.1m (versus a loss of RM91.6m in 4QFY24) due to lower operating expenses in the UK and the US.
Outlook . Following the fallout of its parent co's privatisation bid, GENM's share price has pulled back to the levels closer to before the takeover proposal was announced. While market remains positive of GENM's expansion into a full-scale New York casino business, we believe the initial impact on group's profit may be muted, if not negative. We expect the New York casino to incur start-up costs for having to convert the existing facility into an integrated resort (total project cost at USD5.5bn). While it could open table games as early as in mid-2026 ahead of its competitors, the current state of a weakening consumer confidence in the US may limit the growth in visitorship. In addition, the strengthening of the ringgit against the USD may lead to lower translated revenue for its US operations.
Source: PublicInvest Research - 27 Feb 2026

title: Genting Malaysia (GENM MK) - Dragged by high costs, largely within expectations
author: PhillipCapital
body:
2025 core net profit of RM577m, within our expectations
GENM continued to grapple with escalating cost pressures across key geographical markets, which weighed on 4Q25 results
Maintain HOLD rating with an unchanged TP of RM2.35
Core net profit rose 16% YoY, within our expectations
GENM reported 2025 revenue of RM11.9bn (+9% YoY) and core net profit of RM577m (+16% YoY), representing 95% of our estimates and 89% of consensus forecast. The results fell short of consensus estimates, mainly due to lower-than-expected EBITDA margins amid rising cost pressure across segments. Revenue increased by 9% driven by leisure and hospitality business in Malaysia (+5%), UK (+5%), and US (+30%). EBITDA margin improved by 0.6ppts to 26.1% supported by better operating leverage. Management anticipates better 2026 performances supported by promotional campaign in conjunction with Visit Malaysia 2026.
4Q25 earnings dragged by softer gaming business
4Q25 revenue declined 10% QoQ mainly attributed to softer VIP gaming visitation and reduction in available hotel room due to refurbishment works. EBITDA margin slipped by 1ppts QoQ at 24%, as operating costs continued to rise across key geographical markets. Core net profit was lower at RM114m (-31% QoQ) weighed down by softer gaming business, margin compression, and higher finance costs, but partly mitigated by positive tax effect. GENM declared a final DPS of 7sen in 4Q25 (2025: 7sen vs 2024:10sen). Management reiterated during the analyst briefing that cash reserves will be prioritised for business expansion and working capital, with dividends payments contingent on cash availability.
Reiterate HOLD with unchanged TP of RM2.35
As results came in within expectation, we make no changes to our EPS forecast and introduce 2028E EPS forecast of 16.6sen (+21%). We maintain HOLD rating with unchanged TP of RM2.35 . We continue to see GENM as one of the main beneficiaries of Visit Malaysia 2026 and see long term potential if GENM secures the downstate NYC casino license, expected to be awarded by end25. Key risks include higher/lower-than-expected win rates, a hike/reduction in gaming taxes, lift/drag from key associates, and value-destructive related-party transactions.
Source: Phillip Capital Research - 27 Feb 2026

title: Genting Berhad (GENT MK) - Muted Genting Singapore and O&G contributions
author: PhillipCapital
body:
2025 core earnings of RM421m came in below expectations
We lower our earnings forecasts to reflect weaker Singapore gaming operations and O&G demand
Maintain BUY with a lower SOP-derived target price of RM3.95
Core net profit fell 58% YoY, below expectations
Despite stable revenue of RM27.7bn in 2025, core net profit came under pressure at RM421m (-58%). While Genting Plantation (+83%) and property delivered strong growth, this was largely offset by softer leisure & hospitality and O&G contributions. EBITDA margin narrowed by 2.9ppts to 29% amid rising operating costs. The results came in below expectations, accounting for 62% of our full-year forecasts and 61% of consensus estimates. The earnings shortfall was largely due to weaker Singapore operations, margin compression and higher effective tax rate. GENT declared a final DPS of 5sen in 4Q25, bringing full-year 2025 payout to 5sen (vs. 11sen in 2024).
4Q25 earnings dragged by softer business activity and higher expenses
GENT 's 4Q25 results were weighed down by broad-based operational weakness, with revenue declining 7.2% QoQ to RM6.9bn on softer gaming contributions from RWS and RWG, weaker O&G, and lower power-related activities. EBITDA margin contracted by 4ppts to 25% due to rising operating expenses and reduced operating leverage. As a result, GENT posted a quarterly core net loss of RM76m (from RM78m core profit in 3Q25), further exacerbated by higher interest and tax expenses.
Maintain BUY with a lower TP of RM3.95

We maintain our BUY rating with a lower SOP-derived TP of RM3.95 (from RM4.00). The key earnings growth driver remains its gaming and leisure operations, with a potential catalyst from the successful commercialization and listing of TauRx. title: Genting Falls Into the Red on Impairment Hit; GenM Swings to Profit on Forex Gains
author: edgeinvest
body:
KUALA LUMPUR (Feb 26): Genting Bhd (KL:GENTING) sank into the red in its financial year 2025 (FY2025), as a sharp rise in impairment losses in its final quarter eclipsed earlier gains. In contrast, its 73.88%-owned subsidiary Genting Malaysia Bhd (KL:GENM) swung to a net profit in the same period, bolstered by the strengthening of the ringgit and robust overseas operations.
Genting recorded an annual net loss of RM11.56 million — a sharp reversal from a net profit of RM882.95 million in FY2024 — as its fourth quarter ended Dec 31, 2025 (4QFY2025) saw net loss widen to RM289.97 million from RM169.38 million a year ago despite a slight uptick in revenue to RM6.94 billion from RM6.88 billion.
The group's bottom line was primarily weighed by a significant RM207.7 million impairment loss recognised during the quarter, compared to just RM26 million a year earlier.
Revenue for the year remained largely flat at RM27.71 billion versus RM27.72 billion in FY2024. The group noted that the strengthening of the ringgit against the US dollar, British pound and Singapore dollar also contributed to lower reported figures.
The last time the group posted an annual loss for the year was FY2022, when it incurred a net loss of RM299.91 million.
Segmentally, the group's 4QFY2025 performance was weighed down by several operational and one-off factors.
The power division saw weaker generation from its Banten Plant in Indonesia following maintenance and outages, while its leisure and hospitality arms in Malaysia and Singapore grappled with lower gaming volumes and higher costs. Meanwhile, its plantation business — Genting Plantations Bhd (KL:GENP) — saw its 4Q profit plummet by over 87%, as record revenue was offset by a RM96.6 million administrative fine imposed on its Indonesian unit.
The parent company declared a final dividend of five sen per share, to be paid on April 17. This sole payout for FY2025 halved its annual payout from 11 sen in FY2024.
GenM: A forex-led turnaround
In contrast, GenM swung to the black in the final quarter of the fiscal year, with a net profit of RM145.9 million, recovering from a net loss of RM457.9 million in 4QFY2024.
The return to profitability was largely driven by a net unrealised foreign exchange gain of RM113.8 million on its US dollar-denominated borrowings — versus a net unrealised forex loss of RM356.9 million in 4QFY2024 — as the ringgit strengthened. Its gaming business also saw stronger performance in the UK, Egypt, the US and Bahamas.
Contribution from the newly acquired Stratford casino and higher business volume helped revenue in the UK and Egypt, while the consolidation of Empire Resorts lifted revenue in the US and Bahamas.
For the full year, net profit more than tripled to RM754.92 million — its highest in six years — from RM251.28 million in the same period a year earlier, as revenue rose 8.9% to a record high of RM11.88 billion from RM10.91 billion.
GenM declared a final dividend of seven sen per share, payable on April 10.
Shares in Genting ended six sen or 2.05% lower at RM2.86, valuing the group at RM11.09 billion. The stock has dropped over 22% in the past year.
GenM shares closed unchanged at RM2.03, valuing the group at RM12.05 billion. The counter is down more than 12% from a year ago.
Source: TheEdge - 27 Feb 2026

title: Genting Malaysia Berhad - Surprisingly Low VIPs in 4Q25
author: sectoranalyst
body:
Review
Genting Malaysia’s (GENM) FY25 core profit of RM664.4mn met our expectation but beat consensus estimates. However, the adjusted PBT was lower than our estimates, but the shortfall was mitigated by RM82.2mn tax credit in 4Q25 resulted from adjustment for over provision of taxation. For this quarter, the company declared a single-tier final dividend of 7sen/share, which was 1sen lower than our projection.
GENM’s FY25 adjusted EBITDA surged 13.3% to RM3.3bn on the back of 9% growth in revenue. The decent performance can be attributed to higher contribution from Malaysia operations for first 9M25 as well as strong 4Q25 performance from UK operations.
For 4Q25, the seasonally strong quarter experienced a 17.3% QoQ drop in EBITDA, owing to declines in revenue contribution from Malaysia (- 13.1%) and US (-7.7%) operations, which partially mitigated by stronger UK performance due to higher hold percentage.
Impact
We cut our FY26-28 earnings projections by 17-23% after slashing our VIP volume assumptions by approximately 14.7%.
Conference call highlights
Resorts World Genting chalked up a 16% YoY decline in revenue from the VIP segment for 4Q25 due to lower volume and hold percentage. The impact was partially mitigated by higher revenue from the non-VIP segment, up 13% YoY. Cumulatively, FY25 VIP wins declined by 1% YoY while non-VIP wins surged 14% YoY. Looking forward, management is cautious about VIP volume recovery but optimistic on the growth in the non-VIP segment in 2026.
Foreign visitation remained strong in 4Q25, which surged 6% YoY. This was led by visitors from Singapore (+10%), China (+3%) and India (+3%). However, visitors from Indonesia declined by 6% due to weak Indonesian Rupiah against the Ringgit as well as challenging local economy.
For the new casino licences in downstate New York, the group has started converting the premise to a full-fledge casino and operations will likely start in mid-2026. The capex for phase 1 of estimated $350mn is earmarked for this year.
The license will grant GENM to operate the casino for a duration of 15 years plus 10 years and the gaming taxes for slot and table games have been fixed at 56% and 30% respectively. This is based on a project IRR of mid-teen when the group submitted its proposal.
Valuation
Given the change in earnings, we downgrade GENM’s DCF valuation to RM2.58 /share (from RM3.06 ) with a revised CAPM of 10.2%. Maintain Buy

title: Genting Berhad - Dwindling VIP Volume in Malaysia and Singapore
author: sectoranalyst
body:
Review
Genting’s FY25 core profit of RM85.1mn came in below our expectation at 39.3% of our full-year forecast and 12.7% of consensus estimates. In addition, the ramped-up costs associated with new attractions, operating costs incurred during temporary closures, and ongoing upgrades and technology system enhancements also contributed to lower profit for FY25.
GENM’s FY25 adjusted EBITDA surged 13.3% to RM3.3bn on the back of 9% growth in revenue. The decent performance can be attributed to higher contribution from Malaysia operations for first 9M25 as well as strong 4Q25 performance from UK operations (see GENM report).

Impact
We slash GENT’s FY26-27 earnings projections by 22.8-29.3% after cutting GENS’s FY26-27 earnings by 7.6% and factoring in revised GENM’s earnings projections.
Outlook
Management expects the newly completed Las Vegas Convention Center, which will host 48 conventions in 2026 to drive traffic to its casino in Las Vegas. Meanwhile, it will remain focus on enhancing property margins through operational efficiency.

title: GenM President Lee Choong Yan Now Senior Adviser, to be Redesignated as Non-executive Director in May
author: edgeinvest
body:
KUALA LUMPUR (March 2): Genting Malaysia Bhd (KL:GENM) said its long-time president Datuk Seri Lee Choong Yan has been redesignated as a senior adviser, and is slated to step down from the new role in May.
In conjunction with his slated retirement from the senior adviser role, he will also be redesignated to a non-executive director from his current executive director’s seat, according to the group’s bourse filing on Monday.
Lee, 65, is a veteran of Genting Malaysia, whose appointment as president dates back nearly two decades, when he was appointed to the role as well as chief operating officer in August 2006.
He later joined the group’s board as executive director in January 2020, while retaining the role of president.
Lee is also the CEO of Genting UK Plc, the group’s UK-based unit, which owns and operates over thirty casinos, together with the integrated resort, Resorts World Birmingham.
GenM did not disclose a succession plan in its bourse filings.
Shares in GenM ended six sen or 2.86% lower at RM2.04 on Monday, valuing the group at RM12.11 billion.
Source: TheEdge - 3 Mar 2026

title: Genting Malaysia Berhad - Higher Operating & Finance Costs
author: PublicInvest
body:
Genting Malaysia (GENM) posted a headline net loss of RM3.8m in 1QFY26 compared to a profit of RM72.7m in 1QFY25. Despite posting a revenue growth of 10.5% YoY, bottomline was dragged by higher operating and finance costs. Although 1Q26 results came in below our and consensus estimates, we make no changes to our full-year forecasts at this juncture. However, we note that earnings visibility remains weak given the potential start-up losses in New York and the impact of weakening consumer confidence due to rising inflationary pressure. We maintain our Neutral with an unchanged TP of RM2.14 .
1QFY26 revenue rose 10.5% YoY due to higher contribution from the UK & Egypt and the US & Bahamas operations. The US market posted the strongest growth of 39% due to the consolidation of Empire Resorts while the UK benefitted from the newly acquired Genting Casino Stratford in April 2025. Meanwhile, Malaysia posted a 3% growth due to higher gaming revenue.
1QFY26 net loss on higher costs . Despite recording higher revenue, bottomline was dragged by higher operating cost, particularly payroll cost. Earlier, we had highlighted the risk of rising operating cost and we expect this uptrend to continue in FY26F. Additionally, finance cost jumped from RM158m in 1QFY25 to RM233m in the current quarter as the expansion in New York has resulted in the drawdown of USD loan.
Outlook . While market remains positive on GENM 's expansion into a full-scale New York casino business, we believe the initial impact on group's profit may be muted, if not negative. We expect Resorts World New York City (RWNYC) to incur start-up costs for having to convert the existing facility into an integrated resort (total project cost at USD5.5bn). Although RWNYC has officially launched its first table games on 28 April, ahead of its competitors, we believe the current state of a weakening consumer confidence in the US may limit the growth in visitorship. In addition, the strengthening of the ringgit against the USD may lead to lower translated revenue for its US operations.
Source: PublicInvest Research - 22 May 2026

title: Genting 1Q Profit Surges Over 20-fold on JV Gains, Lower Impairments; Genting Malaysia Slips Into Loss on Casino Transition Costs
author: edgeinvest
body:
Genting Bhd posted a net profit of RM101.1 million for the first quarter ended March 31 compared with RM4.6 million a year ago on lower impairment losses and share of results from joint ventures and associates.
KUALA LUMPUR (May 21): Genting Bhd's (KL:GENTING) net profit for the first quarter jumped more than 20-fold, driven by lower impairment losses and a swing in share of results from joint ventures and associates.
In contrast, its 73.8%-owned subsidiary Genting Malaysia Bhd (KL:GENM) slipped into the red, weighed by pre-opening expenses related to Resorts World New York City’s transition into a full-scale commercial casino.
Genting recorded a net profit of RM101.1 million for the quarter ended March 31, 2026 (1QFY2026), compared with RM4.6 million in 1QFY2025, according to its bourse filing on Thursday. Revenue rose 2% to RM6.66 billion from RM6.51 billion.
Genting’s impairment losses narrowed to RM7.7 million from RM72.3 million a year earlier, while its share of results from joint ventures and associates recorded a profit of RM47.5 million, compared with a loss of RM28.4 million previously.
No dividend was declared for the quarter.
By segment, the group’s leisure and hospitality division posted a 4% year-on-year increase in revenue to RM5.54 billion, driven by stronger gaming performance in Malaysia.
The US and Bahamas operations also improved, supported by consolidation effects from Genting Empire Resorts LLC and contributions from Resorts World Las Vegas, which helped offset disruptions at Resorts World New York City during its transition to a commercial casino, the group said.
The oil palm plantation segment recorded higher revenue but lower Ebitda, mainly due to weaker palm product prices, partially offset by higher fresh fruit bunches production.
The power division recorded higher revenue and Ebitda, driven mainly by stronger generation from the Banten plant in Indonesia, following the absence of outages in 1QFY2026 compared with an unplanned outage in 1QFY2025.
The oil and gas division saw lower revenue and Ebitda, mainly due to weaker crude oil prices and lower production.
Looking ahead, Genting said its leisure and hospitality operations across Malaysia, Singapore, the UK, the US and the Bahamas will continue to be supported by asset enhancements, product refreshes and targeted marketing initiatives aimed at sustaining visitation and improving yield, despite a challenging macroeconomic environment and geopolitical tensions.
For the oil palm plantation segment, prices are expected to remain supported by elevated crude oil and stronger biodiesel demand, although gains may be capped by weaker global demand. Production is expected to improve in 2026, supported by expanded harvesting areas and more mature plantations, though risks remain from fertiliser shortages and potential El Nino conditions.
The group said the power division is expected to remain stable, underpinned by high plant availability and steady generation, particularly from the Banten plant in Indonesia, which continues to operate without disruptions and in line with grid requirements.
Meanwhile, the oil & gas division remains sensitive to crude oil price movements and production levels, with the group continuing to reshape its upstream portfolio to sustain long-term output following the expiry of certain assets, while progressing new projects to support earnings continuity.
Transition costs push Genting Malaysia into loss
Meanwhile, Genting Malaysia slipped into the red in 1QFY2026, posting a net loss of RM3.8 million compared with a net profit of RM72.7 million a year earlier.
The loss was mainly driven by higher operating and payroll-related expenses linked to the transition of Resorts World New York City into a commercial casino, which also caused profit before tax to fall 77% year-on-year to RM43.1 million from RM184 million, the group said in its exchange filing.
This came despite revenue rising 10% to RM2.87 billion from RM2.6 billion, supported by stronger performance across leisure and hospitality businesses in all geographical segments, although partially offset by a stronger ringgit.
Genting Bhd shares closed one sen or 0.4% lower at RM2.35, valuing the group at RM9.11 billion. Genting Malaysia shares fell one sen or 0.5% to RM1.98, giving a market capitalisation of RM11.8 billion.
Source: TheEdge - 22 May 2026

title: Genting Berhad (GENT MK) - Results below expectations

EBITDA margin contracted by 3ppts YoY on the back of rising operating costs across the leisure and hospitality divisions. Despite the softer margins, core net profit improved 51% YoY as associate's contribution staged a strong turnaround.
Sequential earnings swung back into the black
QoQ, GENT's 1Q26 results was impacted by lower FFB production in the plantation segment and softer property activities. EBITDA margin improved by 2ppts QoQ supported by higher hotel occupancy in the US/Bahamas, improved operating leverage in the power segment and stronger visitation at Malaysia gaming operations. Core net profit rebounded from a RM96m loss in 4Q25 to a profit of RM116m in 1Q26, attributable to better margins, lower depreciation charges, absence of other losses recognised in previous quarter, and positive tax effect. title: Genting Malaysia May Report Loss in 2Q, Analyst Warns
author: edgeinvest
body:
KUALA LUMPUR (July 30): Genting Malaysia Bhd (KL:GENM) may report a net loss in what could turn out to be an unusually weak second quarter for the casino-and-resort operator, an analyst flagged.
While April-June are seasonally weak months, the Iran war may have dented both premium and mass market gaming at its flagship resort in Genting Highlands, as well as discouraged Middle Easterners and transit gamblers from its London clubs, Maybank Investment Bank said.
The Fifa World Cup that began mid-June may also have diverted gaming spend, the research house said in a note ahead of its earnings report expected in the final days of August.
Shares of Genting Malaysia have declined close to 10% year-to-date and are approaching this year’s lows in March, as the Iran war dragged into the sixth month and widened in the Middle East. Oil prices have surged, raising the cost of transportation while dragging on travel demand.
Genting Malaysia has seven “buy” and seven “hold” calls among 14 research houses tracked by Bloomberg. The 12-month average target price stood at RM2.34 per share.
Maybank Investment cut its target price to RM2.82, after slashing its earnings forecast but kept its “buy” call on the stock. “We believe these headwinds could be temporary,” the research house said.
Further, table games at its New York City facility have performed better than expected as operations ramp up, resulting in higher gross gaming revenue for Genting Malaysia, the house noted.
By 2027, the entire US operations could account for more than one-third of Genting Malaysia’s operating earnings, an increase of 20 percentage-points from 2025, according to Maybank Investment’s estimates.
“It is this earnings growth that compels us to maintain our buy rating,” the house added.
Source: TheEdge - 31 Jul 2026

title: Genting Malaysia Berhad - Dragged By Higher Operating Cost

The 1HFY26 results came in below our and consensus estimates, mainly due to lower-than-expected profit contribution from Resorts World Genting as well as higher operating and finance cost for its US operations following the commencement of Resorts World New York City ( RWNYC ). Despite our projection of an improving earnings trajectory, visibility remains weak at this juncture given the uncertainty surrounding the health of the US economy. Maintain Neutral on GENM .
Topline lifted by contribution from RWNYC but bottomline dragged by higher costs. The group's underlying performance continued to display a challenging operating environment, affected by moderating travel demand and more careful consumer spending in the entertainment and hospitality sector. In addition, operating cost has risen, particularly wage and finance costs due to inflationary pressures. While 2QFY26 revenue surged 32% YoY, this was mainly due to the commencement of the new casino business in New York. Malaysia and the UK & Egypt operations reported a 1% decline in revenue. Meanwhile, group's adjusted EBITDA fell 18% YoY due to the recognition of forex translation loss, despite its US operations posting an 83% increase following the commencement of RWNYC . However, net profit was sharply lower at RM47.4m versus RM416.6m in 2QFY25 owing to higher operating and finance cost.
Outlook . While the full-scale New York casino expansion may be seen as a catalyst, we believe it is not likely to be earnings accretive in the next 1-2 years given its hefty project cost of USD5.5bn. RWNYC has officially launched its first table games on 28 April, ahead of its competitors. Although this should help to boost gross gaming revenue (GGR), we expect operating cost to escalate on rising inflationary pressures in the US. In addition, as we expect the process of de-dollarisation to persist, USD investments by the group could erode over time should future GGR fails to track historical growth rate. With younger consumers preferring online gaming platform to traditional physical casino games, this changing consumer behaviour could alter GENM 's long-term growth prospects.

Genting Bhd ( GENT ) posted a net loss of RM27m in 2QFY26, compared to a net profit of RM243.5m a year ago due to forex translation losses and higher finance cost. Stripping out non-operating items, 1HFY26 core net profit stood at RM275m, down 5% YoY. The 1HFY26 results came in below our and consensus estimates, mainly due to higher-than-expected finance cost and operating cost. We slash our FY26-28F earnings forecasts by an average of 18% to factor in higher total cost. Operating environment for the entertainment and hospitality industry remains challenging amid rising geopolitical tensions that restricts travel demand and increases operating cost. Following the cut in our TP for Genting Malaysia and lower earnings forecasts for GENT , our TP is revised to RM2.35 . Maintain Neutral .
2QFY26 revenue rose 14.2% YoY due to the incorporation of the financial results of Resorts World New York City ( RWNYC ) and higher plantation revenue. Revenue contribution from the US increased from RM1.35bn in 2QFY25 to RM2.26bn in the current quarter. However, revenue from Malaysia was flattish while Singapore fell 5% due to the strengthening of the ringgit against SGD. Meanwhile, plantation revenue surged 35% YoY to RM911.2m on higher FFB production.
Posted headline net loss of RM27.1m in 2QFY26 due to a 22% increase in finance cost while operating performance was dragged by higher cost, particularly wage cost. Although revenue contribution was higher due to the commencement of RWNYC , the new casino also incurred higher cost as it continues ramping up operations. The group also suffered forex translation losses on its USD denominated borrowings.
Maintain Neutral. While we are projecting a gradual recovery in earnings, visibility remains weak as the rising geopolitical tensions and the slowdown in economic activities are likely to affect the hospitality and entertainment industry globally. Additionally, we expect operating costs to escalate towards 2H26 due to higher energy cost. We do not expect the US operations to deliver higher earnings in the immediate term, in view of the weakening job market and consumer confidence. Meanwhile, we are concerned of its gearing level given the heavy capital commitment of its subsidiaries namely Genting Malaysia and Genting Singapore , for their development projects in RWNYC and Resorts World Sentosa .
Source: PublicInvest Research - 21 Aug 2026
