title: Genting Swings Into 2Q Loss as Higher Finance Costs, Absence of One-off Gain Weigh
author: edgeinvest
body:
KUALA LUMPUR (Aug 20): Genting Bhd (KL:GENTING) slipped into a loss in the second quarter despite increased revenue and operating earnings, as higher finance costs and an absence of significant disposal gains recorded a year earlier weighed on its bottom line.
The diversified gaming and leisure group posted a net loss of RM27.10 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026 (2QFY2026), compared with a net profit of RM243.50 million a year earlier. Revenue, however, rose 14% to RM7.75 billion from RM6.78 billion, thanks to the group's leisure and hospitality, and plantation business.
Genting attributed the huge decline mainly to higher finance costs and depreciation, lower interest income and smaller share of profits from its joint venture and associates. The year-ago quarter also included a RM338.3 million gain from the disposal of assets classified as held for sale.
At one of its resorts, Resorts World Genting, the group managed to report higher Ebitda despite lower revenue, helped by operating cost management. This was despite higher payroll expenses following the renewal of a union agreement that offset the improvement.
Meanwhile, in the US, the initial phase of full commercial casino operations with the introduction of live table gaming and slot machines at Resorts World New York City (RWNYC), which began on April 28, helped lift revenue. Separately, the group's Resorts World Las Vegas also benefitted from increased convention attendance and stronger high-end gaming activity.
Genting's plantation division also reported higher revenue on increased fresh fruit bunch production, while its downstream manufacturing business benefitted from stronger sales volumes and margins.
Genting Malaysia profit tumbles despite 32% revenue growth
Separately, Genting's 73.9%-owned subsidiary Genting Malaysia Bhd (KL:GENM) reported an 89% plunge in net profit to RM47.4 million for 2QFY2026 from RM416.6 million a year earlier.
Revenue nevertheless jumped 32% to RM3.85 billion from RM2.92 billion, mainly due to contributions from the commencement of commercial casino operations at RWNYC, as well as from the acquired Genting Casino Stratford and consolidated Genting Empire Resorts LLC.
The decline in net profit was partly driven by less favourable foreign-exchange comparison. Genting Malaysia recorded a RM18.1 million unrealised forex translation loss on its US dollar-denominated borrowings in 2QFY2026, compared with a RM184.6 million translation gain a year earlier.
Genting Malaysia said it remains cautious about near-term prospects in Malaysia amid higher airfares and travel-related fuel costs, which could weigh on domestic and regional tourism.
"The group is focused on operational discipline and yield management to optimise performance and manage costs, whilst continuing to enhance Resorts World Genting’s integrated resort offerings to drive visitation and customer engagement," it said.
In New York, RWNYC launched its full commercial casino operations with 242 table games and 2,500 slot machines in April, with another 1,400 slot machines subsequently added. Genting Malaysia broke ground in July on the next phase of the project, which is intended to transform RWNYC into a full-scale integrated resort encompassing gaming, entertainment and hospitality.
For the first half of FY2026, Genting's revenue rose 8% to RM14.41 billion, but net profit fell 70% to RM74 million from RM248.1 million. Genting Malaysia, meanwhile, saw first-half revenue rise 22% to RM6.72 billion, while net profit plunged 91% to RM43.6 million from RM489.3 million.
Neither Genting nor Genting Malaysia declared an interim dividend for the first half.
Shares of Genting settled four sen or 1.82% higher at RM2.24 on Thursday, valuing the group at RM8.68 billion. Meanwhile, Genting Malaysia settled one sen or 0.57% lower at RM1.73, giving it a market capitalisation of RM10.27 billion.
Source: TheEdge - 21 Aug 2026

title: Genting Falls 23% to 2007 Lows After Over RM1 Bil Cash Call
author: edgeinvest
body:
KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 12): Genting Bhd (KL:GENTING) fell to its lowest in nearly two decades after the gaming conglomerate announced a RM1.25 billion cash call to pare down borrowings.
Analysts, meanwhile, see sharp dilution to earnings and dividend on a per share basis from the company's first-ever proposed rights issue. Maybank Investment Bank downgraded Genting to the non-consensus ‘sell’ call while CIMB Securities warned of selling pressures ahead for the stock.
“Nobody likes a rights issue,” CIMB Securities said. “While a rights issue does not mathematically destroy shareholders wealth, investors usually view such exercises negatively as it replaces cheaper debt with more expensive equity.”
Shares of Genting fell 43 sen or 23% to close at RM1.45 on Monday, its lowest since April 2007, as over 90 million shares exchanged hands. The sharp fall wiped over RM2 billion from its market capitalisation to a little under RM7 billion at the end of the day.
Selling pressure also spilled over to its listed subsidiary Genting Malaysia Bhd (KL:GENM), which fell 26 sen or 17% to close at RM1.23 as more than 30 million shares traded.
The drop triggered an automatic suspension of intraday short selling in Genting and Genting Malaysia shares on Monday, which kicks in when a stock falls more than 15% or 15 sen from its reference price.
Sensible way
However, the rights issue may be a cheaper way for Genting to raise capital as well as to fund operational expenditure given its heavy capital commitment particularly for Resorts World New York in the US and Resorts World Sentosa in Singapore, said Public Investment Bank.
The house, which cut its target price by 35 sen to RM2.00, noted that credit downgrades by rating agencies had increased its funding costs, making the cash call “a more sensible way” to raise funds.
In September, Fitch Ratings downgraded Genting to BBB-, right at the bottom of investment grades, following and earlier cuts by Moody’s Ratings and S&P Global Ratings.
Genting had total borrowings of RM45.25 billion against cash and cash equivalents of RM17.64 billion. Short-term borrowings, obligations that must be repaid within 12 months, more than doubled to RM9.68 billion from the end-2025, according to its latest financial statements.
For Maybank Investment Bank, further fundraising efforts that may lead to more dilutions, including private placements, could not be ruled out even as its analysis reveals “minimal" interest savings and two percentage-points decline in net gearing for Genting.
The house also flagged potentially lower dividends ahead as Genting rebuilds its cash balance.
Genting now has four ‘buy’, seven ‘hold’, and the sole ‘sell’ ratings from Maybank Investment. The average 12-month target price is RM2.38, based on the 12 analysts tracked by Bloomberg.
Source: TheEdge - 13 Oct 2026

title: Affin Cuts GENTING & GENM to Sell as Rights Issue Offers Little Debt Relief and New York Costs Loom
author: StockTipRatings
body:
Affin Hwang Investment Bank analyst Andrew Lim downgraded Genting and Genting Malaysia to “ Sell ” from “Hold”, cutting their target prices to RM1.10 from RM2.30 and RM1.00 from RM1.80, respectively. These imply approximately 25.2% and 21.3% downside, respectively.
He believes Genting’s proposed RM1.25 billion rights issue offers limited debt relief, as the RM800 million earmarked for repayment represents less than 2% of its RM45.3 billion group borrowings. Substantial ongoing investment commitments also raise concerns over medium-term funding visibility.
Looking ahead, Andrew remains cautious on Genting Malaysia’s New York investment commitments, citing Fitch’s estimate of approximately US$3.7 billion in remaining investment over five years. Although full-scale casino operations offer longer-term growth potential, heavy upfront spending, higher operating costs and a potentially slower earnings ramp-up could delay meaningful free cash flow.
Andrew also highlighted recent credit-rating downgrades as evidence of reduced financial flexibility amid elevated leverage, substantial capital commitments and a slower-than-expected earnings recovery. Fitch lowered Genting Malaysia’s issuer rating to BBB− from BBB in September 2026, leaving it at the lowest investment-grade level.
Domestic recovery also remains subdued, with Resorts World Genting’s hilltop visitation falling 3% year-on-year in 1H26. He left underlying earnings forecasts unchanged, but adopted more conservative valuation assumptions and incorporated potential dilution from Genting’s illustrative rights issue.
He also downgraded the gaming sector to “ Underweight ”, reflecting concerns over elevated leverage, reduced financial flexibility, heavy investment commitments and subdued near-term earnings.
As of 9:25 a.m. on October 13, Genting ’s share price rose 1.4% to RM1.47, while Genting Malaysia rose 3.3% to RM1.27.

title: Genting May Need to Sell Non-core Assets to Avert a Credit-rating Downgrade — CreditSights
author: edgeinvest
body:
KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 13): Genting Bhd (KL:GENTING) may need to sell non-core assets, particularly unused land, to reduce its debt burden and avoid further credit-rating downgrades, according to CreditSights.
The credit research firm said Genting's proposed RM1.25 billion rights issue was a welcome move to reduce its reliance on borrowing, although it expects only a modest improvement in the group's financial position.
"We believe non-core asset sales will be the main tool to stave off downgrade risks," CreditSights said in a report.
The firm warned that Genting remains at risk of losing its investment-grade credit rating, given its heavy debt burden and substantial spending commitments.
It also identified possible dividend cuts, further fundraising and stronger earnings as ways for Genting to improve its finances.
CreditSights highlighted a US$618 million (about RM2.5 billion) bond maturing in January 2027, although it expects Genting to manage the repayment through existing cash and potentially fresh borrowings.
The firm also flagged Genting's heavy investment in its Resorts World New York City casino expansion as a risk, particularly if the spending fails to generate sufficient earnings.
While it noted an earnings recovery at Resorts World Las Vegas in the first half of 2026, sustaining that improvement remains important to the group's financial outlook.
CreditSights also expects Genting to avoid further debt-funded attempts to increase its stake in Genting Malaysia Bhd (KL:GENM) over the next 12 to 18 months to preserve its financial strength.
Genting currently owns about 73.8% of Genting Malaysia, which operates Resorts World Genting and gaming businesses overseas.
In October 2025, Genting launched a RM6.7 billion takeover offer at RM2.35 per share to acquire the remaining Genting Malaysia shares it did not own, with the aim of potentially taking the subsidiary private.
The offer closed in December without achieving privatisation, although Genting increased its shareholding to 73.13%.
The latest assessment follows Genting's announcement last Friday of a RM1.25 billion rights issue, mainly to repay borrowings and strengthen working capital.
CreditSights expects the exercise to secure shareholder approval, supported by the Lim family's commitment to subscribe for its full entitlement. The family collectively holds a 45.1% stake in Genting.
The announcement sent Genting shares plunging nearly 23% to RM1.45 on Monday, their lowest since April 2007.
Shares of Genting were up three sen or 2.07% at RM1.48 as at 10.32am on Tuesday, valuing the group at RM5.74 billion.
CreditSights maintained its "outperform" recommendation on Genting's US dollar perpetual securities and "market perform" recommendation on its senior debt.
Source: TheEdge - 14 Oct 2026

title: GENM Plunges 46% Below Offer Price, Vindicating This Analyst’s Exit Call Last Year—Which Stocks Is He Bearish On Now?
author: StockTipRatings
body:
​ Genting and Genting Malaysia have both suffered sharp share-price declines recently. On October 9, parent company Genting announced plans to raise approximately RM1.25 billion through a rights issue, drawing attention to the group’s debt and funding requirements. On October 12, Genting fell 23% from RM1.88 to RM1.45 in a single session, while Genting Malaysia declined 17% from RM1.49 to RM1.23. As of October 16, the two stocks closed at RM1.45 and RM1.27, respectively.
The sell-off has brought renewed attention to last year’s takeover offer for Genting Malaysia . On 13 October 2025, Genting offered RM2.35 per share, a 9.8% premium to Genting Malaysia’s last closing price of RM2.14 before the announcement. At RM1.27, Genting Malaysia now trades 46% below the offer price.
When the takeover offer was announced last October, CGS International analysts Prem Jearajasingam and Lew Cheng Wei , alongside Hong Leong Investment Bank analyst Chee Kok Siang , recommended that shareholders accept the RM2.35 offer.
​ Prem and Lew maintained a “Reduce” rating on Genting Malaysia with a target price of RM1.88, placing the offer price 25% above their valuation. Although they recognised the New York casino project’s long-term growth potential, they believed higher operating expenditure and capital requirements could constrain near-term earnings growth and dividends. They therefore viewed the offer as an exit opportunity.
​ Chee similarly recommended that existing shareholders accept, as the RM2.35 offer represented a 14% premium to his previous target price of RM2.06. He also noted that a potential New York casino licence could unlock additional value, but developing the project would require substantial capital investment.
However, not all analysts supported accepting the offer. Maybank Investment Bank analyst Yin Shao Yang advised shareholders to reject it, arguing that the price did not adequately reflect potential value from the New York casino licence and Miami land. TA Securities analyst Tan Kam Meng also considered the offer unattractive.
The offer closed on 1 December 2025, with Genting ’s stake increasing to approximately 73.13%. However, the privatisation was not completed, and Genting Malaysia remained listed. Since then, the New York business’s growth potential has not dispelled market concerns over funding requirements and earnings performance.
With Genting Malaysia falling to RM1.27, subsequent share-price performance has validated Prem , Lew and Chee ’s recommendation to accept the offer.
According to StockTipRatings data, Prem Jearajasingam has an expert rating of 50%—the highest among the three analysts who recommended accepting the offer—and a success rate of 37%. Chee Kok Siang has an expert rating of 37% and a success rate of 35%, while Lew Cheng Wei has an expert rating of 33% and a success rate of 17%.
Beyond Genting Malaysia , Prem has also downgraded other stocks ahead of subsequent declines. According to StockTipRatings records, he downgraded Kossan Rubber Industries to “Reduce” on 23 May 2024, with a target price of RM2.07. From that initial downgrade until just before he upgraded the stock to “Add” on 11 August 2026, its share price fell from approximately RM2.25 to RM1.04—a cumulative decline of 53.7%.
